        • Eilidh nic Sheumais b. 20 an t-Ògmhios 185 DE – d. 28 an Lùnastal 273 DE
          Kept the house roll at Baile Mòr dhomhain in Queen Sìleas's reign; the roll is lost and is known only from a later copy.

The custodians of Ceann àrsaidh

A custodian family of Ceann àrsaidh that gave the Council of Custodians its second high custodian under the humans (15 an Dùbhlachd 1799 DE), lost its seat on the council in the next generation, and sent the first Ròdaich child to an Tìr Thall (12 an Giblean 1830 DE).

  • Coinneach Glas = Mòrag nic Uilleim b. 17 an t-Samhain 1753 DE – d. 12 am Faoilleach 1804 DE
    High custodian after Tormod mac Ailein; had never met a human before the Crossing and dealt with little else after it.
    • Eachann Mòr = Seonag nic Dhòmhnaill b. 16 an Dàmhair 1788 DE – d. 18 an t-Iuchar 1843 DE
      A custodian of Ceann àrsaidh who lost his place on the council; sent his son west with the Mission's letter.
      • Calum mac Eachainn b. 14 am Faoilleach 1816 DE – d. 15 an t-Samhain 1853 DE
        Sailed west on a Company ship, 12 an Giblean 1830 DE, and is never recorded returning. No roll records his death, and the dates given for it are uncertain.
      • Ruairidh mac Eachainn b. 14 an Dàmhair 1819 DE – d. 12 an t-Sultain 1877 DE
        Held no seat on the council; the family's place there was not restored in the age.
        • Coinneach mac Ruairidh b. 29 an t-Samhain 1849 DE – d. 5 an Cèitean 1927 DE
          A custodian of the town's shrine; his name is on the petitions of the Levy years.
          • Tormod mac Choinnich b. 27 an t-Iuchar 1886 DE – d. 15 an t-Iuchar 1935 DE
            The last of the line the family roll records.
        • Anna nic Ruairidh b. 1 an t-Sultain 1859 DE – d. 28 an Gearran 1911 DE
          Married inland; the family roll records her going and not where.
      • Seònaid nic Eachainn b. 19 an Cèitean 1813 DE – d. 5 an Dùbhlachd 1894 DE
        Kept the family's house at Ceann àrsaidh after her brother sailed.
    • Iseabail nic Choinnich b. 9 an t-Sultain 1787 DE – d. 24 an Lùnastal 1843 DE
      Kept her father's copies of the council roll after his death.

Na Maoir of Muileann chrom

The line of the Company's overseers at Muileann chrom. The Ròdaich gave the first of them the byname Maor, steward (17 an t-Ògmhios 1815 DE), and the staff and the byname went from father to son until Mòrag nic Iain Maor broke the staff at the Company's door (24 an Cèitean 1927 DE).

  • Dòmhnall b. 5 an t-Sultain 1743 DE – d. 15 an t-Ògmhios 1801 DE
    A hewer of Muileann chrom; known only from his son's name.
    • Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, Raghnall Maor = Catrìona nic Ailein b. 17 an t-Ògmhios 1765 DE – d. 3 an Giblean 1841 DE
      A crew-leader since the first contract; the first overseer, given the Company's staff and a slate-roofed house, 17 an t-Ògmhios 1815 DE.
      • Seonag nic Raghnaill b. 26 an Lùnastal 1804 DE – d. 23 an Cèitean 1875 DE
        Kept her father's house after his death; not named in the Company's letters.
      • Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor = Peigi nic Mhurchaidh b. 21 an Dùbhlachd 1807 DE – d. 8 an Cèitean 1866 DE
        Given his father's staff, 12 am Màrt 1841 DE; signed the order that the camps keep no grain beyond a week's ration.
        • Iain Maor = Oighrig nic Thormoid b. 9 an Giblean 1828 DE – d. 1 an t-Ògmhios 1910 DE
          Schooled at the Mission; kept his reports in the humans' tongue and his household in Ròdais; wrote against the night shift, 22 am Màrt 1899 DE.
          • Ruairidh mac Iain b. 18 an Lùnastal 1864 DE – d. 5 an t-Samhain 1922 DE
            A hewer; the staff passed over him to his sister.
          • Mòrag nic Iain Maor b. 24 an Dùbhlachd 1871 DE – d. 19 am Faoilleach 1942 DE
            The first woman to hold the staff, 12 an t-Sultain 1910 DE; fourth and last of her line to hold it.
          • Catrìona nic Iain b. 9 an Giblean 1878 DE – d. 17 an Giblean 1956 DE
            Sister of Mòrag Maor; kept the slate-roofed house after the staff was broken.
        • Ailean mac Dhòmhnaill b. 6 am Màrt 1838 DE – d. 28 an t-Ògmhios 1891 DE
          Worked the galleries under his brother's staff.

The keepers of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

The family that has kept the carters' house at the halfway stage of the ore road (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr) since Seònaid Bhàn reopened it (1 an Lùnastal 1813 DE). Her great-grandson Aonghas kept it through the years of the fortified houses (26 an Gearran 1922 DE).

  • Seònaid Bhàn = Pàdraig mac Artair b. 29 an Dùbhlachd 1784 DE – d. 28 an Dùbhlachd 1847 DE
    Reopened the house; the only keeper on the road who took both marks and barter.
    • Murchadh mac Phàdraig b. 21 an Gearran 1816 DE – d. 12 an Giblean 1872 DE
      Kept the house after his mother.
      • Seònaid nic Mhurchaidh = Dùghall mac Iain b. 22 an t-Iuchar 1846 DE – d. 16 am Màrt 1914 DE
        Kept the house after her father, through the Levy and the Long Drought.
        • Aonghas mac Dhùghaill b. 30 an Giblean 1873 DE – d. 17 an Giblean 1965 DE
          Great-grandson of Seònaid Bhàn; kept the house in the years the constables searched it most and found least.
          • Seumas mac Aonghais b. 22 am Faoilleach 1910 DE – d. 23 am Màrt 1960 DE
            Kept the house after his father under the restored kingdom.
        • Eilidh nic Dhùghaill b. 3 an t-Ògmhios 1889 DE – d. 18 an Gearran 1956 DE
          Served in the house under her brother.
      • Ruairidh mac Mhurchaidh b. 30 an t-Sultain 1842 DE – d. 13 an t-Iuchar 1901 DE
        A carter on the ore road.
    • Peigi nic Phàdraig b. 16 an t-Samhain 1822 DE – d. 23 an t-Ògmhios 1875 DE
      Kept the byres and the carters' book.

Clann Choinnich of the silver guild

The family at the head of the refiners' guild that held the silver seam of Muileann chiar against the Company (31 am Màrt 1822 DE) and kept it under the Silver Compact until the rising. Its name is the name of the house of custody that brought the silver petitions of the Sundering age; the record does not trace the descent.

  • Coinneach mac Dhonnchaidh b. 16 an Giblean 1735 DE – d. 22 am Faoilleach 1810 DE
    A refiner of the seam; the guild ledger names him among its members at the Crossing.
    • Ùna nic Choinnich = Alasdair mac Ruairidh b. 22 an t-Sultain 1766 DE – d. 7 an Dùbhlachd 1855 DE
      Led the guild; met the Company's surveyors at the adit with the whole guild and its ledgers; refused Martha Gale's partnership when very old, 1 am Faoilleach 1846 DE.
      • Coinneach mac Alasdair b. 22 am Faoilleach 1795 DE – d. 6 an Lùnastal 1856 DE
        A refiner; carried the guild's bars to Seann Bhral.
        • Ùna nic Choinnich Òg b. 21 an Giblean 1828 DE – d. 29 an Dàmhair 1901 DE
          Named for her grandmother; sat on the guild's council in the years it sold bar silver for marks.
          • Ruairidh Ciar b. 30 an t-Sultain 1859 DE – d. 13 an t-Iuchar 1933 DE
            Among the guild members who opened the armoury in 1928 DE.
      • Beathag nic Alasdair b. 4 am Faoilleach 1795 DE – d. 27 an Giblean 1862 DE
        Sat on the guild's council after her mother.
    • Donnchadh mac Choinnich b. 5 an t-Samhain 1767 DE – d. 8 an Cèitean 1835 DE
      Kept the guild's weights and ledgers under his sister.
      • Iain mac Dhonnchaidh b. 3 an t-Ògmhios 1798 DE – d. 20 an Gearran 1864 DE
        Worked the new faces of the seam.
        • Dòmhnall mac Iain b. 22 an t-Iuchar 1831 DE – d. 16 am Màrt 1917 DE
          A refiner of the new town.

The Pikes

A human family descended, by its own account, from Thomas Pike, who kept the first tally-book of the trading post at Ros dhomhain (21 an t-Iuchar 1782 DE) and held the Company alone after Harrow was lost. Its later members stayed on Rodos after the Severance and are counted among the Tuathaich of the north.

  • Thomas Pike = Anne b. 30 an Dàmhair 1754 DE – d. 11 am Màrt 1820 DE
    Trader at Ros dhomhain; partner of Harrow in the Company, and its sole holder from 1800 DE.
    • John Pike b. 22 an t-Samhain 1791 DE – d. 15 an Dàmhair 1843 DE
      Clerk of the Company's post at Ros dhomhain.
      • Daniel Pike b. 30 an t-Iuchar 1821 DE – d. 10 an Lùnastal 1887 DE
        A storekeeper on the northern concession.
        • Matthew Pike b. 14 an t-Samhain 1853 DE – d. 22 an t-Sultain 1906 DE
          A miller of the northern concession.
          • William Pike b. 26 an Dàmhair 1878 DE – d. 19 an t-Ògmhios 1947 DE
            Stayed in the north at the Severance.
            • Agnes Pike b. 22 an Gearran 1905 DE – d. 6 an Dùbhlachd 1988 DE
              A Tuathaich teacher; opened the school at Doire ghlas with Moot money and without the council's leave, 14 am Faoilleach 1944 DE.
            • Joseph Pike b. 8 an t-Iuchar 1920 DE – d. 25 an t-Ògmhios 1982 DE
              A fisherman of Caol mhòr.
      • Ann Pike b. 10 an Dùbhlachd 1818 DE – d. 18 an t-Samhain 1897 DE
        Married a farmer of the concession.
    • Sarah Pike b. 15 an t-Iuchar 1791 DE – d. 3 an Dàmhair 1856 DE
      Went home to an Tìr Thall and is not recorded returning.

The Hales

The family of the first marriage in two tongues on the record, made at Baile dhìreach (26 an Cèitean 1786 DE). The Moot's own genealogy traces its first speaker, Walter Hale, to that marriage. His great-grandson Peter Hale holds the Moot's chair in the present year (19 am Faoilleach 2026 DE).

  • Samuel Hale = Eilidh nic Ruairidh, net-maker of Baile dhìreach b. 27 an Giblean 1765 DE – d. 14 am Faoilleach 1816 DE
    A human cooper; his marriage was entered in both the council's books.
    • John Hale b. 21 an Cèitean 1799 DE – d. 2 an t-Ògmhios 1853 DE
      A cooper of Baile dhìreach, like his father.
      • Thomas Hale b. 13 an Giblean 1824 DE – d. 25 am Faoilleach 1892 DE
        Claimed a customary cutting through his Ròdaich grandmother and lost it by Dunstan's rule, 4 am Màrt 1890 DE.
        • Richard Hale b. 8 an Lùnastal 1853 DE – d. 2 an Giblean 1907 DE
          A harbour hand in the north-west.
          • Walter Hale b. 31 am Faoilleach 1884 DE – d. 23 an Cèitean 1962 DE
            A former harbour clerk; first speaker of the Moot at Caol mhòr, 25 an Lùnastal 1931 DE.
            • David Hale b. 23 an t-Sultain 1914 DE – d. 1 an t-Sultain 1970 DE
              Kept the Moot's minute-books in his father's time.
              • Frank Hale b. 20 an Dùbhlachd 1943 DE – d. 25 an Giblean 2012 DE
                A fisherman of Caol mhòr; father of Peter Hale.
            • Alice Hale b. 21 am Faoilleach 1918 DE – d. 21 an Cèitean 2003 DE
              Taught in one of the Moot's schools.
    • Mary Hale b. 12 an Lùnastal 1794 DE – d. 5 an t-Iuchar 1850 DE
      A net-maker, like her mother.

The house of Mac Ùisdein of Cathair mhòr

A Ròdaich house of Cathair mhòr that held an overseer's post under the humans and the Sloc Mòr concession under the Crown (23 an Cèitean 1940 DE). It sold the concession back piece by piece, and it was the only house of the vein to move its money out before the vein failed it (4 an t-Sultain 2012 DE).

  • Ùisdean mac Ruairidh b. 20 an Giblean 1859 DE – d. 2 am Faoilleach 1932 DE
    Held the house's overseer's post under the Company; the post is the house's first entry in any roll.
    • Uisdean mac Ùisdein = Beathag nic Iain b. 18 an Dàmhair 1895 DE – d. 9 an Cèitean 1971 DE
      Given the Sloc Mòr on the humans' terms with the names changed; raised the market cross and the stone house at Cathair mhòr.
      • Ruairidh mac Uisdein b. 13 an t-Iuchar 1914 DE – d. 21 an Dàmhair 1995 DE
        Held the house's share in his father's last years.
        • Alasdair mac Ùisdein b. 3 an t-Sultain 1948 DE – d. 11 am Faoilleach 1998 DE
          Grandson of the first holder; borrowed against the house's share for the search for a second vein, 20 an Cèitean 1979 DE, and sold half the share to meet the debt.
        • Mòrag nic Ruairidh b. 6 an Dùbhlachd 1942 DE – d. 20 am Màrt 2015 DE
          Sister of Alasdair; kept the house's papers after the stone house was let to the Mine Board.
      • Dòmhnall mac Uisdein b. 28 an t-Samhain 1923 DE – d. 23 an t-Iuchar 1991 DE
        Kept the quarry at Achadh dhomhain under the house's mark.
      • Catrìona nic Uisdein b. 24 an t-Sultain 1922 DE – d. 8 an Dàmhair 2012 DE
        Married at Cathair mhòr; took no part in the concession.
    • Seonag nic Ùisdein b. 28 an t-Samhain 1895 DE – d. 5 an Giblean 1978 DE
      Kept the house's quarry accounts at Achadh dhomhain.

A Gazetteer of Rodos

Every town of the island, by shire: when and by whom it was founded, its history, and what the annals record there.

Siorrachd Achadh chaol

Achadh chaol

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 14,431

Founded 17 an Lùnastal 2776 BDE by Ròdaich barley farmers. Known for narrow barley fields.

Achadh chaol is a large village of narrow barley fields and the seat of its province. Its grain goes to the mills of Muileann dhìreach, and the two places have kept the same bargain since the Holy Age. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

  • 27 an Gearran 5126 BDE — Achadh chaol cleared
  • 5 an t-Sultain 2504 BDE — The shepherds of Achadh chaol
  • 16 am Màrt 1889 DE — Achadh chaol goes to the pits

Baile dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,551

Founded 10 an t-Iuchar 1037 DE by farmers of Achadh chaol. Known for red town on the harbour road.

A red town in the east on the road to the harbour at Seann Toll. It keeps the old spirits.

Baile mhin

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,647

Founded 23 an Dàmhair 1136 DE by carters of the Achadh chaol road. Known for wheelwrights on the Achadh chaol road.

Baile mhin grew where the road from Achadh chaol to the coast levels out, a stopping place for carts. It is a small town of wheelwrights and stables. Its people send their grain to the mills at Muileann dhìreach.

Cnoc ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 9,725

Founded 14 am Màrt 2962 BDE by shepherds of the eastern uplands. Known for red-hill sheepwalks and Cuan ruadh wool.

Cnoc ruadh of Achadh chaol is a hill town of the eastern uplands, a sheep town since the Holy Age. Its wool goes down to Cuan ruadh for shipping. It keeps the ancestor rite.

Muileann dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 10,994

Founded 17 an Lùnastal 1567 BDE by the custodian house of Achadh chaol. Known for grain mills on the straight race.

Muileann dhìreach was raised to grind the barley of Achadh chaol, and its mill-race still runs straight as a ruled line from the stream above the town. In the Age of Strangers it ground for the camps as well as for its own people, and the tithe clerks kept a counting-room beside the wheel. A reading-house of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh stands on the square, and the miller's guild and the school have shared its bell since before anyone wrote the arrangement down.

Àth dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,775

Founded 8 am Màrt 1869 DE by Ròdaich carters of the mining road. Known for the second regiment's garrison.

A straight ford with a citadel in the north-east, built as a waystation on the ore road in the Age of Strangers and fortified in the war before the Severance. Since the Long War it has been the station of An dàrna rèisimeid, the second regiment. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

  • 25 an Dàmhair 2020 DE — An dàrna rèisimeid raised

Siorrachd Achadh mhòr

Achadh mhòr

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 42,136

Founded 13 am Màrt 1897 BDE by Ròdaich farming households of the eastern plain. Known for the great granary fields.

Achadh mhòr is still called a field village, though it is one of the largest settlements on the island and the seat of its province. It is the granary of the east, and the shared-meal custom of the Holy Age is said to have been kept here most faithfully. Travellers on the road stop at An Sligeanach Fad' às nearby.

  • 2 an t-Samhain 3611 BDE — Fields at Achadh mhòr
  • 28 am Faoilleach 1922 DE — Achadh mhòr keeps the ledgers
  • 22 am Màrt 2008 DE — Achadh mhòr's drovers

Ceann bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,325

Founded 29 an t-Samhain 1024 DE by the tavern-keepers of the white headland. Known for An Sligeanach Fad' às and dried venison.

A walled port on a pale headland with the famous tavern An Sligeanach Fad' às at its gate, where travellers eat dried venison. It grew around the tavern road, and its walls went up in the troubles, when the roadside houses became militia posts. It keeps the old spirits and trades with the great village of Achadh mhòr inland.

Siorrachd Achadh naomh

Achadh naomh

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 26,585

Founded 5 am Faoilleach 721 BDE by keepers of the holy field. Known for holy field by Colbh Cnoc chiar.

Achadh naomh is a large village and the seat of its province in the north-central country, founded in the Holy Age on a field held sacred. Colbh Cnoc chiar stands to its east, carved 'remember the fire'. It keeps the ancestor rite.

  • 5 an t-Ògmhios 3516 BDE — Achadh naomh's spring-fields
  • 16 am Màrt 1802 DE — The spirits' priests of Achadh naomh

Achadh naomh

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 24,923

Founded 28 an t-Sultain 675 BDE by Ròdaich households of the ancestor feasts. Known for the ancestor feasts on the unploughed field.

The holy field was a meeting ground for the ancestor feasts of the old folk tradition before any house stood on it, and the houses were built around its edge rather than upon it. It is now a village of twenty-five thousand and the seat of its province, yet the field at its heart is still left unploughed. The feasts are kept there as they were in the Holy Age.

Cnoc bheag

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,478

Founded 9 an t-Ògmhios 1061 DE by the herders of Achadh naomh. Known for hilltop refuge for eastern herds.

A small walled hill in the east, raised as a refuge for the herds of Achadh naomh in the troubled years. Its pastures are thin, and the town has always kept fewer herds than its walls could shelter. It keeps the old spirits.

Cnoc chiar

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 3,269

Founded 24 an Lùnastal 2989 BDE by keepers of the Colbh. Known for the stone of 'remember the fire'.

A dusky hill near the standing stone Colbh Cnoc chiar, which carries only the words Cuimhnich an teine, 'remember the fire'. The stone was old when the Ròdaich came, and the town grew around the families who tended it. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, whose philosophers still come to argue over the imperative that no one has explained.

Cuan àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 11,749

Founded 28 an Dùbhlachd 516 BDE by the harbour-lords of the inner coast. Known for the island's oldest working breakwater.

An ancient harbour facing Cuan bheag across the water, trading grain from the fields around Baile fhiadhaich since the Holy Age. The Green Death, A' Phlàigh Uaine, struck the harbour in the Age of Strangers. It follows the capital's faith of the Dark Unicorn. Its breakwater is held to be the oldest on the island still in use, and it is patched each generation rather than rebuilt.

Inis mhin

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,620

Founded 18 an t-Samhain 1702 BDE by seal-hunters of the eastern coast. Known for causeway harbour and seal-oil.

A smooth low island joined to the shore by a causeway, walled, with a small harbour. The seal-hunters who settled it in the Holy Age became traders and then wall-builders, since the eastern waters were a haunt of pirates in the Age of Strangers. It keeps the old spirits and is the harbour for Àth chaol and Achadh naomh.

  • 20 an Cèitean 4415 BDE — Inis mhin settled

Muileann dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,306

Founded 27 an Dùbhlachd 980 DE by millers of Achadh naomh. Known for black mill of the northern road.

The black mill stands on the northern road near Tobar ghorm, grinding for the villages of Achadh naomh province. Its wheel was darkened, the old telling says, by ore dust carried downstream from the mining roads. It is a small town and has always been one.

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,559

Founded 20 an t-Sultain 620 BDE by the ford-keepers of Achadh naomh. Known for narrow ford on the Inis mhin road.

A narrow ford in the east where the road to the harbour at Inis mhin crosses a stream. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich, and its ford runs low in the dry months. It is a small market town for the holy field of Achadh naomh.

Siorrachd Achadh shean

Achadh shean

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 24,587

Founded 3 am Màrt 2591 BDE by Ròdaich farming households. Known for the old fields and the Long Drought.

Achadh shean, the old field, is a village of twenty-five thousand and the seat of its province. It gave its name to Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, which settled over the island's dry season for three years running in the Age of Strangers. Its granaries were emptied in those years and rebuilt larger afterward, and they are the largest on the eastern coast.

  • 21 an Giblean 4454 BDE — Achadh shean resettled
  • 15 an t-Iuchar 99 BDE — Drought at Achadh shean
  • 2 an t-Samhain 1450 DE — The water-rights of Achadh shean
  • 28 an t-Ògmhios 1886 DE — The wells of Achadh shean
  • 29 an Dàmhair 1888 DE — The Mission's wells
  • 9 am Faoilleach 1973 DE — Grain by the ore line

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,080

Founded 10 an Gearran 2901 BDE by keepers of the sacred forest. Known for keepers of the sacred forest's edge.

Muileann chiar of Achadh shean stands at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, the forest marked sacred before any faith claimed it. Its people were party to the holy-wood dispute of the Holy Age and have kept the forest's edge since. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It is not the silver town of the same name.

  • 7 an Dùbhlachd 2881 BDE — The stag in the grove
  • 15 am Màrt 2085 BDE — The stag-letters
  • 3 an Lùnastal 1713 BDE — Tormod Scrìobhaiche learns the letters

Àth chrom

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,795

Founded 9 an Giblean 225 DE by carters of Achadh shean. Known for bent ford on the Achadh shean road.

A small town at a bent ford on the road from Achadh shean to the coast. It lives on the road and has never been more than a crossing.

Siorrachd Achadh àrsaidh

Achadh àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 32,516

Founded 17 an t-Iuchar 791 BDE by the fishers of the capital's coast. Known for the harbour that feeds the capital.

An ancient field village on the coast west of the capital, grown into one of the largest settlements on the island while keeping its village name. It is the seat of Siorrachd Achadh àrsaidh, and its harbour lands the fish and grain that feed Cathair dhearg. It follows the Dark Unicorn.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 11,443

Founded 20 an Giblean 736 BDE by custodians of the capital's south. Known for black-hill citadel south of the capital.

Cnoc dhubh of Achadh àrsaidh is a black hill with a citadel, south-east of the capital, founded in the Holy Age. Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag lies to its west and the field of Muileann ghlas to its east. It keeps the capital's faith.

Dùn chiar

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,550

Founded 2 an Cèitean 2137 BDE by a custodian house guarding the capital's east. Known for dusky hill fort east of the capital.

Dùn chiar is a hill fort of dusky stone east of Cathair dhearg, called a city for its rank rather than its people, who are few. Its citadel and walls were rebuilt in every age, and it has served as the eastern guard of the capital since the kings of the Holy Age. It follows the capital's faith, and its garrison takes part in the rites of Cathair dhearg.

  • 30 am Faoilleach 1847 DE — Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar

Siorrachd Baile chaol

Baile chaol

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 17,907

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 1660 BDE by the valley-folk of the eastern narrows. Known for terraced houses and the valley toll.

A town squeezed into a narrow valley in the east and the seat of Siorrachd Baile chaol. Its houses climb the valley sides in rows, and the one road through it has been tolled since the Holy Age. It keeps the old spirits and trades with the city of Baile Mòr dhìreach and the market at Cnoc uaine; the sacred forest of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar lies on its western edge.

  • 10 an Dàmhair 96 BDE — Baile chaol's repayment
  • 6 an t-Sultain 1886 DE — The cattle of Baile chaol

Baile Mòr dhìreach

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 11,777

Founded 7 an Gearran 948 BDE by custodians of the eastern road. Known for citadel city of the eastern road.

Baile Mòr dhìreach of Baile chaol is a citadel city on the eastern straight road, founded in the Holy Age to hold the road between the vein country and the coast. It was a tithe station in the Age of Strangers, and the ledgers kept there were among those burned in the raids before the Severance. It keeps the ancestor rite.

  • 25 an Lùnastal 1889 DE — The quota not lowered

Cnoc uaine

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 16,670

Founded 21 an Cèitean 147 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of the holy wood. Known for green hill on the holy wood's edge.

Cnoc uaine is a green hill at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar. It is a large town of nearly seventeen thousand, and its people share the keeping of the wood with Àth dhearg. It keeps the folk tradition of the ancestors, though the wood itself is sacred to the Fèidh.

Seann Dunn

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 8,890

Founded 22 an Dùbhlachd 12,545 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for Seann-Dhaoine harbour stones and citadel.

The harbour stones of Seann Dunn are older than any Ròdaich work, and the name the Ròdaich gave the place keeps a root that is not their own. It became a Ròdaich port in the Holy Age, and its citadel was raised above the harbour to guard the eastern approaches. It is now a city of shipping and salt-fish, and its oldest families still claim that the harbour wall was only repaired, never built, by their ancestors.

  • 28 an Lùnastal 12,187 BDE — The middens of Seann Dunn
  • 7 an t-Samhain 1877 DE — Customs at Seann Dunn

Àth dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 4,282

Founded 25 am Faoilleach 1535 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of the holy wood. Known for ford at the edge of the holy wood.

Àth dhearg stands at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, and its people have acted as keepers of the wood's western paths since the Holy Age. Walls were raised in the Age of Strangers to keep timber-cutters out of the forest as much as to keep raiders out of the town. It is not the Àth dhearg of the lighthouse in the north.

Àth mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 13,331

Founded 12 an t-Samhain 581 BDE by Ròdaich road-keepers of Baile chaol. Known for the great ford and the temple-ruin path.

The great ford carries the road from Seann Dunn inland, and for most of its history it has been the busiest crossing in the province. A path leaves the town southward to Làrach an Teampaill, and the folk of Àth mhòr have kept that path cleared for as long as there are accounts of it, though they will not say why. It is a large, plain town of carters, smiths and innkeepers.

Siorrachd Baile chiar

Achadh fhada

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 1,735

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 877 DE by barley-farmers of the south-west. Known for long field of barley.

Achadh fhada, the long field, is a village of barley farms in the capital's southern country. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and has changed little since. It keeps the Direwolf's faith, unlike most of its neighbours.

Baile chiar

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 23,760

Founded 1 an Gearran 2130 BDE by farmers of the capital's southern country. Known for market of the capital's southern country.

Baile chiar, the dusky town, is the market and provincial seat of the capital's southern country. It has been a farm market since the Holy Age and has never been walled; the citadel at Baile àrsaidh stands close by. Grain from Achadh fhada and the southern farms comes to its market.

  • 18 an Dùbhlachd 1996 BDE — Baile chiar holds
  • 9 an t-Samhain 1819 DE — The pox in the south
  • 6 am Faoilleach 1944 DE — The weavers of Baile chiar
  • 12 am Faoilleach 1985 DE — The Tuathaich marks at the fair

Baile àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 12,323

Founded 1 an Gearran 2523 BDE by custodians of the capital's south. Known for old citadel of the southern country.

Baile àrsaidh, the ancient town, is a citadel town of the capital's southern country, founded in the Holy Age. Its citadel guards the market at Baile chiar. It keeps the capital's faith.

Cill chiar

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,848

Founded 16 an Dùbhlachd 1244 DE by priests of the Dark Unicorn. Known for the chapel watching the unclaimed forest.

A small church-site village at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, the forest no one has settled or fully mapped. Its chapel was built to watch the forest rather than enter it. It follows the Dark Unicorn.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,835

Founded 4 an Dàmhair 831 DE by the garrison of the capital's south road. Known for walled hill on the capital's south road.

Cnoc ìseal of Baile chiar is a walled hill on the capital's south road, founded in the long quiet centuries as a watch-post over the southern farms. Its walls were strengthened in the war of the Severance. It is a small town now, keeping the capital's faith and a toll it no longer collects.

  • 6 am Màrt 1680 DE — Tormod's bridges

Siorrachd Baile chrom

Baile chrom

town · Tuathaich · Rùn-dìomhair na h-Oidhche Glaise · pop. 27,319

Founded 3 an t-Ògmhios 150 BDE by Ròdaich fishers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Grey Night cult and the lighthouse.

A bent town on the far north-west coast, the seat of Siorrachd Baile chrom, beside Taigh-solais Baile chrom, the first of the five lighthouses in the ring. Since the Severance it has been Tuathaich, and it is the one town where Rùn-dìomhair na h-Oidhche Glaise, the cult of Sìne the Peaceful Goose, holds the majority. Gorta Baile chrom, the Great Hunger, takes its name from this town, which it struck in the Age of Strangers.

  • 26 an Dùbhlachd 750 DE — Baile chrom half empty

Siorrachd Baile fhiadhaich

Baile fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 25,789

Founded 29 an Dùbhlachd 2897 BDE by Ròdaich traders of the west. Known for west-coast market harbour.

Baile fhiadhaich of the west is a large harbour town and the seat of its province, founded in the Holy Age. It lies near the field of Àth leathan, and its people remember the first battle of An Cogadh Fada. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith.

  • 17 an t-Iuchar 4888 BDE — Baile fhiadhaich on the west coast
  • 31 am Màrt 2398 BDE — Baile fhiadhaich on the western heath
  • 10 an t-Iuchar 1780 DE — The custodian of Baile fhiadhaich rides south

Muileann mhin

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 4,367

Founded 18 an Gearran 1560 DE by millers of the west. Known for smooth-stone mill of the west.

Muileann mhin of Baile fhiadhaich is a mill town of the west, founded in the long quiet centuries on a stream that turns smooth stones. It grinds for the harbour at Baile fhiadhaich. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith, and its millers are known for honest measures.

  • 29 an Dàmhair 2021 DE — The column goes south

Àth bheag

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,680

Founded 14 an t-Samhain 185 DE by the ford-keepers of Baile fhiadhaich. Known for a small western crossing.

A small ford in the west on the road between Baile fhiadhaich and Cnoc ìseal. It follows the Yellow Scorpion and has never been much more than a crossing, though crown regiments marched through it to Àth leathan in the Long War.

  • 24 an t-Samhain 2021 DE — The column's road

Siorrachd Baile gharbh

Achadh mhin

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,865

Founded 19 an Lùnastal 1762 DE by Ròdaich farmers of Baile gharbh. Known for smooth fields of Baile gharbh.

A village of smooth, well-drained fields that feeds the harbour at Ceann dhubh. It is not the Achadh mhin of the southern coast that the Great Wave struck. It has had few recorded troubles and is mentioned in the older rolls chiefly for its tithe.

Baile gharbh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 35,209

Founded 21 am Màrt 2138 BDE by wool merchants of the north. Known for rough-town wool market.

Baile gharbh is a large market town of the north-east and the seat of its province. It has been a wool market since the Holy Age, and the hill towns of Cnoc chaol and Àth fhada bring their flocks and cheese to it. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and has no walls, trusting to Baile Mòr dhìreach close by.

  • 15 an Lùnastal 4935 BDE — Baile gharbh in the north-east
  • 18 an t-Sultain 322 DE — The wool of Baile gharbh
  • 24 an Cèitean 1928 DE — The northern pits rise
  • 9 an t-Ògmhios 1976 DE — The Fèidh in Siorrachd Baile gharbh

Ceann dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 4,416

Founded 26 an Cèitean 1320 DE by Ròdaich fishers of the black headland. Known for harbour under the black headland.

Ceann dhubh is a harbour under a dark headland, the port of Baile gharbh province, whose boats work the cold waters of the northern coast. Travellers on the coast road break their journey at An Leòmhann Buidhe a short way west, and the inn buys most of the harbour's catch. The harbour was deepened in the Age of Strangers to take the humans' ore ships, and has been too large for its trade ever since.

Cnoc chaol

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,754

Founded 16 an t-Ògmhios 768 DE by goatherds of the northern hills. Known for goat cheese for Baile gharbh.

Cnoc chaol, the narrow hill, is a small herding town of the north. It is not the southern Cnoc chaol that gave Tonn Mhòr its name. Its people keep Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and send their cheese and kids to the market at Baile gharbh.

Àth fhada

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 11,371

Founded 12 an t-Sultain 490 BDE by ford-keepers of the north-east road. Known for long ford of the north-east road.

Àth fhada, the long ford, is a town on the north-east road, founded in the Holy Age. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Its ford is long and shallow, and carts cross it only at low water.

Siorrachd Baile gheal

Baile gheal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 19,129

Founded 3 an t-Ògmhios 1937 BDE by the white-cloth weavers of the west. Known for white cloth of the western plain.

A large white town of the western plain and the seat of Siorrachd Baile gheal. It is a city of the Madadh-allaidh faith in all but name, and it trades cloth with Baile Mòr fhionn and the harbour of Inis thais.

  • 27 an Giblean 3254 BDE — Baile gheal in the south-west
  • 8 an Lùnastal 1360 DE — The second wolf-house at Baile gheal
  • 21 am Faoilleach 1824 DE — The carters of Baile gheal

Àth fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 1,647

Founded 6 an Cèitean 20 BDE by ford-keepers of the Direwolf road. Known for ford on the Direwolf pilgrims' road.

Àth fhiadhaich of the south-west is a ford on the pilgrimage road from Caol leathan to the temple at Inis thais. It grew from a single house of the long quiet centuries into a small town that lives on the pilgrims. It keeps the Direwolf's faith.

Siorrachd Baile ghlas

Baile dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 680

Founded 1 an Giblean 1848 DE by human administrators near Seann Warr. Known for former clerks' town by Seann Warr.

Baile dhubh was built in the Age of Strangers as a clerks' town for the human administration near Seann Warr, where the fifth regiment is now stationed. After the Severance its Ròdaich people took up the Direwolf faith of the country around it. It has fewer than seven hundred people and lives on the garrison.

Baile ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 35,358

Founded 14 an t-Samhain 2067 BDE by rope-makers of the capital shore. Known for rope-walks and sail-lofts.

Baile ghlas is a great harbour town on the capital shore and the seat of its province. Its rope-walks and sail-lofts have fitted ships for the capital since the Holy Age, and it claims, with no record to prove it, to have rigged the Sundering fleet. It has never been walled; the capital's walls stand close by.

  • 7 an Cèitean 3554 BDE — The harbour at Baile ghlas
  • 16 am Faoilleach 1997 BDE — Baile ghlas burned
  • 5 an Dàmhair 1799 DE — The fishermen of Baile ghlas

Doire fhada

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 10,892

Founded 3 an t-Sultain 321 DE by woodsmen of the capital shore. Known for walled long grove.

Doire fhada, the long grove, is a walled village of the capital shore, founded in the long quiet centuries. It was walled in the Age of Strangers to protect its grain stores. It keeps the capital's faith.

Siorrachd Baile ghorm

Achadh fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,804

Founded 23 an Lùnastal 1930 BDE by farmers of the south-east. Known for fair field under Làrach an Dùin.

Achadh fhionn is a village of the south-east, founded in the Holy Age in a fair field under Làrach an Dùin. It keeps the ancestor rite and leaves the ruin alone. Its people say the ruin was old when the first Ròdaich came.

Baile dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 8,916

Founded 7 an t-Samhain 1463 DE by rope-walkers of Baile ghorm. Known for rope-walks and the panthers' road.

The deep town a short walk inland of Baile ghorm, where the harbour's rope-walks and timber-yards were moved to be clear of storms. The panthers' migration road, Imrich nam Pantar, crosses its fields, and the townsfolk shut their stock in when the cats pass. It follows the Madadh-allaidh faith and works almost entirely for the harbour and its fleet.

  • 15 am Faoilleach 5154 BDE — The panther season kept at Baile dhomhain

Baile ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 23,309

Founded 22 an Gearran 2162 BDE by farming kindreds of the south-eastern downs. Known for south-eastern grain and wool market.

Baile ghorm is the market of its shire, a large open town without walls where the south-eastern farms bring their grain and wool. Its people keep the oldest folk rite, and household shrines to the ancestors outnumber any public house of worship. Achadh fhionn is its nearest field-village, and the ruin of Làrach an Dùin stands in its hinterland, left alone by custom.

  • 23 an t-Iuchar 608 BDE — Baile ghorm's penance
  • 16 an t-Samhain 1025 DE — The blue dyers of Baile ghorm
  • 13 am Màrt 1100 DE — The Baile ghorm blue fades
  • 14 an Lùnastal 1899 DE — Ore-lamps from Baile ghorm

Baile ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 27,580

Founded 7 an t-Ògmhios 2484 BDE by net-fishing families of the southern shore. Known for the third fleet's anchorage and wolf-post quays.

A landing of drying-racks and boat-sheds on the southern coast, Baile ghorm grew through the Holy Age into the largest harbour between the capital and the eastern capes. Its people keep the faith of Clach, the Resplendent Direwolf, and its quays are lined with the wolf-head posts that mark a Madadh-allaidh harbour. Since the Long War it has been the station of An treas cabhlach, the third fleet, and its yards do more repair work for the crown than fishing for themselves. Its smaller twin, Baile dhomhain, lies a short walk inland and sends it timber and rope.

  • 9 am Faoilleach 6929 BDE — Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid
  • 12 an Gearran 6918 BDE — The salt-pans of Baile ghorm
  • 8 an t-Ògmhios 6874 BDE — Iain Dubh killed
  • 2 am Màrt 5173 BDE — The first songs kept
  • 8 an t-Samhain 81 BDE — The potters of Baile ghorm
  • 12 an Dàmhair 1700 DE — Storm at Baile ghorm
  • 13 an t-Iuchar 1991 DE — The hides of Baile ghorm
  • 1 an Dùbhlachd 2020 DE — An treas cabhlach raised
  • 25 an Cèitean 2024 DE — The third fleet's tank-hulls

Cnoc bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 10,718

Founded 23 an Dùbhlachd 691 DE by the hill-lords of Baile ghorm. Known for the market above the mill-race.

A walled pale hill in the south-east above the long mill-race of Muileann fhada, which grinds its grain. The walls were raised when the road from Làrach an Dùin became unsafe. It keeps the old spirits and is the market of the southern-eastern farms.

Muileann fhada

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,280

Founded 16 an t-Samhain 578 DE by millers of the house of Tormod mac Ruairidh. Known for the long mill-race and first-sack offering.

A long mill-race cut beside a south-eastern stream gave the town its name and its living, grinding the grain of the farms about the other Baile ghorm. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the roads past Làrach an Dùin carried ore-wagons and the thieves who followed them. It keeps the old spirits, and the millers still leave the first sack of each season at the race-head for the ancestors. Cnoc bhàn on the hill above buys most of its flour.

Siorrachd Baile mhin

Baile mhin

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 20,963

Founded 17 an t-Ògmhios 1314 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the north-east. Known for smooth harbour of the north-east.

Baile mhin is a harbour town of the north-east and the seat of its province, founded in the Holy Age. Its harbour is sheltered and its trade steady. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, and the old harbour of Seann Vell lies within its province.

  • 13 am Faoilleach 1833 DE — Baile mhin ships the eastern ore

Seann Vell

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,910

Founded 1 an Gearran 12,822 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for old harbour stones and seal-hunters.

Seann Vell of Baile mhin is a small harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site in the north-east, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. It lives on the seal-hunt and the fishing. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

  • 26 an t-Sultain 10,644 BDE — The north-eastern Seann Vell

Siorrachd Baile Mòr dhomhain

Achadh dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 776

Founded 30 an t-Ògmhios 1962 DE by settlers under the restored kingdom. Known for kingdom-era straight fields.

Achadh dhìreach was laid out in straight fields by the restored kingdom, when extraction returned to full scale and the towns of the plain needed feeding. It is small, fewer than eight hundred people. It feeds Baile Mòr àrsaidh.

  • 16 an Cèitean 12,593 BDE — The first hearths of the high valleys
  • 13 an t-Sultain 8400 BDE — The stained cloth of Achadh dhìreach
  • 7 an t-Iuchar 6535 BDE — The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach

Baile Mòr dhomhain

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 17,651

Founded 24 an t-Samhain 2957 BDE by the lords of the deep river. Known for the deep-river city and its fords.

A walled city with a citadel on a deep river in the north, the seat of Siorrachd Baile Mòr dhomhain. It was one of the great market cities of the north through the Holy Age and the Sundering and a centre of the human administration in the Age of Strangers. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and holds its four fords and its river landing at Àth shean.

  • 18 an Gearran 2544 BDE — Baile Mòr dhomhain at the foot of the pass
  • 20 am Màrt 155 DE — A court at Baile Mòr dhomhain
  • 16 an Dùbhlachd 522 DE — Death of Dùghall Garbh
  • 1 an Lùnastal 1812 DE — Baile Mòr dhomhain a barge town
  • 30 an t-Sultain 1987 DE — Baile Mòr dhomhain's market

Baile Mòr àrsaidh

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 5,986

Founded 16 an t-Samhain 1662 BDE by Ròdaich traders of the northern plain. Known for ancient market of the northern plain.

Baile Mòr àrsaidh is an ancient market city of the northern plain, ranked a city for its age rather than its size. Its market was old in the Holy Age. It takes oak from Doire dhìreach and grain from Achadh dhìreach.

Baile òg

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,790

Founded 25 am Màrt 71 DE by carters of Baile Mòr dhomhain. Known for a carters' stop between two cities.

A small young town on the road between Baile Mòr dhomhain and Baile Mòr àrsaidh, grown from a carters' stable. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and lives by changing horses.

Cuan bheag

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 18,125

Founded 1 an Dùbhlachd 1515 DE by coasting traders of the northern shore. Known for sheltered harbour and the northern watch.

Cuan bheag, the small harbour, was a fishing water until the Age of Strangers, when human ships wanted a sheltered anchorage on this side of the island and made it busy. The restored kingdom built its citadel to watch the northern approaches, and the town has since become one of the larger ports of the province. Its people keep the capital's faith of the Dark Unicorn.

Doire dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 8,421

Founded 1 an Dàmhair 2352 BDE by Ròdaich woodwards of the Baile Mòr dhomhain plain. Known for straight-grown oak for keels.

An oak grove kept by woodward families, whose trees grow unusually tall and true. The record of the Sundering says the shipwrights sent to Doire dhìreach for keels when the ocean ships were built, and the village has told that story of itself ever since. It has grown into a large village of timber-yards and cooperages, serving Àth mhòr and Baile Mòr àrsaidh.

Inis leathan

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,410

Founded 29 an Giblean 1259 DE by ferrymen of the broad isle. Known for ferrymen of the broad isle.

Inis leathan is a village on a broad island off the north coast, founded in the long quiet centuries by ferrymen who ran boats to the mainland. In the Age of Strangers its ferry carried supplies to the tavern and mill at Muileann fhada. It still keeps the ferry, and little else.

Muileann fhada

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,702

Founded 8 an Dàmhair 2449 BDE by millers of the northern mining road. Known for An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the mining road.

Muileann fhada, the long mill, is a small walled town on the old mining road of the north. An Taigh-seinnse Reòta stands at its edge, one of the great taverns of the old circuit. Colbh Cnoc chiar stands to the west, and the town's people say the stone's two words are older than any mill.

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,924

Founded 5 an t-Sultain 480 DE by the ford-wardens of Baile Mòr dhomhain. Known for walled ford on the city's north road.

One of the island's many narrow fords, this one a walled post on the north road into Baile Mòr dhomhain. The city built its walls to hold the crossing in the troubles before the Severance, and it is still garrisoned in name. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Àth chiar

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 5,863

Founded 30 an Lùnastal 1308 DE by the ford-guards of Baile Mòr dhomhain. Known for carriers' town on the west road.

A dusky ford on the west road out of Baile Mòr dhomhain, walled against the roads' thieves in the Age of Strangers. It is a carriers' town, and the road-house An Taigh-seinnse Reòta at Muileann fhada lies a short way down the road. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Àth ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,648

Founded 16 an Giblean 110 DE by the grey-stone quarrymen. Known for the worked-out grey quarry.

A ford over grey water on the road between Baile Mòr dhomhain and the south, it grew up around a quarry whose pale-grey stone faces half the city's houses. The quarry is now worked out, and the town has shrunk to a waystation for carriers. Its people keep to Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Àth mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 4,601

Founded 26 an Cèitean 1401 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the northern plain. Known for ford on the northern tavern road.

One of several towns of this name, this Àth mhòr carries the tavern road across the river near An Taigh-seinnse Reòta. It was a waypoint on the mining roads in the Holy Age and a militia halt in the years before the war. It trades oak from Doire dhìreach down the road to the towns of the plain.

Àth shean

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 3,324

Founded 8 an t-Ògmhios 513 BDE by boatmen of the Baile Mòr dhomhain river. Known for the river landing of Baile Mòr dhomhain.

The old ford and landing that served Baile Mòr dhomhain before the city had quays of its own. Barges from the landing carry the city's goods to the coast, and the boatmen's guild here is older than the city's walls. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh like its great neighbour and is counted, for most purposes, as the city's river-port.

Siorrachd Baile Mòr mhòr

Baile Mòr mhòr

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 35,852

Founded 26 an Lùnastal 2977 BDE by the early kings of the northern province. Known for the great walled city of the north.

Baile Mòr mhòr is the great city of the north, walled and crowned by a citadel, and the seat of its province. It was a royal seat in the Holy Age and a centre of the human administration in the Age of Strangers. Since the Severance it has stood close to the Tuathaich country to the west, the largest Ròdaich city on that frontier.

Caol ìseal

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,953

Founded 25 am Faoilleach 1571 BDE by the strait-watchers of the north coast. Known for the strait watch-fire.

A small harbour-village on the northern strait, with a citadel built to watch the channel. It served Baile Mòr mhòr as a signal-station and watch-post and has never outgrown that role. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich, and the watch-fire on its citadel is still lit on the old feast nights.

Dùn thais

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,755

Founded 10 an Dàmhair 1545 BDE by custodians of the northern coast. Known for northernmost Ròdaich citadel.

Dùn thais of the north is the northernmost Ròdaich citadel, raised by the Holy Age custodians on the northern coast. Since the Severance it has watched the Tuathaich country. It keeps the ancestor rite.

Siorrachd Baile ruadh

Baile ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 19,896

Founded 3 an Dàmhair 2028 BDE by red-earth farmers of the east. Known for red-earth fields of the east.

A red town of the east and the seat of Siorrachd Baile ruadh. It keeps the old spirits and trades grain with Achadh naomh.

  • 13 an Lùnastal 90 BDE — The watch-tower at Baile ruadh
  • 3 an t-Sultain 1207 DE — Baile ruadh's quarrel with Achadh naomh
  • 20 an Dàmhair 1827 DE — Baile ruadh loses its seed
  • 3 an Lùnastal 1981 DE — The shafts at Baile ruadh left open

Cnoc fhionn

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 11,165

Founded 25 an t-Samhain 2811 BDE by orchard-keepers of the north-east. Known for fair-hill orchards and cider.

Cnoc fhionn, the fair hill, is a large town of orchards and farms in the north-east. It has been settled since the Holy Age and keeps the ancestor rite. Its apples and cider go down to the harbour at Seann Tarr.

  • 5 an t-Iuchar 9143 BDE — The first dog graves

Siorrachd Baile àrsaidh

Baile àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 20,073

Founded 6 an t-Ògmhios 2171 BDE by Ròdaich teachers of the Yellow Scorpion. Known for the Yellow Scorpion's teachers.

Baile àrsaidh is the ancient town of the west, the seat of its province and the place where the teachers of the Yellow Scorpion have kept their school since the faiths divided. It is a large town of twenty thousand. It trades with Seann Skell to the north and with the fleet at Cuan shean to the south.

  • 19 an t-Samhain 2120 BDE — Baile àrsaidh on the western heath
  • 9 an Gearran 1789 DE — The fever at Baile àrsaidh

Doire chaol

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 5,858

Founded 16 an t-Ògmhios 84 DE by Ròdaich woodwards of Baile àrsaidh. Known for narrow oakwood of Baile àrsaidh.

A village in a narrow oakwood south of Baile àrsaidh, felling for the yards at Cuan shean as the larger Doire gharbh does. The two oakwood villages have argued over the same buyers in every age. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

Seann Bhral

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 20,300

Founded 5 an Dàmhair 11,997 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for west-coast harbour of the Scorpion faith.

Seann Bhral of the west coast is a Seann-Dhaoine site the Ròdaich resettled in the Holy Age. It grew into a large port on the western sea roads and took up the Yellow Scorpion faith, which is strong along this coast. Its harbour is unwalled, trusting to the citadel at Ros bheag to the north.

Siorrachd Baile ìseal

Baile ìseal

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 17,099

Founded 16 an t-Sultain 1528 DE by Ròdaich farmers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the low walled town of the north-west.

A low walled town in the north-west, the seat of Siorrachd Baile ìseal, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It follows the Yellow Scorpion and is one of the larger Tuathaich towns.

  • 2 an t-Ògmhios 1868 DE — Baile ìseal sends its people

Baile òg

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,885

Founded 5 an t-Samhain 1933 DE by Tuathaich families sent north at the Severance. Known for the first Tuathaich-built houses.

Baile òg, "the young town", was built by Tuathaich families who arrived after the Severance and found no empty village to take. It stands a short way from the larger Tuathaich town of Baile ìseal and has always depended on it. Its houses are the first the Tuathaich built for themselves on the island rather than inherited.

Doire gheal

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 830

Founded 10 an Dàmhair 1844 DE by human settlers of the Age of Strangers. Known for one of the oldest human families.

A small white oak grove settled by humans in the early years after the Crossing, one of the few human foundations of the north-west. Its people stayed through the Severance and are among the oldest human families on the island. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

Àth bheag

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 932

Founded 14 an Giblean 1938 DE by Tuathaich families sent north at the Severance. Known for a ford settled after the Severance.

A small ford settlement founded by Tuathaich families who came north at the Severance. It has fewer than a thousand people. It trades with Baile ìseal and Baile òg, the other Tuathaich towns of its province.

Siorrachd Caol bheag

Baile bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 6,025

Founded 21 an Giblean 1595 DE by fullers of the northern coast. Known for bleached cloth from the fulling-mills.

A town of fulling-mills and white cloth between the port-city of Ros chiar and the city of Baile Mòr dhìreach. Its fullers bleached wool for the harbours of the north coast and still do, though in smaller measure since the trade moved to Inis mhòr. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Baile Mòr dhìreach

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,107

Founded 8 an Gearran 1267 BDE by custodians of the north-eastern road. Known for walled town on the straight road.

Baile Mòr dhìreach of Caol bheag is a walled town with a citadel, built by Holy Age custodians where the north-eastern road runs straight. It is small for a city, but it holds the road and the market between Inis mhòr and Baile gharbh. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Caol bheag

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,189

Founded 15 am Màrt 2522 BDE by fishers of the north coast. Known for the elder Caol bheag on the strait.

A small harbour on the northern strait, older than its far larger namesake inland and the one that gave that town its name. It keeps the old spirits and is a quiet fishing town, though An ceathramh rèisimeid, stationed at the larger Caol bheag, sends its patrols here.

  • 9 an Dàmhair 1924 DE — Caol bheag's empty quay

Caol bheag

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 42,649

Founded 14 an Lùnastal 2406 BDE by Ròdaich seafarers of the small strait. Known for fourth regiment's harbour town.

Caol bheag is a harbour town of more than forty thousand on the small strait, crowned by a citadel and the seat of its province. The fourth regiment, raised in the Long War, is stationed here. The mills of Muileann bheag and the wool of Cnoc chiar pass through its quays.

  • 14 an Gearran 5154 BDE — Boats named for the winds
  • 2 an t-Samhain 2020 DE — An ceathramh rèisimeid raised
  • 22 an Dùbhlachd 2024 DE — The fourth regiment leaves Ceann mhòr

Siorrachd Caol fhiadhaich

Caol fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 19,115

Founded 12 an t-Iuchar 2857 BDE by the strait-pilots of the south-west. Known for strait-pilots and the harbour wolf-stone.

A harbour on a wild strait whose pilots earned their living guiding ships through the rocks. It is the seat of Siorrachd Caol fhiadhaich and a large town of the Madadh-allaidh faith, trading with the great tavern-village of Doire shean on its road. The strait pilots still take no ship through without an offering to Clach at the harbour wolf-stone.

  • 27 am Màrt 6012 BDE — The fish-traps of Caol fhiadhaich
  • 14 an Dùbhlachd 1963 BDE — Caol fhiadhaich rebuilt
  • 2 an Gearran 117 DE — The coughing sickness at Caol fhiadhaich
  • 2 an Gearran 1866 DE — The boats of Caol fhiadhaich sold
  • 7 an t-Sultain 2004 DE — The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich

Cnoc dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 1,587

Founded 4 am Màrt 1079 DE by carters of Caol fhiadhaich. Known for carters' stop on the south-west road.

A small town on a straight hill road between Caol fhiadhaich and the great mill-town of Muileann bheag. It follows the Madadh-allaidh faith and is a stop for carters.

Muileann bheag

fort · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 13,749

Founded 31 an Cèitean 1256 DE by wardens of the panther roads. Known for citadel north of the panther roads.

Muileann bheag is a fort with a citadel north of Baile dhomhain, whose fields the panthers of Imrich nam Pantar cross. It is not the Muileann bheag of the northern lighthouse. Travellers stop at Am Buabhall Fortanach nearby, and the first fleet lies at Àth gharbh a short way west.

Siorrachd Caol gharbh

Caol chrom

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 3,192

Founded 13 an Dùbhlachd 1236 DE by the garrison of the bent strait. Known for fortified bent strait.

Caol chrom is a fortified harbour on a bent strait of the north-east, walled and given a citadel in the long quiet centuries. It is a city by rank but small in people, and its garrison has always outnumbered its fishermen. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

  • 7 an Gearran 1977 DE — The north-eastern harbours

Caol gharbh

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 26,717

Founded 5 am Màrt 2276 BDE by Ròdaich seafarers of the rough strait. Known for boatyards on the rough strait.

Caol gharbh is a walled harbour on the rough strait and the seat of its province, a village in name but a town of twenty-seven thousand in fact. Its boatyards take oak from Doire chaol and build the heavy boats the strait demands. Its quarrel with Seann Bhrenn next door is as old as the rolls.

  • 10 am Màrt 3473 BDE — Caol gharbh on the rough strait

  • 10 an t-Samhain 1695 DE — Caol gharbh loses the salt
  • 11 an Gearran 1834 DE — Caol gharbh bypassed

Doire chaol

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,925

Founded 22 an Lùnastal 723 DE by woodwards for Caol gharbh's yards. Known for oak for Caol gharbh's boatyards.

A village in a narrow oakwood that has sent timber to the boatyards of Caol gharbh since the yards were opened. It has always been small and has always been owed money by the yards. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Siorrachd Caol leathan

Baile Mòr fhionn

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 18,849

Founded 6 an t-Samhain 982 BDE by the lords of the western plain. Known for the fair citadel of the western plain.

A great fair walled city of the west, seat of lords before the kingdom and a fortress since. Its citadel was held by Ròdaich forces through the war that ended in the Severance, and it is a city of Clach, the Resplendent Direwolf. It is the chief market of the plain between the capital and the western harbours.

  • 31 an Dàmhair 1865 DE — Wool devalued at Baile Mòr fhionn
  • 29 an Cèitean 1935 DE — The Wolf houses stand aside

Caol leathan

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 8,622

Founded 12 am Faoilleach 2784 BDE by the strait-pilots of the western shore. Known for strait tolls and the western pilots' guild.

Caol leathan grew on the wide strait that gives it its name, where the western pilots of the Holy Age took a toll from every boat bound for the capital's waters. Its walls and citadel were raised in the Age of Sundering to hold the strait, and were manned again when the strangers' ships began to use it after the Crossing. It is the northern anchor of the Direwolf country, and its priests look south to the temple at Inis thais for their rite.

Siorrachd Caol mhin

Caol mhin

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,648

Founded 17 am Màrt 1654 BDE by Ròdaich seafarers of Baile Mòr mhòr. Known for calm-strait harbour of Baile Mòr mhòr.

Caol mhin is the harbour of Baile Mòr mhòr on the calm strait, and its fortunes have always followed the city's. It is walled against raiders from the sea. Its quays load wool and hides from the northern uplands.

  • 11 an Giblean 1855 DE — Quarantine at Caol mhin

Siorrachd Caol mhòr

Baile dhubh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,709

Founded 4 an t-Samhain 1865 DE by human colliers of the northern seams. Known for coal pits of the northern holdouts.

Baile dhubh, "the black town", was built by human colliers in the Age of Strangers on one of the northern coal seams, which the humans worked alongside the vein in the south. After the Severance it passed to the Tuathaich with the rest of the north. Before the Long War it was one of the communities that refused the new fuel and kept working the last workable seams.

Baile àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,857

Founded 15 am Màrt 1348 BDE by Ròdaich shore-lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for old walls in the Tuathaich north.

An ancient walled town near the harbour of Caol mhòr, one of the Ròdaich towns resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The walls are older than the Ròdaich say they know, and the Tuathaich have kept them. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

Caol mhòr

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 42,002

Founded 23 an Dùbhlachd 621 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for chief harbour of the Tuathaich.

Caol mhòr, the great strait, was a Ròdaich harbour of the Holy Age. After the Severance it became the chief port of the Tuathaich, and it is now their largest town. Its yards take timber from Doire mhin, and its people keep the Yellow Scorpion faith.

Caol naomh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 3,184

Founded 9 an Dàmhair 956 BDE by Ròdaich ferrymen; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the holy strait's ferry.

Caol naomh, the holy strait, is a harbour of the north-west founded by Ròdaich ferrymen in the Holy Age, who held the crossing sacred and blessed each boat before it put out. It was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance, and the new ferrymen kept the blessing without the old words. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith.

Cnoc bhàn

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 10,780

Founded 11 an Lùnastal 1806 BDE by Ròdaich hill-lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Tuathaich southern guard-post.

A pale hill with a citadel built by a Ròdaich family in the Holy Age, taken over by the Tuathaich when their homeland was fixed. The Tuathaich garrison it as a guard-post on their southern marches, and it follows the Yellow Scorpion. The town sells cattle and hides to Cnoc àrsaidh.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 8,231

Founded 5 an t-Iuchar 1683 DE by Ròdaich founders; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for the last coal pits of the north.

Cnoc dhubh is a black hill with coal seams in its flank, first dug by the Ròdaich for building-stone and later by the humans for coal. The Tuathaich who resettled it kept the pits open. It was among the northern communities that refused the dubhan economy, and its pits were the last in the north to close after the Long War.

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,000

Founded 19 am Màrt 2579 BDE by Ròdaich shepherds; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for hill pasture and the old cairn.

Cnoc àrsaidh is a hill village of the Holy Age crowned by a cairn older than its name. Its Ròdaich families went south at the Severance and Tuathaich households took their holdings. It is a small place of hill pasture, looking down on the harbour of Caol mhòr.

  • 8 an Giblean 5824 BDE — The flint of Cnoc àrsaidh

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 704

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 986 BDE by Ròdaich hill-lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for an empty citadel on the southern march.

A tiny ancient hill with a citadel, far larger than the handful of people who now live in it. It was a Ròdaich keep until the Severance and has been a Tuathaich watch-post since. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

Cuan bheag

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,782

Founded 10 am Màrt 1946 DE by Tuathaich fishing families. Known for Tuathaich fishing boats and drying racks.

Cuan bheag of the north-west was built by Tuathaich fishing families in the first years after the Severance, on a shore the Ròdaich had never settled. It is a village of boats and drying racks. It sells its catch through Caol mhòr.

  • 20 an t-Sultain 1948 DE — Boats lost off Cuan bheag

Doire mhin

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 10,048

Founded 3 an Giblean 256 BDE by Ròdaich woodsmen of the Holy Age. Known for oak timber for the Caol mhòr yards.

An oak-grove village of the Holy Age, Doire mhin was emptied of its Ròdaich families in the years of the Severance and filled by Tuathaich households moved north. It is a large village for its kind, living on the smooth-barked oaks that name it. Its timber goes down to the yards of Caol mhòr, and its people keep the Yellow Scorpion faith.

  • 2 an Gearran 1935 DE — Joseph Marlow's ploughshares

Muileann fhionn

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,690

Founded 12 an t-Iuchar 1802 DE by human administrators of the northern landing. Known for strangers' fort of the north.

Muileann fhionn was built as a fort and mill by human administrators in the Age of Strangers, to guard the northern landing. After the Severance it became a Tuathaich town. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith.

  • 6 am Màrt 1920 DE — Muileann fhionn shut in

Ros mhòr

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 8,600

Founded 15 an t-Ògmhios 393 DE by Ròdaich fishers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for big headland harbour of the Tuathaich.

Ros mhòr of the north-west is a harbour on a great headland, founded by Ròdaich fishers in the long quiet centuries. After the Severance it was resettled by the Tuathaich and grew with the northern trade. It lies between the harbours of Caol mhòr and Caol naomh.

  • 5 an Cèitean 1971 DE — Ros mhòr's boatyard

Àth fhionn

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 844

Founded 25 an Cèitean 1793 DE by human traders, as a waystation. Known for a human waystation at the fair ford.

Àth fhionn was a waystation of human traders on the road north, built in the Age of Strangers at a fair ford. The Tuathaich kept it after the Severance. It is small, fewer than a thousand people, and its inn is still built in the humans' manner.

Àth leathan

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,686

Founded 24 am Faoilleach 886 DE by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for a drovers' ford in the north.

The northern Àth leathan is a drovers' ford resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is not the battlefield of the Long War, which lies far to the south-west, and its people have spent a generation correcting travellers. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

  • 11 am Faoilleach 5787 BDE — The flint road

Siorrachd Caol shean

Achadh dhomhain

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 11,801

Founded 27 an t-Iuchar 128 BDE by hosts of the Allt an Àigh pilgrims. Known for hosts to Allt an Àigh pilgrims.

Achadh dhomhain of Caol shean is a large village beside Allt an Àigh, the stream of fortune. Pilgrims have come to drink from it since the Holy Age, and the village lives on them. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 10,649

Founded 13 an t-Ògmhios 402 BDE by the keepers of Allt an Àigh. Known for Allt an Àigh, the stream of fortune.

A rough field village beside Allt an Àigh, the stream said to grant fortune to those who drink at the right phase of the moon. Pilgrims have come since the Holy Age, and the keepers' citadel was built to guard the stream from anyone who would bottle and sell it. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, whose philosophers have never agreed whether the stream's luck is real.

  • 11 an Gearran 1940 DE — The walkers at Achadh gharbh

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 3,640

Founded 16 an Giblean 2124 BDE by Ròdaich pilgrims to Allt an Àigh. Known for the nearest town to Allt an Àigh.

Baile dhìreach is the nearest town to Allt an Àigh, and the straight road that gives it its name runs from its square down to the stream. It grew up in the Holy Age to serve the pilgrims and still does, alongside Cnoc ìseal further up the road. Its people are wary of strangers who come at the wrong phase of the moon.

Caol shean

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 31,718

Founded 21 an Lùnastal 2960 BDE by the strait-fishers of the east coast. Known for the great eastern harbour, pilgrims' landing.

An old harbour on the eastern strait and one of the great ports of the island, seat of Siorrachd Caol shean. It shipped the ore of the central mountains when the extraction was at its height and now ships dubhan and grain. The spring of Allt an Àigh lies in its hinterland, and pilgrims to it land here; the town follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

  • 11 am Faoilleach 3374 BDE — The harbour at Caol shean

Cnoc chrom

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,719

Founded 26 an Cèitean 1814 DE by Ròdaich miners under contract. Known for abandoned shafts beneath a walled hill.

A crooked hill-town raised when the extraction contracts pushed the diggings out from the central mountains toward the coast. Its walls were thrown up against the raids of the troubles before the war, and the shafts beneath it gave out before the Severance. It is now a small town of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh that sends its young to the harbour at Ros fhionn.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 8,278

Founded 23 an Giblean 1174 BDE by Ròdaich pilgrims to Allt an Àigh. Known for pilgrim lodgings on the Allt an Àigh road.

Cnoc ìseal began as a halt for pilgrims going down to Allt an Àigh, and its inns still fill at the phase of the moon when the stream is said to give fortune. Its nearness to Muileann chaol has drawn scholars as well, and many readers of the library lodge here. The town keeps the Fèidh habit of arguing a question before answering it.

Doire fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,551

Founded 19 an Lùnastal 2330 BDE by woodsmen of the eastern hills. Known for oak grove on the pilgrims' way.

Doire fhionn of Caol shean is an oak-grove village on the way to Allt an Àigh. Pilgrims to the stream have lodged in its houses since the Holy Age, and the Library at Muileann chaol stands on the road to the north. Its people follow Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Ros fhionn

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 4,377

Founded 10 am Màrt 1737 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the east. Known for harbour of the Allt an Àigh pilgrims.

Ros fhionn of Caol shean is a citadel harbour on the eastern coast, near the stream of Allt an Àigh. It is where most pilgrims to the stream land, and its citadel was raised in the Age of Sundering to guard them. It is not the Ros fhionn of the old bridge, which lies to the north.

  • 15 am Faoilleach 1929 DE — The eastern pits at Ros fhionn

Àth dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 5,250

Founded 22 an t-Samhain 1598 DE by ford-keepers of Caol shean. Known for the inland ford of Caol shean.

A deep ford on the road from Caol shean inland, where goods from the harbour are loaded from boats to carts. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Siorrachd Caol ìseal

Baile shean

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,859

Founded 13 an Dùbhlachd 2272 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the northern shore. Known for old quay of the northern shore.

Baile shean is an old quay on the northern shore and the port of its province. The inn An Taigh-seinnse Reòta lies inland on the road south, and its pickled spinach goes out through the quay. It is one of several places named Baile shean.

Caol ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 16,600

Founded 21 am Màrt 1549 BDE by salt-makers of the northern coast. Known for salt pans of the low strait.

Caol ìseal is a harbour town on a low strait of the north coast and the seat of its province. Its salt pans have supplied the northern fisheries since the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite.

  • 31 an Cèitean 1330 DE — The Caol ìseal fishers go east
  • 2 an Gearran 1915 DE — Powder landed at Caol ìseal

Cnoc bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,395

Founded 21 am Màrt 5 BDE by fishers of Caol ìseal. Known for white-hill kelp and herring.

Cnoc bhàn grew as an overflow of the harbour at Caol ìseal, a white hill with a landing at its foot. Its boats work the kelp beds and the herring of the northern shore. It keeps the ancestor rite and has never needed walls.

Cnoc uaine

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,458

Founded 17 an t-Ògmhios 1266 DE by the garrison of the north-coast road. Known for hill fort over the north-coast road.

Cnoc uaine of Caol ìseal is a hill fort over the north-coast road, raised in the long quiet centuries and walled since. Its garrison watched the road through the Age of Strangers. It keeps the ancestor rite.

Siorrachd Cathair dhearg

Cathair dhearg

capital · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 10,274

Founded 23 an t-Samhain 2533 BDE by the custodian-kings of the Holy Age. Known for royal seat and temple of the Dark Unicorn.

Cathair dhearg, the red city, began as the stone-walled seat of the Holy Age custodians where the mining roads came down to the sea on the Abhainn dhomhain; Drochaid Cathair dhearg, heir of the first bridges, still carries the road across the river. It kept its walls, citadel and temple through the Sundering and the Age of Strangers, and after the Severance Rìoghachd Ròdais was declared here and Niall was crowned in it, first of the restored line. The royal precinct is small for a capital, ringed by the great harbours of Ros dhomhain, Cathair dhomhain and Baile ghlas, and its temple is the first house of Uallach, the Dark Unicorn.

Siorrachd Cathair dhomhain

Cathair dhomhain

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 29,409

Founded 7 an Gearran 2379 BDE by Ròdaich shipwrights of the river mouth. Known for deep-water harbour beside the capital.

Cathair dhomhain, the deep city, stands beside the capital on the deep-water side of the river mouth, and takes the ships whose draught the royal quays cannot. It was walled and given a citadel in the Holy Age, and its temple of the Dark Unicorn is second only to the capital's. Its harbour carried much of the ore trade in the Age of Strangers and most of the dubhan trade since.

Ceann gheal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 12,722

Founded 8 an Gearran 1289 DE by fishers of the white headland. Known for white headland and the Toll-dubh hollow.

Ceann gheal is a harbour town north of the capital, founded in the long quiet centuries. The hollow called Toll-dubh lies in the hills behind it; it has never been mapped, and the town's people do not go near it. It keeps the capital's faith.

Cill ghorm

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,014

Founded 13 an t-Ògmhios 366 BDE by priests of the Dark Unicorn. Known for fortified chapel above the capital road.

A chapel site on the ridge above the road north from Cathair dhearg, fortified in the Holy Age to guard the approach to the capital. The citadel dwarfs the village, which has never numbered more than a thousand or so, most of them in service to the garrison and the shrine. Pilgrims of Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh stop here before entering the capital.

Siorrachd Cathair fhada

Cathair fhada

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 20,928

Founded 9 am Màrt 1239 BDE by the lords of the long city. Known for merchants of the Fèill Muileann òg.

A long walled city in the south, strung along a ridge between the capital's country and the coast, and the seat of Siorrachd Cathair fhada. It follows the Dark Unicorn and has always been one of the capital's chief supports. The Fèill Muileann òg is held a short way north, and the city's merchants dominate it.

  • 13 an Cèitean 5077 BDE — Cathair fhada on the south coast

Cnoc ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 6,817

Founded 9 an Dàmhair 1580 DE by herders of the south road. Known for red-hill pasture on the south road.

Cnoc ruadh of Cathair fhada is a hill town on the south road, founded in the long quiet centuries by herders who grazed the red hill. It grew as a stopping place between the southern ford towns and the capital. Its people keep the capital's faith and sell hides at the market of Àth shean.

Siorrachd Cathair mhòr

Cathair mhòr

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 49,298

Founded 30 an Giblean 2422 BDE by Ròdaich custodians of the interior roads. Known for the great city beside the old outpost.

Cathair mhòr, the great city, was raised by the Holy Age custodians beside Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, a Seann-Dhaoine outpost already in ruins when the first Ròdaich walls went up beside it. It commands the roads between the gulf and the vein country, and it was a counting-house of the tithe in the Age of Strangers and a mustering place in the war that ended it. An treas rèisimeid, raised in An Cogadh Fada, is stationed here and bears its name.
