Siorrachd Ceann bheag

Achadh fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 3,499

Founded 10 an t-Ògmhios 726 DE by horse-breeders of the north. Known for wild-field hay and horses.

Achadh fhiadhaich is a village of the north-east, founded in the long quiet centuries on wild pasture that no earlier people had fenced. It breeds horses and grows hay for the coast, and the carters of Ceann bheag have bought its horses for generations. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Ceann bheag

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 22,637

Founded 15 an t-Iuchar 2688 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the north-east. Known for citadel harbour of the north-east.

Ceann bheag is a citadel harbour of the north-east, a Holy Age landing that grew with the coastal trade. Its citadel was raised in the Age of Strangers to guard the anchorage the human ships used. The villages of Ceann thais and Achadh fhiadhaich lie within its province and send their goods through its quays.

  • 27 am Màrt 1922 DE — Ceann bheag stops

Ceann thais

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,605

Founded 30 an Giblean 295 DE by fishers of the north-east. Known for An Leòmhann Buidhe, the Yellow Lion.

Ceann thais is a harbour village of the north-east, best known for An Leòmhann Buidhe, one of the great taverns of the old mining circuit, which stands at its edge. It was founded in the long quiet centuries. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Ros chiar

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 4,614

Founded 1 an t-Iuchar 2992 BDE by the headland-lords of Ceann bheag. Known for the fortified headland harbour.

A dusky headland city on the north coast, walled, with a citadel on the rock and a harbour below. It was one of the harbours the human traders first used after the Crossing, and its citadel was taken and retaken in the war before the Severance. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and competes with Caol bheag for the northern trade.

Siorrachd Ceann leathan

Baile gheal

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,009

Founded 11 an t-Samhain 243 DE by lime-burners of Ceann leathan. Known for lime kilns of the east.

A small town of lime kilns whose white dust gives it its name. It supplies lime to the builders of the eastern coast and the fields around Ceann leathan. It keeps the folk tradition of the ancestors.

Ceann leathan

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 14,116

Founded 27 am Màrt 1189 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the east. Known for broad headland harbour of the east.

Ceann leathan of the east is a harbour town and the seat of its province, founded in the Holy Age on a broad headland facing the open sea. It is not the gulf city of the melee, and its people resent the confusion. It keeps the ancestor rite and a fishing fleet that works as far south as the waters off Seann Bhral.

  • 25 an t-Iuchar 1826 DE — A cove burned near Ceann leathan

Siorrachd Ceann mhin

Achadh fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,747

Founded 15 an Dùbhlachd 21 DE by Ròdaich barley farmers. Known for barley fields and remount pastures.

A farming village of fair barley fields between Baile mhin and Àth ghlas. In the Age of Strangers its pastures were taken for the horses of the administration, and they have served as remount grounds for the soldiers of the district ever since. It is a quiet place, larger in fields than in people.

Caol dhomhain

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,070

Founded 8 an Gearran 1190 DE by the watch of the deep strait. Known for the deep strait's watch-tower.

Caol dhomhain is a harbour village on a deep strait of the south-east, with a citadel raised in the long quiet centuries to watch it. The village is small and the citadel is its reason. It keeps the ancestor rite.

Ceann mhin

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 32,321

Founded 18 an Lùnastal 2254 BDE by shipwrights of the smooth headland. Known for shipyards of the smooth headland.

Ceann mhin is a citadel harbour on the southern gulf shore, long the chief shipyard of the east. When Tonn Mhòr struck in the first years of the restored kingdom, its yards were spared and it took in the survivors of Achadh mhin. It has since grown into one of the great cities of the south.

  • 5 an t-Sultain 1510 DE — The fire of Ceann mhin
  • 6 an t-Sultain 1840 DE — The pay office at Ceann mhin
  • 11 am Màrt 1983 DE — Ceann mhin's fish-market

Ceann mhin

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 19,533

Founded 12 an t-Iuchar 1336 BDE by harbour-lords of the smooth headland. Known for the northern ore harbour.

A smooth headland port, walled, and the seat of Siorrachd Ceann mhin. It was a trading harbour for the northern mines in the Age of Strangers and follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Ceann mhin

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 19,395

Founded 17 an t-Iuchar 220 BDE by Ròdaich fishers settling in the ruin of Làrach an Dùin. Known for harbour beneath Làrach an Dùin.

Ceann mhin is built in and around Làrach an Dùin, the ruined fortress of the old builders, and its harbour lies under the fallen walls. The Ròdaich fishers who settled there in the Holy Age reused its stones but never finished clearing it; nobody knows who built the fortress. It is now a walled port town of nearly twenty thousand, the seat of its province, and the rival of Ceann chaol along the same coast.

  • 26 an Dùbhlachd 4554 BDE — Ceann mhin on the south-eastern shore
  • 12 an t-Ògmhios 183 BDE — Anna Ruadh at Ceann mhin

Cnoc dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,252

Founded 20 an Lùnastal 2977 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of Tuam Cnoc dhìreach. Known for keepers of Tuam Cnoc dhìreach.

A small town beside Tuam Cnoc dhìreach, the necropolis whose oldest graves are older than its oldest legible names. Its families have kept the necropolis since the Holy Age, when it received its first formally recorded burial. It lives on the burials of the eastern coast and on the masons who cut the stones.

  • 26 an t-Ògmhios 2805 BDE — The grave-keepers of Cnoc dhìreach

Cnoc fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,584

Founded 2 an t-Samhain 1769 DE by hunters of the north-east hills. Known for game and hides for Ceann mhin.

A wild hill above Ceann mhin, settled by hunters and later by carters on the harbour road. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and sends game and hides down to the port.

Cnoc ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 16,474

Founded 30 am Faoilleach 707 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of Calbh Cnoc ghorm. Known for the doctrine stone.

The blue hill grew up around Calbh Cnoc ghorm, the standing column carved with the doctrine itself: Cha do thàinig sinn; bha sinn ann. If the doctrine has a birthplace it may be here, and the town has never let the island forget it. It is a large town now, and pilgrims of every faith climb to the stone.

  • 17 an Giblean 8000 BDE — The gatherings at the column
  • 6 an Lùnastal 1929 DE — The fight at Cnoc ghorm

Cnoc thais

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,511

Founded 3 an t-Iuchar 497 DE by hill-farmers of the south-east. Known for cattle on a misty hill.

A damp hill above the small harbour of Caol dhomhain in the south-east. It keeps the old spirits and sends its cattle to Baile gheal.

Muileann leathan

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,802

Founded 16 an Dàmhair 1384 DE by millers of Ceann mhin. Known for broad mill serving Ceann mhin.

A walled mill town a short way inland from Ceann mhin, whose broad mill-pool is the largest on that coast. It was walled when Ceann mhin was, in the Age of Strangers, to protect its stores. Its flour goes to the ships at Ceann mhin and never to the rival quays of Ceann chaol.

Seann Bhrenn

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 8,695

Founded 15 an Lùnastal 12,894 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for old harbour quarrelling with Caol gharbh.

Seann Bhrenn is an old harbour of the Seann-Dhaoine, settled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. It lies hard beside Caol gharbh, and the two harbours have quarrelled over the same water for as long as there are records, each claiming the other was built on its fishing ground. It is a port town of nearly nine thousand and the older of the two by its name.

  • 5 an Giblean 10,806 BDE — The twin landings of Seann Bhrenn

Àth ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,789

Founded 7 am Màrt 353 DE by Ròdaich ford-keepers. Known for grey ford that replaced the old bridge.

A small town at a grey ford upstream of Drochaid Ros fhionn. It took the traffic when the old bridge fell out of use, and grew as the bridge-villages shrank. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Siorrachd Ceann mhòr

Ceann mhòr

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 32,420

Founded 6 an Cèitean 1987 BDE by Ròdaich fishers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for great headland harbour under the Baile chrom light.

Ceann mhòr is a great harbour on a headland of the north-west, under the beacon of Taigh-solais Baile chrom. It was a Ròdaich port of the Holy Age, struck by Gorta Baile chrom in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith.

  • 14 am Màrt 1830 DE — A fishing station at Ceann mhòr

  • 8 am Màrt 2014 DE — The Tuathaich depots
  • 10 an t-Samhain 2020 DE — The regiments at Ceann mhòr

Cill ìseal

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 15,029

Founded 14 an t-Iuchar 896 DE by Ròdaich shrine-keepers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Scorpion shrine of the north-west.

A low church-site village of the Ròdaich, emptied at the Severance and resettled by Tuathaich families. It has grown past any village size, with the shrine of the Yellow Scorpion at its heart, and it farms for the harbour of Ros ruadh. The Tuathaich here call it by its Ròdaich name and no other.

Doire chaol

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,560

Founded 28 an Dùbhlachd 1195 DE by Ròdaich charcoal-burners; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for narrow oakwood and charcoal.

A charcoal village in a narrow oakwood, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The newcomers kept the Ròdaich shrine of the Yellow Scorpion they found there rather than raising their own, as several villages of this coast did. It still burns charcoal for the smiths of Àth fhionn and Àth dhearg.

Ros ruadh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 7,782

Founded 29 an t-Iuchar 1636 DE by Ròdaich fishers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the First Canoe telling of the north-west.

A red headland harbour on the north-west coast, one of the Ròdaich harbours given to the Tuathaich after the Severance. The fishing families of Ros ruadh are among those who keep the First Canoe fragment alive in speech, and some say the steersman of that telling put out from this headland. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

  • 29 an Dàmhair 9829 BDE — Seven boats lost off Ros ruadh

Àth dhearg

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 5,681

Founded 15 an Giblean 1090 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for red ford under the Baile chrom light.

A red ford on the western coast below the lighthouse of Baile chrom, struck by Gorta Baile chrom in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its people keep the Yellow Scorpion, as most of this coast does. It is not the Àth dhearg of the north-eastern lighthouse.

Àth fhionn

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 8,986

Founded 14 an Dùbhlachd 1224 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for fair ford of the western coast.

A fair ford on the western coast road below the lighthouse of Baile chrom, struck by Gorta Baile chrom in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is a town of nearly nine thousand and the market for Doire chaol's charcoal. Its people follow the Yellow Scorpion, as most of this coast does.

Siorrachd Ceann àrsaidh

Achadh fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 9,904

Founded 21 an t-Sultain 1774 DE by Ròdaich farmers who reclaimed the wild field. Known for reclaimed wild fields.

A village of fields reclaimed from wild ground in the Age of Sundering, when the island had fewer mouths and more hands to spare. It feeds the towns of Ceann àrsaidh and sends its surplus to Muileann chrom to be ground. It is a large village now, of nearly ten thousand.

Baile chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 8,072

Founded 16 an Lùnastal 697 DE by Ròdaich market families of Ceann àrsaidh. Known for the bent-street market.

Baile chrom is named for its bending main street, which follows an old stream-bed. It is a market town between the capital and the northern plain, serving Baile fhiadhaich and Cuan chrom. It shares its name with three other places on the island, and the chroniclers take care to give its province.

Baile fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 3,925

Founded 7 an Dàmhair 368 DE by Ròdaich hunters of Ceann àrsaidh. Known for hunters and hide-curers.

The wild town was a hunters' camp in the Age of Sundering, when the forests of Ceann àrsaidh were larger. It still lives on hides and game, and its curing-sheds can be smelled from the road. Its people trade at Baile chrom.

Ceann àrsaidh

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 18,711

Founded 19 an t-Iuchar 877 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the east. Known for ancient headland on the eastern ship road.

Ceann àrsaidh is a walled harbour city on an ancient headland east of the capital. It has been a port since the Holy Age and the gateway to the eastern sea road. An Taigh-seinnse Mòr stands on the road to the west.

  • 19 an t-Sultain 377 BDE — The bridge at Ceann àrsaidh
  • 12 an Giblean 1830 DE — The family of Eachann Mòr

  • 26 an Giblean 1943 DE — The chandlers of Ceann àrsaidh

Cnoc bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 8,536

Founded 5 an t-Samhain 1225 DE by priests of Uallach, the Dark Unicorn. Known for training acolytes of the Dark Unicorn.

A pale hill in the midlands, crowned by a house of Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh, the faith of the capital. The town grew around the priests' farms and remains a quiet place of tithe-barns and schools that train acolytes for the capital's temples. Baile dhomhain and Àth ghlas send it their tithes and their sons.

Cnoc ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 4,631

Founded 24 an t-Sultain 1152 DE by herders of Cathair mhòr. Known for horse pastures of Cathair mhòr.

A blue-grey hill town just north of Cathair mhòr, pasturing the garrison's horses. It follows the Dark Unicorn and has always been the city's stable.

Siorrachd Cill dhìreach

Baile bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 5,156

Founded 30 an t-Sultain 1229 DE by a custodian house of Cill dhìreach. Known for citadel above Cill dhìreach.

Baile bhàn is a white town with a citadel above Cill dhìreach, built to guard the church-town and its treasuries. It is a town of five thousand. Its garrison keeps order at Còmhrag Ceann leathan.

Cill dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 24,187

Founded 12 am Màrt 400 BDE by priests of the Dark Unicorn. Known for church-town of the Ceann leathan melee.

Cill dhìreach is a church village of twenty-four thousand and the seat of its province. It lies beside Ceann leathan, where Còmhrag Ceann leathan is held each year. Its priests tend the wounded of the melee and bury its dead.

  • 19 an t-Sultain 1851 DE — The shrine at Cill dhìreach

Siorrachd Cill thais

Baile ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,818

Founded 1 an t-Sultain 788 DE by farmers of Cill thais. Known for small walls near the capital.

A small walled town near Cill thais and Baile chiar, west of the capital. The walls were raised in the war before the Severance. It follows the Dark Unicorn and has little trade of its own.

Cill thais

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 18,934

Founded 15 an t-Samhain 1066 BDE by wardens of the sacred wood. Known for wardens of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag.

Cill thais, the damp cell, is a large village and the seat of its province, founded in the Holy Age beside Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag. The forest is sacred to the Dark Unicorn and has never been settled, logged or fully mapped, and the village's wardens keep others out of it under the division of custody that settled the holy-wood dispute. In the Age of Strangers the wardens refused the timber contracts, and the record does not say how they were allowed to.

  • 6 an t-Iuchar 1805 DE — The orphans of Cill thais

Cnoc bheag

fort · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 12,455

Founded 26 an t-Ògmhios 1865 BDE by custodians named in the holy-wood dispute. Known for fort at the edge of the holy wood.

Cnoc bheag is a fort with a citadel at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, the forest that has never been settled or logged. It was raised after the holy-wood dispute of the Holy Age, when custody of the wood was divided rather than awarded, to house the custodians of the share that went to the faith now called Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh. It stands outside the trees, never within them, and its twelve thousand people guard the capital's south as well as the wood.

  • 8 an t-Iuchar 5148 BDE — The first house at Cnoc bheag

Siorrachd Cnoc bheag

Achadh fhada

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 5,174

Founded 31 an Cèitean 625 DE by priests of the Hungry Hawk. Known for the Hawk-faith fields.

A long field village in the wooded middle west, one of the few settlements where Creideamh an t-Seabhaig, the Rite's older form, still holds. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers. Its fields feed the Hawk-faith mill at Muileann uaine.

Achadh mhòr

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 6,399

Founded 28 an Gearran 143 BDE by Ròdaich farmers of Cnoc bheag. Known for border fields south of the Tuathaich line.

A farming village of six thousand just south of the Tuathaich line. It follows the Yellow Scorpion, like its neighbours across the line. It trades with both sides and has been watched by both.

Baile dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 2,324

Founded 2 an t-Samhain 1101 DE by Ròdaich followers of the Hawk. Known for walled deep-valley town of the Hawk.

Baile dhomhain is a walled town in a deep valley near Cnoc bheag, one of the towns of the Hawk. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers and strengthened after the Severance, when the Tuathaich line was drawn close by. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers. Its trade goes down to the quay at Ceann òg.

Ceann òg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 3,349

Founded 19 an t-Sultain 1787 DE by Ròdaich and human traders together. Known for young quay near Carragh Cnoc bheag.

Ceann òg, "the young headland", was built as a trading quay in the first years after the Crossing, when exchange with the humans was still reciprocal. It stands near Carragh Cnoc bheag, the stone carved Bha teine sa chloich. The Green Death, A' Phlàigh Uaine, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It follows the Hawk, and its quay was rebuilt after the Severance for Ròdaich ships alone.

Cnoc bheag

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 49,661

Founded 10 an Dàmhair 1401 BDE by hill kindreds of the north-central coast. Known for the carved stone and the Sixth Regiment.

Cnoc bheag is the small hill only in name: it is the largest town of the north-central coast and the heart of the Hawk's congregations. The standing stone Carragh Cnoc bheag, carved 'there was fire in the stone', stands a short walk to the south, and the town's older families say their fathers' fathers found it there. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck the town in the Age of Strangers. Since the Severance it has faced the Tuathaich border, and An siathamh rèisimeid, raised in An Cogadh Fada, is stationed here under the town's name.

Inis ìseal

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 3,217

Founded 11 an Dùbhlachd 820 DE by the garrison of Cnoc bheag. Known for island fortress guarding Cnoc bheag.

Inis ìseal is a low island off Cnoc bheag, fortified in the long quiet centuries to guard that town's harbour and walled again in the Age of Strangers. Since the Severance it has been a frontier fortress, facing the Tuathaich coast across the water. The Green Death, A' Phlàigh Uaine, struck its garrison in the Age of Strangers, and it is a city by rank and a barracks in practice.

  • 26 an Cèitean 1964 DE — The Hawk houses' own custodian

Muileann uaine

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 5,601

Founded 3 an t-Sultain 406 BDE by priests of the Hungry Hawk. Known for the Hawk-faith mill.

A green mill in the wooded middle west, one of the few towns where Creideamh an t-Seabhaig, the Rite's older form, still holds. The carved hawk over the mill-door is said to be as old as the Binding of the First Flame. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and since then the second sense of 'uaine' has clung to its name.

Ros dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 4,232

Founded 30 an Lùnastal 586 DE by fishers of the Hawk coast. Known for walled fishing village of the Hawk coast.

Ros dhìreach of Cnoc bheag is a walled fishing village on the north-central coast, founded in the long quiet centuries. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It was walled after the Severance, when the Tuathaich coast became a frontier. It keeps the Hawk's rite.

Tobar dhomhain

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 665

Founded 17 am Màrt 1811 DE by miners of the western hills. Known for the well of a lost camp.

A deep well-village in the western hills, dug to supply a mining camp that has since been abandoned. It is one of the smallest villages on the island and follows the Yellow Scorpion.

Siorrachd Cnoc bhàn

Baile thais

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 11,570

Founded 28 an Cèitean 816 BDE by Ròdaich eel-fishers of the water-meadows. Known for water-meadows and eel traps.

Baile thais stands on damp ground where the meadows flood each wet season, and its people have always fished the ditches for eels. It is a large town now, and it supplies Cnoc bhàn with hay and fish. The river works that keep the meadows are older than the town's charter.

Ceann dhomhain

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,589

Founded 7 am Màrt 1257 BDE by custodians of the eastern headland. Known for the library's harbour and cargo registers.

A small city on a deep-water headland, with a citadel that looks out to sea and back toward the mountain roads. Ships put in here for the library town of Muileann chaol, whose scholars and copyists travel through its gate, and its harbour-masters have long kept a copy of every cargo list for the Leabharlann. The Feallsanachd an Fhèidh holds the city, and its scholars are counted among the library's oldest correspondents.

Cnoc bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 16,069

Founded 12 am Màrt 2945 BDE by a custodian house of the Binding. Known for white citadel and the Fèidh disputations.

The white hill was fortified early by a custodian house, and its citadel of pale stone is the oldest standing work in the province that bears its name. In the Age of Strangers it served as a district seat of the human administration, and the ledgers kept in its strong-room were among those later lost in the war. It is now a large town of scholars and advocates: the disputations of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh are held in its hall, and its readers walk daily to the library at Muileann chaol.

Doire dhubh

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 5,158

Founded 26 an Dùbhlachd 476 BDE by Ròdaich woodwards of Cnoc bhàn. Known for dark oak for the library's shelves.

A village in a dark oak grove a short way north of Muileann chaol. When the library was founded its oak was cut for the shelves and reading-tables, and the woodwards still claim a right to repair them. It sends its remaining timber to Cnoc bhàn and Baile thais.

Muileann chaol

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,706

Founded 12 am Màrt 429 BDE by grain-millers of the Holy Age. Known for the library's misaddressed parcels.

The smaller and older of the two Muileann chaols, a narrow mill beside a small keep in the eastern hills. The great library stands in its namesake to the south-east, and the library's carriers are said still to bring misaddressed parcels here. It is a Feallsanachd an Fhèidh town, and its mill feeds the villages of Achadh gharbh and Tobar dhubh.

  • 5 am Faoilleach 1904 DE — The second Muileann chaol

Muileann chaol

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 5,496

Founded 24 an Dùbhlachd 469 DE by millers of the narrow race. Known for Leabharlann Muileann chaol, the great library.

A narrow mill town in the eastern hills, and the home of Leabharlann Muileann chaol, the library that keeps the most complete record of the island. The library was founded in the new kingdom and has since taken in the provincial archives, and its war archive is sealed. The town lives on the library and on the harbour at Ceann dhomhain, and to put a thing in the Library is to settle it.

Muileann fhada

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,719

Founded 21 an Giblean 1759 BDE by millers of the Ros fhionn river. Known for a river port gone quiet.

A long mill-house on the Ros fhionn gave the place its name, and a river quay below it made it a port, sending flour downstream by barge. Its walls date from the Age of Strangers, when a tithe store was kept here and needed guarding. Trade on the river dried up when the carts took the traffic, and the crossing of Drochaid Ros fhionn just upstream is now rarely used; the town has shrunk to its walls.

Tobar dhubh

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,743

Founded 7 an t-Samhain 1409 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers of Cnoc bhàn. Known for the dark well of old telling.

A village around a deep well whose water runs dark, said in the old telling to rise from near the vein. It has never been proved so, and the Fèidh scholars of Cnoc bhàn have argued it both ways. The well still draws visitors who drink from it for luck.

Tobar dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 8,108

Founded 25 an t-Iuchar 362 DE by well-diggers of Baile thais. Known for the straight water-channel.

A large well village in the central-east, laid out along a straight channel that carries its water. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and supplies water and vegetables to Baile Mòr uaine and Baile thais.

Siorrachd Cnoc dhubh

Baile òg

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,898

Founded 7 an Dàmhair 479 DE by stone-gatherers of the temple hills. Known for houses of stone from Làrach an Teampaill.

A young town in the eastern hills close by the ruins of Làrach an Teampaill, whose altar faces the vein. Its early houses were built of stones carried off the ruins, a use the priests of the old spirits later forbade. It keeps the old spirits and serves travellers who come to look at the ruins.

Ceann ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 12,761

Founded 29 an Giblean 356 DE by pilots of the eastern coast. Known for pilots of the eastern coast.

Ceann ghorm, the blue headland, is a harbour town of the eastern coast whose pilots have long guided ships into the waters of Ros fhionn and Seann Dunn. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and grew in the Age of Strangers. Its people follow Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Cnoc bheag

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,621

Founded 5 an Dàmhair 988 DE by shepherds of Cnoc dhubh. Known for shepherds' market below Cnoc dhubh.

A small hill town below Cnoc dhubh, holding the shepherds' market for the province. It has always been a dependent of the larger town. It is one of several places named Cnoc bheag and is not the fort of the holy wood near the capital.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 11,141

Founded 10 an t-Iuchar 601 DE by charcoal-burners of the black hill. Known for charcoal for the smithies.

A black hill where charcoal burners worked through the long centuries of the Sundering, the Small-Burning Law forbidding them the ore. It is the largest of the cluster of Cnocs in the eastern hills and their common market. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, and its charcoal is still sold to smiths who will not work with dubhan.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 10,389

Founded 2 am Faoilleach 2734 BDE by a custodian house that quarried the black hill. Known for black-stone quarries and walled market.

The black hill is an outcrop of dark stone that the early custodians hoped was the vein; it was not, and the quarry that tested it became a town. Cnoc dhubh is the seat of its province, a walled market for the herders and quarrymen of the hills near Làrach an Teampaill. Prospectors dug here again in the Age of Strangers and found only rock, a result the town's chroniclers record with some satisfaction.

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,738

Founded 20 an t-Iuchar 371 DE by hill-farmers from Cnoc dhubh. Known for the summit cairn and eastern barley.

The 'ancient hill' of the eastern cluster of Cnocs is in fact among the younger of them; the chroniclers think the name was taken from a cairn on its summit rather than from the town. It is a small farming town of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh that sells its barley in Cnoc dhubh and Àth dhomhain.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,884

Founded 8 an Dùbhlachd 1860 DE by miners' families from Cnoc dhubh. Known for overflow houses of Cnoc dhubh.

The 'young hill' was settled by families spilling out of Cnoc dhubh when the mass excavation drew workers to the eastern hills. It has little of its own beyond houses and a meeting-hall of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, and its people work in the fields and shops of its larger neighbour.

Doire bhàn

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,141

Founded 14 an t-Iuchar 13 BDE by the oak-cutters of Seann Dunn. Known for timber for the coast harbours.

A white oak grove between Seann Dunn and Seann Mhorn, cut for charcoal and ship-timber. It keeps the old spirits and is a large, quiet village with no walls.

Doire fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 16,332

Founded 13 an t-Samhain 1651 BDE by custodians of Cnoc dhubh. Known for citadel village of Cnoc dhubh.

Doire fhiadhaich of Cnoc dhubh is a village only by the old rank; it is large, and it has a citadel raised by the Holy Age custodians who held these hills. Làrach an Teampaill lies in the hills to its east. Its people keep the ancestor rite and will not cut the oaks nearest the ruin.

Doire ghlas

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 7,971

Founded 14 an Gearran 2496 BDE by woodsmen of Cnoc dhubh. Known for grey oaks by Làrach an Teampaill.

Doire ghlas of Cnoc dhubh is a village of grey oaks near Làrach an Teampaill. It was founded in the Holy Age, and its people have guided visitors to the ruin ever since. It keeps the ancestor rite.

Inis uaine

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 5,290

Founded 3 an t-Ògmhios 941 DE by boatmen of the eastern coast. Known for barracks of the Eighth Regiment.

Inis uaine is a harbour town on a green island of the eastern coast, founded in the long quiet centuries. After An Cogadh Fada, An t-ochdamh rèisimeid was stationed here and took the town's name, and the barracks have changed the town's trade from fish to soldiers' wants. It keeps the ancestor rite.

  • 16 an t-Samhain 2020 DE — An t-ochdamh rèisimeid raised
  • 14 an Dùbhlachd 2024 DE — The eighth regiment at Inis uaine

Muileann gharbh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,475

Founded 12 am Màrt 1812 DE by a human ore concern. Known for rough mill of the ore road.

Muileann gharbh, the rough mill, was built in the Age of Strangers to crush ore on the road down to the eastern harbours. When the mountain was worked day and night the mill never stopped, and the town grew no larger than the mill needed. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, which found many hearers among the mill hands.

Muileann leathan

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 7,664

Founded 15 an Dùbhlachd 1253 BDE by the millers of the wide stream. Known for wide mill-wheels, grain for Seann Mhorn.

A broad mill on a slow river, old enough that its founding is recorded only in the king-lists of the Holy Age. It grinds for the coast-town of Seann Mhorn and for the villages round Àth àrsaidh, and its people keep the old spirits. The temple ruins of Làrach an Teampaill lie in the hills behind it, and the millers will not quarry them.

Seann Dunn

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 15,318

Founded 5 an Cèitean 4773 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for An Taigh-seinnse Òir and the temple road.

Seann Dunn keeps a Seann-Dhaoine name, and its citadel stands on footings no Ròdaich mason laid. It is the harbour and lodging-place for those who visit Làrach an Teampaill in the hills to the north, and its own temple serves the ancestor rite. An Taigh-seinnse Òir, one of the great taverns of the old mining circuit, stands in the town itself.

Seann Mhorn

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 5,044

Founded 5 an t-Iuchar 11,931 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for Seann-Dhaoine stones in the harbour wall.

The Seann-Dhaoine left the harbour-stones and the name Morn; the Ròdaich, finding both, called the place Seann Mhorn and built on top. It is a walled port with a citadel over the harbour mouth, fought over more than once in the troubles before the Severance, and it keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich. Stones of the older builders are set into the harbour wall, and the fishermen touch one before they sail.

Tobar shean

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,420

Founded 29 an Lùnastal 783 DE by well-keepers of Baile òg. Known for the walled well on the temple road.

An old well-village in the eastern hills, walled in the troubled years because its well was the only sure water on the road past Làrach an Teampaill. It keeps the old spirits, and the well-keepers still close the gate in dry seasons and ration the water by the bucket.

Àth uaine

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 4,214

Founded 6 an Cèitean 1842 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Known for camp graves by the green ford.

Àth uaine of Cnoc dhubh began as a mining camp at a ford in the Age of Strangers. Its camp graves lie in the field by the ford, tended by the ancestor rite's keepers. The camp outlived its working and became a small farm town.

Siorrachd Cnoc dhìreach

Cnoc dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 18,778

Founded 21 an Lùnastal 817 DE by a custodian house of the eastern diggings. Known for walled seat of the mining district.

Cnoc dhìreach is the walled seat of the eastern mining district, a town of nearly nineteen thousand. It was walled in the Age of Strangers, when the strikes in the district made the administration nervous. It is not the small town of the necropolis on the south-east coast.

  • 18 an Dàmhair 133 BDE — Cnoc dhìreach's weavers
  • 12 an Lùnastal 1918 DE — The signatories of Cnoc dhìreach

Doire gharbh

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 12,662

Founded 5 an t-Iuchar 1230 DE by Ròdaich woodwards of Cnoc dhìreach. Known for palisade under the Doire uaine hills.

A large village in rough oakwood below the Doire uaine hills, walled against the thing that the old inscriptions say walks in those hills. The record gives a more ordinary reason: the walls went up in the Age of Strangers, when the strikes in the eastern district reached its gates. The warm springs of Muileann ruadh lie a short walk east.

Siorrachd Cnoc gheal

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,843

Founded 6 am Màrt 1115 DE by road-builders of Cnoc gheal. Known for the straight road to Seann Bhrenn.

A straight town on the road from Cnoc gheal to Seann Bhrenn, named for the road that made it. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and is a carters' stop on the way to the coast.

Baile fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,834

Founded 6 am Faoilleach 563 DE by farmers of the north-east. Known for walled farm town of the north-east.

Baile fhiadhaich of Cnoc gheal is a walled farm town of the north-east. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and walled in the Age of Strangers against raiders from the sea. It keeps the ancestor rite.

Cnoc gheal

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 14,488

Founded 5 an t-Iuchar 71 BDE by hill-farmers of the north-east. Known for the white hill market of the north-east.

A white hill in the north-east, seat of Siorrachd Cnoc gheal, looking down on the Seann-Dhaoine harbour of Seann Bhrenn. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and is the market for Baile dhìreach and Àth dhearg.

  • 27 am Màrt 1922 DE — The quarrymen of Cnoc gheal

Seann Tarr

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,869

Founded 17 an Lùnastal 8218 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the Old Ones' landing stones.

Seann Tarr is a small harbour whose landing stones are older than any Ròdaich work, and the root in its name is not Gaelic. Ròdaich fishers settled it in the Holy Age and gave it the name it bears, marking it as a place of the Old Ones. On clear nights the lighthouse of Àth dhearg can be seen from its quay, and its boats steer by it.

  • 2 an t-Iuchar 7173 BDE — The count at Seann Tarr

Tobar bhàn

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 4,449

Founded 13 an Cèitean 2031 BDE by well-keepers of the north-eastern shore road. Known for white well and the lighthouse keepers.

Tobar bhàn is a well village on the north-eastern shore road, named for a spring whose water runs white with chalk. The beacon of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg stands on the coast beyond it, and through the later Age of Strangers the village kept the lamp-keepers in bread and peat. Its people hold to the ancestors and the weather, and still leave a cup at the well before a sea-journey.

Àth dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 8,302

Founded 19 an Dùbhlachd 2635 BDE by ford-keepers of the north-east coast. Known for Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, the north-east beacon.

A red ford-town near the north-east coast, whose name was given to Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, one of the five lighthouses built in the Age of Strangers at the request of human navigators. The beacon burned the ore for more than a century and was among the first things on the island converted to dubhan. The town keeps the old spirits and lives by the coast road and the lighthouse.

  • 28 an Cèitean 1825 DE — Àth dhearg builds the tower

Siorrachd Cnoc ghorm

Baile dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 5,262

Founded 22 an Dàmhair 1103 DE by Ròdaich herders of the black-soil fields. Known for Ròdaich enclave on the Tuathaich border.

Named for the dark earth of its fields, Baile dhubh was an ordinary Ròdaich farm town until the Severance drew the northern border around it. It kept its people when the province of Cnoc ghorm passed to the Tuathaich, and has lived since as a place of exchange and quiet mutual suspicion. Its folk hold the Yellow Scorpion faith, as their northern neighbours do, which is thought to be why they were left in peace.

Ceann dhubh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 3,075

Founded 25 an Cèitean 1257 BDE by Ròdaich headland-fishers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the black headland beside Inis àrsaidh.

A black headland harbour on the north-west coast, all but joined to the city of Inis àrsaidh. It was a Ròdaich fishing town until the Severance and has been a Tuathaich harbour since. It follows the Yellow Scorpion, and its boats sail with Inis àrsaidh's.

Cnoc ghorm

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 25,112

Founded 15 an Dàmhair 717 BDE by Ròdaich farmers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for inland seat of the Tuathaich.

Cnoc ghorm of the north-west is the inland seat of its province and one of the largest Tuathaich towns. It was a Ròdaich farm town of the Holy Age, resettled after the Severance. It is not the place of the stone Calbh Cnoc ghorm, which lies far to the south-east.

  • 25 am Màrt 6238 BDE — Cattle in the north-west
  • 26 an t-Ògmhios 1829 DE — Human farms at Cnoc ghorm
  • 12 an Giblean 1938 DE — The Scorpion houses of the north
  • 29 an Giblean 1939 DE — The school of the Scorpion at Cnoc ghorm
  • 11 an Gearran 1955 DE — The northern Scorpion feast

Inis àrsaidh

city · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,740

Founded 28 an t-Sultain 2757 BDE by Ròdaich island-lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Tuathaich island harbour.

An ancient island city on the north-west coast, all but joined to Ceann dhubh. It was a Ròdaich harbour-city until the Severance and has been Tuathaich since. It follows the Yellow Scorpion and is one of the few Tuathaich harbours with a fleet of its own.

  • 10 an t-Iuchar 1931 DE — The north-west ports without a master

Àth fhada

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 15,665

Founded 18 am Màrt 869 DE by Ròdaich ford-wardens, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the long ford and its toll.

A long ford on the north-western roads, held by a Ròdaich warden-family through the quiet centuries of the Sundering. After the Severance its houses were emptied and given to Tuathaich families shepherded north, who raised the present walls and made it one of the chief towns of their homeland. The Tuathaich here keep the faith of Cnut, the Yellow Scorpion, inherited from the shrines the Ròdaich left behind, and the ford is still paid for in toll.

  • 26 am Faoilleach 1970 DE — The Tuathaich carters' road

Àth uaine

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 10,109

Founded 18 an t-Samhain 823 BDE by Ròdaich weavers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for green ford and flax-weaving.

Àth uaine of Cnoc ghorm is a green ford of the north-west, founded by Ròdaich flax-weavers in the Holy Age. It was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance and still weaves. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith.

Siorrachd Cnoc leathan

Cnoc dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,850

Founded 18 an Dàmhair 1200 DE by tavern-keepers of the eastern road. Known for An Taigh-òsta Grianach.

A straight hill on the mining road in the south-east, home of An Taigh-òsta Grianach, a famous roadside inn that serves pan-fried spinach with black wine. The inn was fortified as a militia waypoint in the troubles before the Severance and took dubhan lamps with the rest of the tavern circuit. It keeps the old spirits and lies close by the ruins of Làrach an Dùin.

Cnoc leathan

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 24,072

Founded 11 am Màrt 2813 BDE by innkeepers of the south road. Known for An Taigh-òsta Grianach on the south road.

Cnoc leathan is a large town and the seat of its province, on the south road of the east. An Taigh-òsta Grianach, one of the great inns of the old circuit, stands to its south. It keeps the ancestor rite.

  • 1 an Gearran 2388 BDE — Cnoc leathan's market
  • 3 am Faoilleach 1929 DE — Cnoc leathan's riflemen
  • 21 an Giblean 1979 DE — Cnoc leathan's schools

Cnoc thais

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 11,502

Founded 20 an Dùbhlachd 235 DE by reed-cutters of Cnoc leathan. Known for reed-cutters and thatch.

Cnoc thais is a damp hill whose reed-beds thatch the roofs of the eastern plain. It is a town of eleven thousand. Its cutters work the beds in the dry months and its thatchers travel in the wet.

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 4,133

Founded 15 am Faoilleach 151 DE by Ròdaich millers of Cnoc leathan. Known for red mill on the inn road.

Muileann ruadh is a walled mill town near An Taigh-òsta Grianach, the great inn of the eastern road. Its walls were raised when the inns fortified before the war, and the town and the inn have shared a watch ever since. The unexplored hollow called Toll-dubh lies close by, and the townsfolk keep away from it. It is not the Muileann ruadh of the warm springs to the west.

Àth ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,610

Founded 27 an Lùnastal 390 DE by Ròdaich innkeepers of Cnoc leathan. Known for blue ford by An Taigh-òsta Grianach.

A small town at a blue ford a short way from An Taigh-òsta Grianach, the great roadside inn of the eastern circuit. Its people keep stables and sell to travellers. It fortified its inns before the war, as the tavern road did everywhere.

Siorrachd Cnoc mhòr

Cnoc chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,718

Founded 23 an Lùnastal 1923 DE by the ore-carriers of the interior. Known for walled depot of the ore road.

Cnoc chrom was built in the Age of Strangers as a depot on the ore road from the interior to the gulf. It was walled in the years before the war of the Severance, when the mining roads began to arm themselves. It is a small town now and keeps the capital's faith.

Cnoc mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 25,190

Founded 8 am Màrt 1789 BDE by cattle-drovers of the interior. Known for cattle market below Cathair mhòr.

Cnoc mhòr is the market hill below Cathair mhòr, where the interior drove roads meet. It was walled in the Age of Strangers, when the city's markets spilled out to it. It is a prosperous town that keeps the capital's faith and sells the gulf its beef.

Ros dhìreach

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 4,452

Founded 22 an t-Ògmhios 37 DE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the gulf. Known for straight headland harbour.

Ros dhìreach of Cnoc mhòr is a harbour on a straight headland of the gulf, founded in the long quiet centuries. It is a city by rank and the harbour of Cnoc mhòr's cattle trade. It keeps the capital's faith.

  • 15 an Dùbhlachd 1849 DE — Ros dhìreach the second ore port
  • 27 an t-Iuchar 1894 DE — The tram-road to Ros dhìreach

Founded 1 an Lùnastal 2261 BDE by farmers of the southern coast. Known for rebuilt after the Great Wave.

Achadh mhin is a farming village of the south, founded in the Holy Age. Tonn Mhòr struck it in the first years of the restored kingdom and destroyed it in a single night. It was rebuilt and keeps the capital's faith.

  • 13 am Faoilleach 1957 DE — Achadh mhin resettled

Cnoc naomh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 19,961

Founded 10 an Gearran 2669 BDE by the priests of the Dark Unicorn. Known for the priests who buried Muileann ghlas's dead.

A holy hill with a citadel south of the capital, the seat of Siorrachd Cnoc naomh and a house of the Dark Unicorn since the Holy Age. It lies close by the battlefield of Muileann ghlas, and its priests buried the dead of both sides after the Long War's last battle. It is a large town of priests, soldiers and pilgrims.

  • 8 an t-Ògmhios 1231 DE — The battle of Cnoc naomh

Dùn fhiadhaich

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,664

Founded 20 an Giblean 1615 BDE by the lords of the wild hill. Known for refuge from the Great Wave.

A small wild city on a hill south of the capital, near Achadh mhin, which the Great Wave struck. Its hill kept it clear of the water, and it took in the survivors of the villages below. It follows the Dark Unicorn.

  • 4 an Lùnastal 1837 DE — Weighing the grain at Dùn fhiadhaich

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,657

Founded 14 an Lùnastal 1346 DE by red-sandstone millers. Known for red sandstone mill-house.

A small mill-town built of red sandstone, grinding for Baile chrom and the village of Cill fhada. It was never walled, relying on Baile chrom's walls in hard times. Its people keep the faith of Uallach, and the mill-house has a small shrine to the Dark Unicorn above the wheel.

Siorrachd Cnoc shean

Achadh fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,825

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 491 DE by farmers of Cnoc shean. Known for hay from the fair fields.

A fair field village in the south-east, with meadows between the hill-towns of Cnoc shean and Cnoc fhada. It keeps the old spirits and is known for its hay.

Cnoc fhada

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 9,834

Founded 18 am Màrt 1322 DE by hill-farmers of Cnoc shean. Known for terraced farms on the long hill.

A long hill in the south-east farmed in terraces since the centuries after the Sundering. It keeps the old spirits and trades with Muileann dhomhain.

Cnoc shean

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 21,362

Founded 18 am Màrt 2996 BDE by Ròdaich traders of the eastern plain. Known for old hill market of the granary fields.

Cnoc shean is the old hill market for the granary fields of Achadh mhòr, and the seat of its province. It is a town of more than twenty thousand, with grain-halls and a weighing-house older than any coinage on the island. The tavern An Sligeanach Fad' às lies on the road to Achadh mhòr, and its dried deer is sold in Cnoc shean's market.

  • 3 an Cèitean 1888 DE — The fever at Cnoc shean

Àth dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,921

Founded 26 an Giblean 1801 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Known for red ford of the mining camps.

Àth dhearg of Cnoc shean began as a mining camp at a ford in the Age of Strangers, and its red water is said to come from the spoil. It is neither the Àth dhearg whose name the northern lighthouse bears nor the western ford that the Great Hunger struck.

Siorrachd Cnoc thais

Baile shean

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,936

Founded 27 an Cèitean 2442 BDE by Ròdaich founders; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for old walls held by the Tuathaich.

An old Ròdaich town with walls and a citadel, emptied at the Severance and taken over by Tuathaich families. In the years before An Cogadh Fada it was counted among the northern communities that refused the dubhan economy. Its walls still stand, and the Tuathaich guard them as the Ròdaich once did.

Cnoc thais

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 19,291

Founded 13 an Giblean 67 BDE by Ròdaich hill-farmers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the market of the two ancient mills.

A damp hill in the north-west, seat of Siorrachd Cnoc thais, and one of the larger Tuathaich towns since the Severance. It follows the Yellow Scorpion and is the market of the two Muileann àrsaidhs.

Muileann àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 4,008

Founded 20 an Giblean 1740 DE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the younger ancient mill.

The younger of the two Muileann àrsaidhs, walled, a short distance from the elder. Gorta Baile chrom, the Great Hunger, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and it was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

Àth naomh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 12,892

Founded 26 an t-Sultain 219 BDE by Ròdaich priests of the holy ford; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for citadel over the holy ford.

The holy ford was a Ròdaich shrine and crossing, and a citadel was raised over it in the Holy Age. At the Severance the Ròdaich left and Tuathaich families took the town, which is now one of the largest they hold. They keep the citadel manned and the shrine of the Yellow Scorpion open.

  • 6 an Giblean 2015 DE — Àth naomh joins the pit towns
  • 17 an Dùbhlachd 2020 DE — Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg

Siorrachd Cnoc àrsaidh

Cnoc uaine

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 4,930

Founded 31 an t-Iuchar 1116 DE by hill-lords of the south-west. Known for the walled green hill.

A green walled hill in the south-west, fortified against pirates who raided the coast in the centuries after the Sundering. It follows the Madadh-allaidh faith and sends its young to the first fleet at Àth gharbh.

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 16,832

Founded 11 am Màrt 1238 BDE by Ròdaich followers of the Direwolf. Known for Direwolf shrines and the panther watch.

Cnoc àrsaidh is a walled town of Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh and the seat of its province, holding the oldest shrines of that faith. The panther roads pass close by, and the town keeps a watch on them in the season of crossing. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers and have not been needed since.

  • 7 an t-Sultain 7654 BDE — Eleven lost on the panther road
  • 14 am Màrt 5173 BDE — Bone pipes at Cnoc àrsaidh
  • 19 an Giblean 79 BDE — Cnoc àrsaidh's kilns
  • 14 an t-Samhain 1789 DE — The fever turned back at Cnoc àrsaidh

Siorrachd Cuan ghlas

Baile Mòr uaine

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 8,060

Founded 22 am Màrt 2017 BDE by custodians of Cuan ghlas. Known for walled city of the Feallsanachd.

Baile Mòr uaine is a walled city with a citadel in the north-eastern hills, founded in the Holy Age. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and is among its strongholds. Its walls were repaired in the Age of Strangers.

  • 15 an Dùbhlachd 1828 DE — The Deer students of Baile Mòr uaine

Cill àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 9,277

Founded 29 an Cèitean 2326 BDE by teachers of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for retreat of the Feallsanachd teachers.

Cill àrsaidh of Cuan ghlas is an old cell that the teachers of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh took as a retreat early in the school's history. It became a large village of students and farmers. The school's dormant teachers kept it alive through the Age of Strangers, and it filled again at the revival.

Cnoc chiar

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 12,643

Founded 24 am Faoilleach 2583 BDE by Ròdaich shepherds of Cuan ghlas. Known for sheep walks and wool market.

A large town on the dusky hill, living on the sheep walks above it and on the wool trade with Caol bheag. It was a mustering place for fleeces in the Age of Strangers, when the humans bought wool as eagerly as ore. Its market is the busiest in the province.

Cnoc thais

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,622

Founded 28 an Dùbhlachd 45 DE by shepherds of the Cuan ghlas hills. Known for mist, wool and hill cheese.

A damp hill-town above the harbour of Cuan ghlas, its name taken from the mists that sit on it most mornings. It was never walled and never fought over, and its people send wool and cheese down to the harbour and to Cnoc chiar. A small philosophers' house of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh keeps the only books in the place.

Cuan ghlas

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 15,114

Founded 15 an t-Ògmhios 2778 BDE by grey-water fishers of the north-east. Known for the grey harbour and its citadel.

A grey harbour in the north-east with a citadel, the seat of Siorrachd Cuan ghlas, and a large village. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and is served by the hill town of Cnoc thais above it.

Muileann bheag

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 14,577

Founded 23 an t-Sultain 689 DE by millers of Cuan ghlas. Known for mills for Inis mhòr and Caol bheag.

Muileann bheag is a mill town of fourteen thousand grinding for Inis mhòr and Caol bheag. Its mills are among the busiest in the north. It is one of several places named Muileann bheag, and not the fort above the panther roads nor the town of the northern lighthouse.

Àth gharbh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,628

Founded 13 an Gearran 1477 DE by drovers of the central hills. Known for a drovers' ford in the hills.

A rough ford on the hill road near Baile Mòr uaine, where the drovers rest their beasts. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and is a very small place.

  • 10 an t-Samhain 8514 BDE — The hill-folk of the vein
  • 12 an Dàmhair 8454 BDE — The first small burning
  • 5 an Lùnastal 6590 BDE — The measured handful

Siorrachd Cuan ruadh

Baile ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,364

Founded 4 an Gearran 333 DE by Ròdaich slate-quarriers of Cuan ruadh. Known for grey slate of the east coast.

A small town of grey slate on the eastern coast, quarrying for the roofs of Achadh shean and Cnoc uaine. Its people keep the folk tradition of the ancestors.

Cuan ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 19,209

Founded 1 an t-Sultain 477 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the east. Known for the island's easternmost harbour.

Cuan ruadh is the easternmost harbour of the island and the seat of its province, a port since the Holy Age. Its boats go out further than any on the coast, and it has lost more to pirates than any other eastern town. It keeps the ancestor rite.

  • 1 an Gearran 5184 BDE — A' Ghaoth Dhubh
  • 29 am Faoilleach 5124 BDE — Cuan ruadh rebuilt
  • 11 an t-Sultain 87 BDE — Cuan ruadh's boats
  • 20 an Giblean 27 BDE — The star-lore taught at Cuan ruadh
  • 29 an t-Ògmhios 1370 DE — Cuan ruadh's new harbour
  • 24 an Lùnastal 1870 DE — Cuan ruadh loses its trade
  • 25 an Gearran 1952 DE — Cuan ruadh's harbour light

Siorrachd Cuan shean

Baile ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 17,942

Founded 9 am Màrt 1754 DE by red-clay potters of the Cuan shean country. Known for red roof-tiles and scorpion-marked jars.

A red town of potters and brick-makers behind the harbour of Cuan shean, whose kilns have fired the roof-tiles of the western coast since the centuries after the Sundering. It follows the Yellow Scorpion, and its potters mark each jar with a small scorpion under the base. Most of what it makes goes out through Cuan shean.

Cill thais

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,704

Founded 22 an Giblean 122 BDE by priests of the Yellow Scorpion. Known for fortified chapel over the fleet anchorage.

Cill thais is a chapel village on damp ground above the anchorage of Cuan shean, fortified with a citadel in the Holy Age to watch the western sea. The fourth fleet, raised in the Long War, is stationed at Cuan shean below, and the village's priests bless each ship before it first puts out. It is a small place whose citadel is larger than its village.

Cuan shean

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 32,433

Founded 4 an Gearran 2931 BDE by the harbour-lords of the west coast. Known for the fourth fleet's harbour.

The old harbour of the west, the seat of Siorrachd Cuan shean and one of the largest towns on the island. It shipped western grain and timber through the Holy Age and served the human traders after the Crossing. Since the Long War it has been home to An ceathramh cabhlach, the fourth fleet. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

  • 29 an Giblean 2403 BDE — Cuan shean's salt-pans

Doire gharbh

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 12,372

Founded 2 an Dàmhair 1304 BDE by Ròdaich shipwrights' woodwards. Known for rough oak for the western fleet.

A large walled village in rough oakwood that has supplied timber to the yards at Cuan shean since the Holy Age. When the fleet of Cuan shean was raised in the Long War its hulls were cut here. It follows the Yellow Scorpion, as does most of the west.

Àth naomh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,746

Founded 26 an Giblean 861 DE by priests of the Yellow Scorpion. Known for blessing of the harbour carts.

A holy ford near Cuan shean, where the priests of Cnut bless the carts that go down to the harbour. It follows the Yellow Scorpion and is a small town of shrine-keepers and carters.

Siorrachd Doire chaol

Doire chaol

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 24,225

Founded 30 an t-Sultain 1947 DE by households of the restored court. Known for the capital's household village.

Doire chaol was laid out after the Severance on a narrow oak strip south of the capital, to house the families of the royal household. It grew into a large village and the seat of its province. It keeps the capital's faith.

  • 20 an Giblean 1814 DE — The carters of Doire chaol

Àth fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 10,445

Founded 14 an t-Sultain 2004 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the capital. Known for wild ford on the capital's south road.

Àth fhiadhaich is the wild ford on the south road out of Cathair dhearg, a town of ten thousand that grew as the capital grew. Its crossing was paved in the Holy Age, and the road over it carries the capital's trade toward the southern coast. It follows the capital's faith, and its shrine keepers take part in the rites at Cathair dhearg.

  • 21 an Dàmhair 1998 BDE — The fight at Àth fhiadhaich

Siorrachd Doire chiar

Cill dhearg

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,761

Founded 7 an t-Samhain 2450 BDE by priests of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for red chapel by the old bridge.

A church village of red stone near Drochaid Ros fhionn, whose chapel gave shelter to travellers crossing the old bridge when the river trade was busy. As the trade dried up and the bridge fell out of use, the village shrank to its chapel and a few farms. Its priests still keep a lamp at the bridge-end.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,684

Founded 7 an t-Samhain 1222 DE by flax-growers of the north. Known for flax fields and linen.

Cnoc ìseal, the low hill, is a small town of the north-east given to flax and linen. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and has changed little since. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Doire chiar

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 23,587

Founded 28 am Faoilleach 1575 BDE by oak-keepers of the north-east. Known for disputations under the oaks.

A dusky oak grove grown into a large village, the seat of Siorrachd Doire chiar. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, and its philosophers are said to hold their disputations under the oldest trees.

  • 8 an Giblean 3422 BDE — Doire chiar
  • 23 an t-Ògmhios 445 DE — Eilidh Dhubh's tracts
  • 30 an Giblean 1869 DE — The last disputation at Doire chiar

Muileann fhada

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,677

Founded 10 am Màrt 746 DE by millers of Doire chiar. Known for flour for Doire chiar.

A long mill in the north-east beside Muileann dhearg, grinding for the large village of Doire chiar. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Siorrachd Doire fhada

Cuan uaine

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 6,529

Founded 23 an Dùbhlachd 465 BDE by Ròdaich custodians of the capital's east. Known for the green harbour's temple of Uallach.

Cuan uaine, the green harbour, is a walled temple city east of the capital, fortified in the Holy Age to guard the eastern shore. Its temple of the Dark Unicorn is much visited by those who cannot reach the capital's. The barracks harbour of Inis mhòr lies just to the north.

  • 25 an Lùnastal 1929 DE — Cuan uaine opens its harbour

Doire fhada

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 21,905

Founded 27 am Faoilleach 986 BDE by oak-cutters of the capital's forests. Known for ship-timber and the fenced oak.

A long oak grove west of the capital cut for ship-timber since the Holy Age, and the shipwrights who built the Sundering fleet are said to have taken their keels here. The village grew enormous without changing its name, and it is now the seat of Siorrachd Doire fhada and a harbour of the capital's faith. The grove itself is mostly gone, and the village keeps one old oak fenced by the quay.

Siorrachd Doire fhiadhaich

Cnoc shean

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,179

Founded 6 an t-Sultain 1782 BDE by Ròdaich herders of the south. Known for market common on the old hill.

Cnoc shean, the old hill, is a small town of the south, settled since the Holy Age. Its common holds the market of the farms around it. It keeps the capital's faith.

Doire fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 27,501

Founded 19 an Lùnastal 1018 BDE by the oak-keepers of the south. Known for timber for Cathair fhada.

A wild oak grove in the south, grown into a very large village and the seat of Siorrachd Doire fhiadhaich. It follows the Dark Unicorn and supplies timber to the city of Cathair fhada close by.

  • 12 an Dùbhlachd 1809 DE — Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich

Siorrachd Doire fhionn

Achadh àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,452

Founded 12 an t-Ògmhios 2178 BDE by Ròdaich herders on an older field. Known for field-walls older than any record.

Achadh àrsaidh, the ancient field, was named by Ròdaich herders who found its field-walls already standing and old when they came. No record says who laid them. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers and parched its hay-meadows for three dry seasons running. It has stayed a small village of cattle and hay on the eastern uplands, keeping the ancestor rite and its walls in repair.

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 9,699

Founded 1 an t-Samhain 212 DE by carters of the Seann Dunn road. Known for straight road to Seann Dunn.

A town of one straight road running down to Seann Dunn, whose carters take the dyed cloth of Baile ghorm to the harbour. It is a town of nearly ten thousand. It keeps the folk tradition of the ancestors.

Baile ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 4,277

Founded 22 an Lùnastal 270 DE by Ròdaich dyers from Achadh shean. Known for woad dyers and blue-washed houses.

Baile ghorm grew up around woad pits and dye-houses, and in the chroniclers' day its houses were still washed blue from the vats. It sent cloth to Seann Dunn for shipping and yarn to Achadh shean for weaving. The old folk tradition of the ancestors holds here strongly, and the dyers still leave a first skein at the hearth-stone each season.

Baile shean

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,687

Founded 5 an Dàmhair 1344 BDE by keepers of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar. Known for the keepers of the sacred forest's edge.

An old town beside Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, the forest marked sacred before any faith claimed it. Its people have kept the forest's edge since the Holy Age and keep the old spirits, though the forest is now held by Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Cill àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,982

Founded 19 an Giblean 551 BDE by keepers of the ancestor rite. Known for ancient cell of the ancestor rite.

Cill àrsaidh of the north is an old cell of the ancestor rite, founded in the Holy Age and never much more than a village around its shrine. It lies inland of the Hawk bay and has kept to the older faith while its neighbours took up Mòd. The shrine keepers are hereditary.

Cnoc ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 8,412

Founded 22 an Dàmhair 2265 BDE by bee-keepers of the north. Known for blue hill and bee-keeping.

Cnoc ghorm of Doire fhionn is a town of the north-central country, founded in the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite and its bees, whose wax lit the shrines at Cill àrsaidh before dubhan lamps came.

Doire fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 21,604

Founded 20 am Màrt 2602 BDE by Ròdaich woodsmen of the east. Known for great oak grove of the east.

Doire fhionn of the east is the seat of its province, a great village of the Holy Age in an oak grove, which has never been raised to the rank of town despite its size. Its oaks are managed under rules older than the kingdom. It keeps the ancestor rite, and the old field-village of Achadh àrsaidh lies to its north.

  • 10 an Gearran 9200 BDE — The deer-drives of the eastern forest
  • 5 an Dàmhair 1886 DE — Doire fhionn walks for water

Doire fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 13,873

Founded 4 an t-Samhain 1850 BDE by the oak-keepers of the old spirits. Known for an uncut grove of the ancestors.

A fair oak grove in the north, the seat of Siorrachd Doire fhionn and a large village of the old spirits. The grove has never been cut for ship-timber, its keepers holding it for the ancestors, and it lies on the road between Cathair naomh and the Tuathaich line.

  • 26 an Lùnastal 35 BDE — The oaks of Doire fhionn

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 10,120

Founded 29 an Giblean 1416 BDE by Ròdaich millers of the north. Known for red mill and border citadel.

Muileann ruadh of Doire fhionn is a mill town of the north-central country, founded in the Holy Age. Its citadel was raised after the Severance to watch the Tuathaich border. It keeps the Hawk's rite.

Tobar ghorm

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,465

Founded 27 am Faoilleach 78 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers of the northern road. Known for blue spring on the northern road.

A village around a blue spring on the road running north toward the Tuathaich country, and the last Ròdaich water on that road. Since the Severance it has traded with both sides of the line and has been trusted by neither. It is not the larger Tobar ghorm of the wool fairs, and it resents the confusion.

Àth ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,509

Founded 25 an t-Sultain 664 BDE by cattle-drovers of the eastern hills. Known for the drovers' ford and cattle fair.

A red-banked ford where the drovers' road crosses a stream in the east, it has been a cattle-market since the Holy Age. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich, and the drovers still pour a cup into the ford before driving a herd across. The town trades beasts to Seann Dunn on the coast and hides to Baile shean.

Àth uaine

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,572

Founded 25 an Giblean 1676 DE by the wardens of the Achadh shean road. Known for garrisoned green ford.

A small garrison town at the green ford on the road between Doire fhionn and Achadh shean. Its citadel is larger than the town needs, a sign that the ford was once contested, though the record does not preserve by whom. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and it lives now on toll and on the soldiers who still keep the tower.

Siorrachd Doire ghlas

Cnoc mhòr

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 5,564

Founded 5 an t-Sultain 1194 DE by Ròdaich herders; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for keepers of the Muileann bheag light.

Cnoc mhòr of Doire ghlas is a Tuathaich town of the north coast, founded by Ròdaich herders in the long quiet centuries and resettled after the Severance. Its people supply the keepers of Taigh-solais Muileann bheag. It keeps the Tuathaich folk tradition.

  • 17 an Lùnastal 1876 DE — Cnoc mhòr walks south

Doire fhionn

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 5,264

Founded 5 an Dàmhair 443 DE by Ròdaich woodwards; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for pale oaks and Tuathaich hearth-tellings.

A Ròdaich village in a grove of pale oaks, left empty at the Severance and resettled by Tuathaich families sent north. Its people keep Creideamh nan Tuathach, and it is one of the northern households where the First Canoe is still told at the hearth, a telling the Ròdaich priesthood calls superstition. It lives on timber and on the fort at Cnoc leathan nearby.

Doire ghlas

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 40,740

Founded 7 an t-Iuchar 1266 DE by Ròdaich oak-cutters, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the great Tuathaich gathering-village.

A small Ròdaich village in a grey oak grove until the Severance, when the families shepherded north were gathered here before being sent on, and so many stayed that it became the largest settlement in the Tuathaich homeland almost at once. It never took a town's name, and the Tuathaich keep it a village in speech on purpose. It is the seat of Siorrachd Doire ghlas and the heart of Creideamh nan Tuathach, whose keepers are said to hold the First Canoe fragment here; the library has asked to copy it and been refused.

  • 9 an Dùbhlachd 1930 DE — The hungry year at Doire ghlas

Siorrachd Doire mhin

Baile bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 9,453

Founded 19 an Dùbhlachd 1199 DE by Ròdaich traders of Doire mhin. Known for white town on the Muileann ghlas road.

Baile bhàn is a white town of nine thousand near Cathair mhòr, on the road toward Muileann ghlas. Before the last battle of the Long War the state's columns marched through it. It follows the capital's faith.

Baile chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 3,296

Founded 24 am Faoilleach 231 DE by the tithe-reeves of Cathair mhòr. Known for the walled tithe-granaries.

A walled town on a bend of the road below Cathair mhòr, raised to store and guard the tithe-grain of the Doire mhin country. Its walls were strengthened when the human administration raised the tithe, and the chroniclers note that the grain was guarded but not shared. It keeps the faith of the Dark Unicorn and serves Cill fhada and Muileann ruadh as their market.

  • 11 an Gearran 1853 DE — The Green Death at Baile chrom

Cathair mhòr

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 6,637

Founded 28 an Cèitean 852 BDE by the lords of Doire mhin. Known for the citadel on the capital's north road.

A hill-city with a citadel close to the capital, raised by lords of the Doire mhin country who held the roads north of Cathair dhearg. It has always been a garrison town and was one of the strongholds from which the war before the Severance was fought. It follows the Dark Unicorn and draws on the tithe-granaries of Baile chrom and the great village of Doire mhin. It is not the Cathair mhòr of the third regiment, which lies further east.

Cnoc chiar

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,716

Founded 10 an t-Samhain 1564 DE by herders of Doire mhin. Known for hill pastures of Doire mhin.

A small dusky hill between Doire mhin and Muileann ruadh, pastured by herders of the great village. It follows the Dark Unicorn.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,411

Founded 31 an Cèitean 4 DE by farmers of Doire mhin. Known for hill farms by Muileann ghlas field.

Cnoc ìseal of Doire mhin is a small town of hill farms east of the capital, founded in the long quiet centuries. The field of Muileann ghlas, where An Cogadh Fada ended, lies just to the west, and the town's barns sheltered the wounded after the battle. It keeps the capital's faith.

Doire mhin

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 33,558

Founded 10 an t-Ògmhios 1629 BDE by the oak-keepers of the capital's north. Known for the great grove-village of the north road.

A smooth-barked oak grove north of the capital, grown into one of the largest settlements on the island while keeping its village name and customs. It is the seat of Siorrachd Doire mhin and follows the Dark Unicorn. Its people farm for Cathair mhòr and send much of their grain to the tithe-granaries at Baile chrom.

  • 18 an Dàmhair 362 BDE — The bridge at Doire mhin
  • 24 an t-Sultain 516 DE — The burning of Doire mhin
  • 31 an Dùbhlachd 1800 DE — The last count at Doire mhin

Siorrachd Doire shean

Doire shean

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 35,064

Founded 14 an Lùnastal 1810 BDE by the tavern-keepers of the south-west. Known for Am Buabhall Fortanach and jugged buffalo.

An old oak grove in the south-west, grown into one of the largest villages on the island and the seat of Siorrachd Doire shean. At its heart is Am Buabhall Fortanach, the most famous tavern on the old roads, which serves jugged buffalo and has stood since the Holy Age. It is a harbour as well, and follows the Madadh-allaidh faith.

  • 11 an Giblean 6896 BDE — The first pots at Doire shean
  • 5 an Lùnastal 595 DE — The oyster beds of Doire shean
  • 30 an Lùnastal 1921 DE — The harbour of Doire shean
  • 24 an t-Ògmhios 1959 DE — Doire shean's harbour

Àth gharbh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 2,556

Founded 28 an t-Sultain 1144 BDE by drovers of the western road. Known for the First Fleet's walled ford town.

Àth gharbh, the rough ford, is a walled town of the south-west, a short walk from Doire shean and its great roadside tavern, Am Buabhall Fortanach. That tavern fortified with the others of the old mining circuit before the war of the Severance. Since An Cogadh Fada, A' chiad chabhlach has been stationed here and carries the town's name.

  • 20 an Cèitean 2020 DE — A' chiad chabhlach raised

Siorrachd Dùn chrom

Baile chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,068

Founded 5 am Màrt 643 DE by herders from Dùn chrom. Known for Dùn chrom's stockyards.

The lesser of the two Baile chroms in the central midlands, this one lies under the citadel of Dùn chrom and grew as its stockyard. The fighting at Muileann ghlas in the last year of the Long War passed close enough that the town housed wounded for a season. It keeps the faith of the Dark Unicorn.

Cnoc leathan

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,626

Founded 12 an Dàmhair 1150 DE by Ròdaich herders of Dùn chrom. Known for lodgings and horse-lines for Fèill Muileann òg.

A modest town on the broad hill beside Muileann òg, whose people live for most of the year on herding and for one season on the fair. Since Fèill Muileann òg became the island's greatest gathering, Cnoc leathan has lodged the traders the fair town cannot hold and stabled their animals. It stood near the lines at Muileann ghlas and was emptied for the battle.

Dùn chrom

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 21,065

Founded 27 an t-Sultain 2712 BDE by the lords of the bent hill. Known for the citadel above Muileann ghlas.

A fortified city on a crooked hill in the midlands, seat of Siorrachd Dùn chrom, with a citadel that commands the roads south of the capital. The last battle of the Long War, at Muileann ghlas, was fought within sight of its citadel, and the crown's commanders used its citadel as their headquarters. It follows the Dark Unicorn and is served by the stockyard town of Baile chrom and the ford at Àth mhin.

  • 21 an Lùnastal 393 BDE — The bridge at Dùn chrom
  • 13 an t-Samhain 1810 DE — Rope for the winding-gear
  • 26 am Màrt 1919 DE — Barracks at Dùn chrom
