Muileann ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 4,877

Founded 16 an t-Samhain 2251 BDE by Ròdaich millers of Dùn chrom. Known for the last battle of the Long War.

The grey mill is an old grain town near the fair at Muileann òg and within a day of the capital. It is remembered above all for the Battle of Muileann ghlas, the second and final major battle of An Cogadh Fada, fought on its fields, in which the Tuathaich holdouts were broken. The battlefield, Àraich Muileann ghlas, lies just north-west of the town.

  • 19 an t-Iuchar 1235 DE — The battle of Muileann ghlas
  • 6 an Dùbhlachd 2021 DE — The camp by Muileann ghlas

Muileann òg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,667

Founded 10 am Faoilleach 1950 DE by millers of the restored kingdom. Known for Fèill Muileann òg, the great fair.

Muileann òg, the young mill, was built in the first years of the restored kingdom. Its annual fair, Fèill Muileann òg, became the island's largest gathering. The field of Muileann ghlas, where An Cogadh Fada ended, lies close by.

  • 13 an Giblean 2000 BDE — The War of the Roads begins at Muileann òg
  • 20 an Giblean 1910 DE — The old market at Muileann òg

Àth dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 5,063

Founded 1 an t-Sultain 738 DE by Ròdaich ferrymen of Dùn chrom. Known for the black ford and its walls.

The black ford takes its name from the dark water over the crossing. Walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the crossing carried much of the capital's traffic eastward. The Battle of Muileann ghlas, the last of An Cogadh Fada, was fought within sight of its walls.

Àth mhin

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,630

Founded 7 an t-Ògmhios 1025 DE by wardens of the Dùn chrom crossings. Known for the smooth ford and its citadel.

A walled town with a citadel at the smooth ford, one of a chain of crossings east of the capital. It was a quartering place for soldiers in the Age of Strangers and again in the Long War, when it held the state's stores for the campaign that ended at Muileann ghlas. Its people are mostly carters and stable-keepers.

Siorrachd Dùn dhearg

Cill bhàn

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,569

Founded 20 am Màrt 2723 BDE by keepers of the ancestor rite. Known for white cell of the ancestor rite.

Cill bhàn, the white cell, is a village of the ancestor rite in the east, founded in the Holy Age. It lies near the hot springs and the silver workings of the vein country. It has kept its shrine through every age and every change of master.

Cnoc ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,914

Founded 21 an Dùbhlachd 655 DE by quarriers for Dùn dhearg. Known for grey stone for Dùn dhearg.

Cnoc ghlas is the grey hill whose stone built much of Dùn dhearg. It is a quarry town, dependent on the city. Its quarrymen keep the old folk rites of the ancestors and will not open a new face without them.

  • 22 an Dàmhair 2972 BDE — The weather-cairns of Cnoc ghlas
  • 13 an Giblean 527 BDE — The late snow on the high passes

Dùn dhearg

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 25,678

Founded 27 an Giblean 2689 BDE by a custodian house of the eastern hills. Known for red hill-fort city of the east.

Dùn dhearg is the red hill-fort city of the east and the seat of its province, a city of more than twenty-five thousand. The mills of Muileann dhomhain grind its bread and the quarries of Cnoc ghlas built its houses. It keeps the folk tradition of the ancestors, and its old fort is the site of the province's ancestor feasts.

Muileann gheal

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 12,710

Founded 7 an Dàmhair 1043 DE by white-stone millers. Known for flour for Dùn dhearg.

A white stone mill in the south-east that grinds for the city of Dùn dhearg. It keeps the old spirits and is a large mill-town with a guild of millers older than the city's walls.

  • 26 an Lùnastal 1400 DE — The grey glaze of Muileann gheal
  • 30 an Dùbhlachd 1470 DE — The grey glaze lost

Tobar ìseal

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,174

Founded 26 am Faoilleach 469 DE by well-keepers of Dùn dhearg. Known for the well that waters Dùn dhearg.

A low well-village in the east that waters the city of Dùn dhearg in dry seasons. It keeps the old spirits, and its well-keepers still bless the water before it is carted up the hill.

Àth àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,029

Founded 19 am Màrt 1105 BDE by the ford-keepers of Dùn dhearg. Known for the pebble-cairn at the ford-stone.

An ancient ford in the east, between the mill town of Muileann leathan and Seann Mhorn on the coast. It keeps the old spirits and a ford-stone where travellers leave a pebble, and it has been a small crossing town since the Holy Age.

Siorrachd Dùn thais

Baile leathan

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 10,418

Founded 21 am Faoilleach 906 BDE by Ròdaich scribes of Dùn thais. Known for copyists and binders for the library.

Baile leathan is one of the towns nearest Leabharlann Muileann chaol, and many of its people are copyists, binders and parchment-makers for the library. It was a market town of the broad valley long before the library was founded, and it grew quickly after. It keeps the Fèidh habit of reading aloud in the evenings.

Dùn thais

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 34,173

Founded 20 am Màrt 2469 BDE by custodians of the north-eastern hills. Known for great hill city near the Library.

Dùn thais of the north-east is a great hill city with a citadel and a temple, the chief place of its province. It lies close to Leabharlann Muileann chaol, and many of the Library's clerks and copyists live in it. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Muileann àrsaidh

fort · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,831

Founded 19 am Faoilleach 1329 BDE by a custodian house of Dùn thais. Known for fortified ancient mill.

Muileann àrsaidh is an ancient mill fortified with a citadel, a short way from Muileann chaol. The citadel guarded the road to the ore in the Holy Age and now guards the road to the library. It is a small place of fewer than two thousand.

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,837

Founded 12 an Lùnastal 1362 DE by carters of Dùn thais. Known for narrow ford on the Dùn thais road.

A small town at a narrow ford on the Dùn thais road, living on the carts that pass through it. Since the library was founded at Muileann chaol many of its young people have gone to work there as porters and copyists. It has never been walled or fought over.

Àth dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 11,388

Founded 6 an t-Ògmhios 1069 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of Dùn thais. Known for deep ford below Muileann chaol.

The deep ford lies below Muileann chaol, and every reader bound for the library crosses it. It is a town of eleven thousand. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Siorrachd Dùn ìseal

Baile naomh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,008

Founded 1 an Gearran 2680 BDE by custodians of the holy wells. Known for holy wells of the vein country.

Baile naomh, the holy town, grew around wells in the vein country that the Holy Age custodians held sacred. The hot springs of Muileann ruadh lie to the west and the silver workings of Muileann chiar to the north-west. It is a small town of shrines and lodging houses, keeping the ancestor rite.

Cill dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,922

Founded 6 am Màrt 349 BDE by priests of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh for the silver-miners. Known for miners' chapel by the silver seam.

A church village a short way from the silver seam at Muileann chiar, whose chapel has served the silver-miners since the seam was first worked. In the Age of Strangers its priests kept a record of the miners killed underground, one of the few such records to survive. It is not the Cill dhìreach of the central country.

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,625

Founded 5 an t-Sultain 2222 BDE by shepherds of the eastern hills. Known for cairn hill and its shepherds.

Cnoc àrsaidh of Dùn ìseal is a hill town crowned by old cairns, above Baile naomh. It has been a shepherding place since the Holy Age. Its people keep the ancestor rite and tend the cairns at the turning of the seasons.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 9,720

Founded 7 an t-Iuchar 1859 DE by silver miners of Muileann chiar. Known for the citadel over the silver seam.

A young hill-town with a citadel beside the silver mine of Muileann chiar, raised when the Ròdaich held the silver seam against the human claims. The citadel was built to guard the seam, and the town grew as the silver town expanded. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Dùn ìseal

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 22,571

Founded 10 an Dàmhair 2997 BDE by the custodian house of Dùn ìseal. Known for the great temple of the old spirits.

A low fort-city in the east with walls, a citadel and a temple, the seat of Siorrachd Dùn ìseal. Its temple is the chief shrine of the old spirits in the eastern hills, where the Ròdaich custodians kept the ancestors' rites through every age. It stands between the silver seam of Muileann chiar and the hot springs of Muileann ruadh, and it was held by the Ròdaich in the dispute over the silver.

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,771

Founded 10 an Lùnastal 2992 BDE by Ròdaich custodians who found the silver seam. Known for the island's silver seam.

Muileann chiar was founded when a silver seam was found near, but distinct from, the great vein, the island's first confirmed resource that was not obsidian. In the Age of Strangers human interests tried to claim the silver as well, and the Ròdaich kept it; the town grew alongside the obsidian workings as demand for both rose. It is smaller now than in its great years.

Muileann dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 8,100

Founded 23 am Màrt 362 BDE by Ròdaich millers of Dùn ìseal. Known for its deep-cut mill-race.

The deep mill takes its name from a mill-race cut far down into the rock to reach a steady flow. It grinds for Dùn dhearg and the villages around it and has done so since the Holy Age. The folk tradition of the ancestors holds here, and each new millstone is blessed at the hearth before it is set.

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,558

Founded 11 an t-Ògmhios 2666 BDE by keepers of the hot springs. Known for the hot springs of Muileann ruadh.

A red walled mill town beside Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh, the hot springs whose warm water drives its wheel through winter. The springs were held sacred by the old spirits, and the town walled them against claims from the human administration. It is a place for the sick and the old to bathe.

  • 1 an Dùbhlachd 2463 BDE — The bath-house at Muileann ruadh

Siorrachd Inis bheag

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 9,900

Founded 7 an Dàmhair 166 DE by farmers from Inis bheag. Known for stony fields that feed Inis bheag.

Rough ground behind the port of Inis bheag, broken to the plough in the long centuries after the Sundering fleet had gone. It feeds the harbour and the fishing fleet, and it has grown larger than many towns while keeping the name and customs of a village. The Feallsanachd an Fhèidh has a strong following among its farmers, who are said to argue philosophy over the furrow.

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,679

Founded 3 am Faoilleach 1065 DE by farmers of Muileann chaol. Known for stony fields for the old mill.

A rough field village beside the older Muileann chaol, breaking stony ground for the mill. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and shares its name with two other Achadh gharbhs of the east, which the library's clerks tell apart only by their shires.

Inis bheag

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 21,240

Founded 25 an t-Iuchar 2523 BDE by boat-builders of the north-east. Known for boatyards of the small isle.

Inis bheag is an island harbour of the north-east and the seat of its province. Its boatyards have built fishing craft for the coast since the Holy Age. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and shares its waters with Ros fhionn of the old bridge.

  • 22 an t-Ògmhios 1138 BDE — Inis bheag's school of letters
  • 29 an Dàmhair 1832 DE — Ore through Inis bheag
  • 2 an Giblean 1948 DE — The chest from Inis bheag

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,708

Founded 15 an Giblean 1527 DE by red-stone millers. Known for red mill beside Muileann fhada.

A red mill town beside Muileann fhada in the north-east, the two together grinding for Doire chiar. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Ros fhionn

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,812

Founded 29 an Lùnastal 2958 BDE by custodians of the river crossing. Known for Drochaid Ros fhionn, the old bridge.

Ros fhionn of Inis bheag is a walled city on a headland, founded in the Holy Age where the first bridges crossed the river. Drochaid Ros fhionn, the old crossing, is still standing but has seen little traffic since the local trade dried up. Its temple is a hall of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

  • 3 am Màrt 315 DE — Salt pans at Ros fhionn
  • 9 an Lùnastal 920 DE — The salt fair at Ros fhionn
  • 29 an t-Ògmhios 1120 DE — The silting of Ros fhionn

Tobar òg

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 6,303

Founded 21 an t-Iuchar 1356 DE by well-diggers of Inis bheag. Known for the young well behind Inis bheag.

A young well village in the north-east, dug to water the fields behind Inis bheag when those fields were first broken. It has grown into a sizeable village and follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Siorrachd Inis bhàn

Doire ruadh

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 4,987

Founded 24 an Cèitean 1452 DE by hawk-keepers of the north. Known for red oak grove and hawk-keepers.

Doire ruadh is a village of red oaks inland of the Hawk bay, founded in the long quiet centuries by families who kept hawks for the rite of Mòd. Its birds are still flown at the rite's gatherings in Cnoc bheag. Since the Severance it has lain close to the Tuathaich border and has seen more soldiers than it wishes.

Inis bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 37,990

Founded 16 an Giblean 2587 BDE by Ròdaich seafarers of the white island. Known for white-island harbour and Hawk shrines.

Inis bhàn is the great harbour of the north-west Ròdaich coast and the seat of its province, a port of nearly forty thousand. It is a town of the Hawk, and its shrines face the sea. The Green Death, A' Phlàigh Uaine, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It is one of several harbours that claim the dock from which the ships of the Sundering set out, a claim the others dispute and no roll can settle.

Siorrachd Inis chrom

Baile shean

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 1,839

Founded 18 an t-Iuchar 1814 BDE by Ròdaich followers of the Direwolf. Known for old walled town of the Direwolf.

An old walled town of Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh, beside the fort of Muileann bheag. Its walls are older than the fort, and for most of its history it was the stronger of the two. It is small now, and lives on the fort's custom.

Cnoc shean

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 1,784

Founded 19 an Dùbhlachd 2797 BDE by the lords of the old hill. Known for the old hill citadel.

A small old hill-town with a citadel in the west, commanding the road between Baile Mòr fhionn and the harbours of the south-west. It follows the Madadh-allaidh faith and has kept a garrison since the war before the Severance.

Inis chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 31,994

Founded 25 an Giblean 1398 BDE by Direwolf sailors of the south-west. Known for bent isle harbour and Direwolf sailors.

Inis chrom is a large walled harbour on a bent island of the south-west. It has been a port since the Holy Age and its sailors keep the Direwolf's faith. It lies close to Am Buabhall Fortanach and Àth gharbh.

Siorrachd Inis mhin

Baile ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 11,186

Founded 9 an t-Iuchar 2042 BDE by Ròdaich farmers of the red ground. Known for a shared market on the border.

A red town in the north-west that stayed Ròdaich when the Tuathaich homeland was fixed around it, and the line of the border wall that was proposed and never built would have run past its gate. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich, and its market is used by Tuathaich from Baile fhionn and Ròdaich from Àth uaine alike.

Inis mhin

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 12,779

Founded 17 an Gearran 1152 DE by Ròdaich harbour-folk; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for Tuathaich port where the First Canoe is told.

Inis mhin was a Ròdaich island harbour of the long quiet centuries, and its citadel was raised in the Age of Strangers by human administrators guarding the northern landing. After the Severance it passed wholly to the Tuathaich, and it is now one of their chief ports. It is among the coastal towns where the First Canoe fragment is still told, and the Tuathaich folk tradition holds here rather than the Yellow Scorpion faith of its neighbours.

  • 29 an Cèitean 1874 DE — Inis mhin eats its seed

Siorrachd Inis mhòr

Cnoc naomh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 7,832

Founded 29 an Cèitean 1857 BDE by a custodian house of Inis mhòr. Known for citadel on the holy hill.

The holy hill carried a shrine before it carried a citadel; the citadel was added to guard Inis mhòr from the landward side. The shrine still stands inside the walls. The fourth regiment from Caol bheag drills on the plain below it.

Inis mhòr

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 23,990

Founded 31 an Lùnastal 2037 BDE by net-fishers of the north-eastern coast. Known for north-eastern fishing fleet and debating halls.

Inis mhòr of the north-east is the great island harbour of its province, a fishing town of the Holy Age that became a city under the Age of Strangers' trade. Its people follow Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, and the town's debating halls were among the first to reopen at the school's revival. It shares the coastal trade with Ceann bheag and the walled town of Baile Mòr dhìreach inland.

Siorrachd Inis thais

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 3,014

Founded 14 an t-Iuchar 1353 DE by Scorpion-faith traders of the west. Known for straight-street harbour of the Scorpion faith.

Baile dhìreach, the straight town, is a harbour on the west coast built around one long street to the quay. It was founded in the long quiet centuries by traders of the Yellow Scorpion faith, among Direwolf neighbours. The two faiths have shared its market without any trouble the rolls think worth noting.

Caol fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 11,425

Founded 13 an t-Iuchar 598 DE by fishers of the wild strait. Known for fishing the wild strait.

Caol fhiadhaich is a harbour on a rough strait of the west coast, within the province of Inis thais. It was founded in the long quiet centuries by fishers who braved waters the older harbours avoided. Its people keep the Direwolf's faith.

Inis thais

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 34,904

Founded 21 an Lùnastal 2740 BDE by priests of the Direwolf. Known for the Direwolf's temple and pilgrims.

Inis thais is a walled temple city of the south-west and the seat of its province. Its temple of Clach, the Resplendent Direwolf, is the chief shrine of that faith, and pilgrims come to it from Caol leathan and the whole western coast. It has been a holy city since the Holy Age.

Àth ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 16,521

Founded 31 am Faoilleach 1586 BDE by Ròdaich traders of Inis thais. Known for grey ford market of the west.

Àth ghlas is a large ford-market of the west, near Seann Warr. It follows the Yellow Scorpion. It is one of three places named Àth ghlas and the largest.

Siorrachd Muileann bheag

Baile bheag

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,897

Founded 3 an t-Samhain 1007 DE by toll-keepers of Muileann bheag. Known for a walled town of tolls.

A small town on the road to Muileann bheag, walled to collect tolls rather than to keep enemies out. It still collects them, and has outlasted every attempt to abolish the right. It is one of several places named Baile bheag.

Cill àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 11,868

Founded 25 an t-Sultain 75 BDE by priests of the old spirits. Known for a philosophers' house on an old shrine.

An ancient church-site village in the north-east, older than the Feallsanachd an Fhèidh that now holds it. The founding shrine is said to have been of the old spirits, and its foundations lie under the present meeting-house. It is a large village supplying Muileann bheag.

Doire uaine

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,576

Founded 16 an Lùnastal 1261 BDE by the grove-keepers of the old spirits. Known for oak for Muileann bheag.

A green oak grove in the north-east, not the Doire uaine of the Hollow Man's hills, a confusion the library records note with some weariness. It keeps the old spirits and cuts its oak for Muileann bheag.

Dùn dhubh

city · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,841

Founded 26 an Cèitean 1817 BDE by a custodian house of Muileann bheag. Known for black fort over the coast road.

Dùn dhubh is a walled hill fort of dark stone, ranked a city though it holds under three thousand people. It commands the coast road above Muileann bheag and the harbour of Seann Toll. Its walls were raised in the Holy Age and repaired in every age after.

Muileann bheag

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 11,908

Founded 23 an Giblean 1210 BDE by grain-millers of the north-east. Known for flour for the north-east harbours.

A small mill that grew into a sizable town and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann bheag. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and grinds for the harbour at Ros chiar. It shares its name with three others on the island, including the Tuathaich lighthouse town.

  • 27 am Màrt 1922 DE — Muileann bheag in the north-east

Ros chiar

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,817

Founded 19 an Lùnastal 1449 DE by fishers of Muileann bheag. Known for the flour harbour of Muileann bheag.

A dusky headland harbour village on the north-east coast that ships the flour of Muileann bheag. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and competes with Seann Toll for the coast trade.

Seann Tarr

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,806

Founded 30 an Cèitean 12,550 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for north-eastern ancestor shrine.

Seann Tarr is a Seann-Dhaoine site on the north-eastern coast, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age, and its temple is one of the oldest houses of the ancestor rite still in use. A citadel was raised over the harbour in the Age of Sundering. It is small for a city, but the shrine draws the whole north-east at the great feasts.

Seann Toll

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,603

Founded 19 an Giblean 10,605 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for cleft-rock harbour of the Old Ones.

Seann Toll is a harbour in a cleft of the rock, and its lowest quay is cut in a manner the Ròdaich did not use; it is held to be the work of the Seann-Dhaoine, and nothing more is known of it. The Ròdaich settled it in the Holy Age as the nearest harbour for Dùn dhubh and Muileann bheag. It is a small port town of fishers and lightermen.

Àth gheal

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 9,316

Founded 20 an t-Ògmhios 982 DE by farmers of Muileann bheag. Known for white ford near Seann Tarr.

Àth gheal of Muileann bheag is a ford town near Seann Tarr, founded in the long quiet centuries. It keeps the ancestor rite. At the great feasts it lodges the pilgrims bound for the shrine at Seann Tarr.

Siorrachd Muileann bhàn

Cnoc mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 8,008

Founded 31 an Cèitean 1606 DE by hill-lords of Muileann bhàn. Known for hill-farms above Seann Warr.

A great hill in the south, above the harbour of Seann Warr and the large mill town of Muileann bhàn. It keeps the old spirits, and its hill-farms supply both.

Doire dhearg

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,668

Founded 21 an t-Iuchar 1811 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Known for red spoil-heaps of the camp years.

Doire dhearg began as a mining camp in the Age of Strangers, when the interior was first worked by the ton. Its red spoil-heaps are still visible above the village. Many of its people left when the workings moved on, and the village that remains keeps the ancestor rite.

Muileann bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 34,517

Founded 8 am Màrt 272 DE by a custodian house of the ore road. Known for white mills and citadel of the ore road.

Muileann bhàn is a town of thirty-four thousand with a citadel, the seat of its province, standing where the ore road from the eastern diggings met the mills. In the Age of Strangers its citadel held the human administration's weighing-house and its guards. The mills have turned to grain since the Severance, and the folk tradition of the ancestors, never lost here, has returned to the square.

Doire uaine

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,599

Founded 13 an Gearran 120 BDE by herders of the Doire uaine hills. Known for the Hollow Man of the hills.

Doire uaine is a small village in the hills where inscriptions describe the Hollow Man, something that walked without breathing and attacked anyone who lit a fire in its sight. The village was founded in the Holy Age. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

  • 8 an Cèitean 9714 BDE — Signs cut in the Doire uaine hills
  • 5 an t-Iuchar 9600 BDE — The hill fires go under the ground

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 15,578

Founded 23 an t-Iuchar 326 DE by ore-crushers of the eastern diggings. Known for ore mills of the eastern district.

Muileann chiar, seat of the province of the same name, began as an ore-crushing mill for the diggings in the hills east of the capital. It grew large in the Age of Strangers, when the district was worked by the ton, and lost its trade when Scàineadh Cill ghlas, a short way west, closed the district for a generation. It is not the silver town of the same name further east, and the two are often confused in the older records.

Muileann gheal

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 688

Founded 20 an Lùnastal 1841 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Known for walled mill-camp under Doire uaine.

Muileann gheal was a walled mill-camp under the Doire uaine hills, built in the Age of Strangers to crush ore from the eastern diggings. It is small, fewer than seven hundred people. The warm springs of Muileann ruadh lie a short walk away, and the camp's miners bathed there.

  • 15 an Dùbhlachd 526 BDE — The granaries opened

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,790

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 1845 DE by miners of the central diggings. Known for miners' town of the Rending.

A narrow ford-town in the central hills, grown in the Age of Strangers around the camp-roads to the diggings near Cill ghlas. The Rending, Scàineadh Cill ghlas, killed miners of this town in the collapse, and the people here still use scàinte of a man who is shaken. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Àth dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 3,056

Founded 20 an Giblean 1829 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Known for straight ford of the ore carts.

Àth dhìreach was a ford where the ore carts crossed in the Age of Strangers. It is a town of three thousand in the eastern mining district. Its ford is paved with spoil from the diggings.

  • 18 an Dàmhair 525 BDE — Àth dhìreach after the poor season

Founded 10 an t-Ògmhios 2727 BDE by farmers of Muileann chrom. Known for deep-field granaries of the camps.

Achadh dhomhain of Muileann chrom is a large farming village in deep fields, founded in the Holy Age. Its granaries fed the mining camps in the Age of Strangers and were requisitioned in the war of the Severance. It keeps the capital's faith.

Baile dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,666

Founded 28 an Lùnastal 67 DE by priest-farmers of Cnoc bhàn. Known for tithe-fields of the Cnoc bhàn priests.

A small town in a deep valley, farming for the priests of the Dark Unicorn at Cnoc bhàn. It has no walls and little history beyond the tithe-rolls of the priests' house, which record its harvests without a gap from the Sundering to the present.

Ceann fhada

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 6,509

Founded 27 an Cèitean 1320 DE by Ròdaich river pilots. Known for long quay and river pilots.

A long spit of land made Ceann fhada a landing for river craft, and its pilots have guided boats on the Abhainn uaine for centuries. It is the old rival of Inis ìseal, a short way downstream, and the two quays have quarrelled over tolls in every age the rolls cover. It prospered in the Age of Strangers carrying ore-cart loads by water and has held its trade since by carrying grain.

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,965

Founded 17 am Màrt 449 DE by hunters of the Muileann chrom country. Known for a walled hill by the river road.

A wild walled hill in the middle country, near the canoe-landing of Cidhe Beag on Abhainn uaine. Its walls were raised in the troubled years when the river road carried ore. It follows the Dark Unicorn and trades with Muileann chrom and Inis ìseal.

Cuan dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 3,135

Founded 12 an Dàmhair 1750 DE by fishers of the eastern gulf. Known for red-cliffed gulf harbour and ferries.

Cuan dhearg is one of the ring of small harbours on the gulf below Cathair mhòr, named for the red cliffs over its anchorage. It lives on the fish and the short ferry runs between the gulf towns, and has never been walled. It is not the southern Cuan dhearg that Tonn Mhòr destroyed; the chroniclers have confused the two more than once.

Doire mhòr

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,738

Founded 24 an Giblean 1858 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Known for pit-props from a vanished oak wood.

Doire mhòr was cut out of a great oak wood in the Age of Strangers, when the workings east of the capital needed pit-props faster than any Holy Age forester would have felled them. The wood is gone and the village farms the clearing.

  • 20 an Cèitean 1808 DE — Doire mhòr's water taken

Inis ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 10,887

Founded 12 an Giblean 1071 DE by Ròdaich river boatmen. Known for river-island port on the Abhainn uaine.

Inis ìseal is a river port on a low island in the Abhainn uaine, a short way from the landing at Cidhe Beag. It is the rival of Ceann fhada a short way upstream, and the two have disputed tolls in every age. It prospered in the Age of Strangers carrying ore and has kept its trade by carrying grain.

Muileann chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 18,448

Founded 11 an Gearran 2994 BDE by Ròdaich millers on the river bend. Known for the great mill on the river bend.

The mill on the bend of the river gave its name to the town and then to the province, of which it is the seat and the largest place. It ground grain for the whole central country and, in the Age of Strangers, for the camps east of it as well. It is a busy, unwalled town that has never needed walls, standing between Cathair mhòr and Ceann leathan on the road that joins them.

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,843

Founded 26 an Gearran 758 DE by millers of Muileann chrom. Known for walled red mill.

A walled mill town on the road north of Muileann chrom, one of three places named Muileann dhearg. It was walled in the Age of Strangers to protect its stores. It follows the capital's faith.

Seann Toll

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 8,455

Founded 8 an Gearran 12,423 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the rock-hollow harbour and Còmhrag crowds.

A Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the inner coast of the midlands, called Seann Toll by the Ròdaich for the hollow in the rock where its boats lie. It is walled and follows the Dark Unicorn, and it stands a short way west of Cill ghlas, where the Rending opened. It lies close to Ceann leathan, where the Còmhrag is fought each year, and fighters from the tournament fill its taverns.

Àth ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,979

Founded 7 an t-Iuchar 285 DE by Ròdaich ferrymen of Muileann chrom. Known for the low ford and its ferry.

The low ford floods each wet season, and for part of every year the crossing is made by ferry. The town is small and has always been poor. It sends its surplus down to the quays at Inis ìseal and Ceann fhada.

Siorrachd Muileann dhearg

Baile thais

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 13,140

Founded 5 an t-Ògmhios 913 BDE by river-boatmen of the Abhainn uaine. Known for Cidhe Beag landing on the Abhainn uaine.

Baile thais stands where the Abhainn uaine reaches the gulf, and the river landing of Cidhe Beag lies just upstream. Boats have been launched here since the Holy Age to carry goods inland and ore down. It is a busy, unwalled town of boatmen and warehouses.

Cill fhada

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,783

Founded 17 an Dùbhlachd 57 DE by priests of the Dark Unicorn. Known for the long chapel of the Dark Unicorn.

A church-site village strung along a long ridge near Baile chrom, whose chapel of the Dark Unicorn is the longest building in the district. It farms for the market at Baile chrom and sends its grain to the tithe-granaries there.

Cill ghlas

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,711

Founded 4 am Faoilleach 1185 BDE by a house of the Feallsanachd. Known for Scàineadh Cill ghlas, the Rending.

Cill ghlas, the grey cell, was a quiet village of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh in the hills east of the capital until the Age of Strangers pushed the workings under it. Late in that age a routine excavation tore open a fault around it, killing dozens and closing the working; the Rending gave the island the word 'scàinte'. The village was rebuilt on the far side of the crack, and its people still mark the day of the dead.

Cnoc chaol

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 655

Founded 22 an Cèitean 1850 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Known for a spent camp on the narrow hill.

Cnoc chaol was a mining camp on the narrow hill, worked by the ton in the Age of Strangers. It emptied after Scàineadh Cill ghlas closed the district and never recovered. Fewer than seven hundred people live there now, among the spoil heaps.

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 22,453

Founded 2 an t-Ògmhios 1798 BDE by Ròdaich millers of the central country. Known for stamping mills turned to grain.

The red mill is the seat of its province and one of the largest towns of the centre, standing between Seann Chwen and Cnoc ghorm. Its mills stamped ore in the Age of Strangers and turned back to grain after the Severance. It is a town of the capital's faith, busy and unwalled.

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 14,052

Founded 30 an t-Sultain 38 BDE by ore-millers of the central diggings. Known for red mill beside Cill ghlas.

Muileann dhearg, seat of its province, is a mill town a short way from Cill ghlas. Scàineadh Cill ghlas tore open the hills nearby and killed dozens, and the town's mills stood idle for a generation after. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Siorrachd Muileann dhomhain

Achadh chaol

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,691

Founded 23 am Faoilleach 527 DE by Ròdaich farmers of Muileann dhomhain. Known for narrow fields feeding the diggings.

A village of narrow fields that has fed the eastern mining district since the district was opened. Scàineadh Cill ghlas, the Rending, struck it when the fault tore open, and the diggings it fed were closed after. It still sends its grain to the mills around it.

  • 5 an Dùbhlachd 1916 DE — Achadh chaol raised by the displaced

Achadh ìseal

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,104

Founded 27 an t-Sultain 1145 DE by farmers from Muileann dhomhain. Known for harvests for the southern mills.

A low field village in the south-east, farming for the mill town of Muileann dhomhain and the port of Ceann chaol. It keeps the old spirits and has no history the chroniclers found worth writing beyond its harvests.

Caol naomh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh nan Ròdach · pop. 2,711

Founded 17 an Giblean 442 DE by priests of the Obsidian Rite. Known for pilgrim landing of the Obsidian Rite.

A holy strait-harbour near the ruins of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, where the orthodox Obsidian Rite built a landing for pilgrims coming to the mountain. It is one of the few towns where Creideamh nan Ròdach holds the majority, and its priests were among those who formalized the Rite in the first years of the new kingdom. It is a small town and quiet outside the pilgrim season.

Ceann chaol

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 9,536

Founded 23 an Giblean 946 DE by Ròdaich seafarers of the narrow point. Known for narrow-point harbour, rival of Ceann mhin.

Ceann chaol is a port city on the narrow point, and the old rival of Ceann mhin along the same shore. Its ships carry the flour of Muileann dhomhain and the grain of the eastern plain. The two harbours have disputed fishing grounds in every age, and the disputes are recorded at length.

  • 4 am Màrt 2848 BDE — The carriers' path to Ceann chaol
  • 20 an t-Samhain 1882 DE — The deep quay at Ceann chaol

Muileann dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 16,277

Founded 8 an t-Iuchar 1252 BDE by the millers of the deep race. Known for the grain-exchange of the south-east.

A mill on a deep, fast race in the central country and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann dhomhain. It was a milling town for centuries and grew rich carrying grain to the mining settlements in the Age of Strangers, when the camps could no longer feed themselves. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich, and its grain-exchange still sets the price of flour for the south-east.

  • 21 an Lùnastal 127 BDE — Muileann dhomhain's mill
  • 5 an Dùbhlachd 1896 DE — The strikebreakers of Muileann dhomhain

Muileann dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 20,506

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 1582 BDE by Ròdaich millers of the south-east. Known for deep mill-pools feeding Ceann chaol's ships.

Muileann dhomhain, seat of its province, is a town of twenty thousand built around deep mill-pools fed from the hills. Its flour goes down to the quays of Ceann chaol and out by sea, and the two towns have depended on each other since the Holy Age. It is not the smaller Muileann dhomhain of Dùn ìseal to the north.

  • 29 an Lùnastal 1040 DE — The swallowing cough at Muileann dhomhain
  • 5 an Lùnastal 1065 DE — Muileann dhomhain resettled

Muileann uaine

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh nan Ròdach · pop. 1,705

Founded 8 am Màrt 1827 DE by a human milling concern with Ròdaich labour. Known for ore-crushing mill of the interior workings.

Muileann uaine was built in the Age of Strangers as a crushing mill for ore from the interior workings. It is not the Muileann uaine of the Cnoc bheag country that the Green Death struck, though the two are often confused. It is a small town now and keeps the orthodox Obsidian Rite.

Siorrachd Muileann leathan

Baile fhionn

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 1,628

Founded 31 an Dàmhair 1733 DE by Ròdaich farmers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for trade across the line with Baile ruadh.

A small fair town in the north-west, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It follows Creideamh nan Tuathach and trades across the line with the Ròdaich town of Baile ruadh.

Baile leathan

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 1,609

Founded 21 an t-Iuchar 1802 DE by human settlers from an Tìr Thall. Known for an old strangers' settlement of the north.

Baile leathan was built by human settlers in the Age of Strangers on the northern coast, one of the few places the strangers founded rather than took. After the Severance it became a Tuathaich town. It keeps the Tuathaich folk tradition and its oldest families still count their descent from the Crossing.

Cill chaol

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 1,898

Founded 10 am Màrt 985 BDE by Ròdaich priests; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for a Tuathach shrine in a Ròdaich chapel.

Cill chaol was a narrow Ròdaich chapel village near the northern coast, emptied at the Severance and taken by Tuathaich families. They turned its chapel to the worship of Donn, an Sìorraidh, under Creideamh nan Tuathach, and the Ròdaich carvings on its doorposts were left in place beside theirs. It is a small place near the lighthouse of Muileann bheag.

Cnoc leathan

fort · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 2,319

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 1793 DE by the human administration, as a coast fort. Known for Tuathaich-held fort on the north coast.

Cnoc leathan was built by the human administration as a fort on the northern coast road, not far from the lighthouse at Muileann bheag. The Tuathaich have held it since the Severance and keep its citadel manned. Its small garrison follows Creideamh nan Tuathach.

Muileann bheag

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 2,177

Founded 14 an Giblean 1491 DE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for Taigh-solais Muileann bheag.

A small mill town on the north coast beside Taigh-solais Muileann bheag, one of the five lighthouses built in the Age of Strangers. It became Tuathaich at the Severance, and the Tuathaich lighthouse-keepers tended the beacon for the kingdom until it was converted to dubhan. It follows Creideamh nan Tuathach.

  • 13 am Faoilleach 1843 DE — The fishermen of Muileann bheag

Muileann leathan

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 22,366

Founded 24 an Giblean 303 BDE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Tuathaich mill-citadel.

A wide mill on a northern river, walled with a citadel, and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann leathan. It was a Ròdaich town until the Severance, when the Tuathaich took it over as one of the principal towns of their homeland. It is a centre of Creideamh nan Tuathach, and its keep is where the Tuathaich northern coast is governed.

Siorrachd Muileann mhin

Doire bheag

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 693

Founded 4 an t-Samhain 1521 DE by Ròdaich woodcutters of the capital. Known for firewood for the capital.

A small village in an oak copse north-east of Cathair dhearg, which has cut firewood and charcoal for the capital for as long as there are accounts. It has never grown past a few hundred households. Its people follow the capital's faith and take their wood into the city on market days.

Muileann mhin

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 30,105

Founded 20 an t-Iuchar 1541 BDE by millers of the capital shore. Known for the capital's flour mills.

Muileann mhin is a large harbour town east of the capital and the seat of its province. Its flour mills have fed the capital since the Holy Age. It keeps the capital's faith and ships its flour along the shore to Cathair dhearg and Ros dhomhain.

  • 10 an Gearran 1992 DE — The ore-lamp shortage

Siorrachd Muileann naomh

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,961

Founded 3 an Gearran 1036 DE by Ròdaich traders of Muileann naomh. Known for straight-street twin of Cnoc gheal.

A small town of one straight street on the far west, twinned with Cnoc gheal a short walk away. It lies close to the Tuathaich line and trades with the villages beyond it. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

Caol ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh nan Ròdach · pop. 11,899

Founded 22 an t-Iuchar 992 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the red strait. Known for red strait and the orthodox Rite.

Caol ruadh takes its name from the red rock of the strait it watches on the southern coast. It was a quiet fishing town for most of its history, and was among the first to take up the orthodox Obsidian Rite when Creideamh nan Ròdach was formalized. Since An Cogadh Fada its harbour has victualled the garrisons and fleet stationed at Seann Skell close by.

  • 14 an Giblean 5029 BDE — Caol ruadh on the southern strait

Cill gharbh

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,948

Founded 27 an Lùnastal 1073 BDE by Ròdaich priests of the western coast. Known for rough stone chapel of the west.

A village around a rough stone chapel on the far western coast of the Ròdaich country. Its chapel is older than any of its houses, and the Yellow Scorpion was worshipped there before the faiths divided. It is a small village of fewer than two thousand.

Cnoc dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,714

Founded 31 an Lùnastal 605 DE by potters of the west. Known for red-clay potteries of the west.

Cnoc dhearg of Muileann naomh is a small town of the west, founded in the long quiet centuries on a hill of red clay. Its potteries supply jars and tiles to the western harbours, and the Age of Strangers brought it a brief trade in crucibles for the assayers. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith.

Cnoc gheal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,713

Founded 16 am Màrt 745 DE by Ròdaich priests of the Yellow Scorpion. Known for white hill shrine of the Scorpion.

The Ròdaich Cnoc gheal is a white hill with a shrine of the Yellow Scorpion, twinned with Baile dhìreach. A second Cnoc gheal, held by the Tuathaich, lies a short walk north-east over the line. The two villages share a name and a faith and very little else.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 752

Founded 31 am Faoilleach 1931 DE by the restored kingdom, as a border post. Known for border walls facing the Tuathaich.

Cnoc òg, "the young hill", was walled by the restored kingdom soon after the Severance, on the Ròdaich side of the line facing the Tuathaich towns to the north and west. It has never been more than a small town of soldiers' families and carters. In An Cogadh Fada it lay a short march behind the field at Àth leathan, and its walls held the wounded after that first battle.

Muileann naomh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 10,137

Founded 4 an t-Ògmhios 2400 BDE by priests of the Yellow Scorpion. Known for the consecrated mill-wheel.

A holy mill in the west, the seat of Siorrachd Muileann naomh, whose wheel is said to have been consecrated to Cnut. It lies near the Àth leathan battlefield and was taken over by crown regiments in the Long War. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

  • 6 an Dùbhlachd 1868 DE — Muileann naomh buys its way out

Muileann naomh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh nan Ròdach · pop. 12,401

Founded 16 an t-Iuchar 88 DE by priests of the Obsidian Rite. Known for grain blessed by the Rite's priests.

A holy mill in the south, the seat of Siorrachd Muileann naomh, whose priests of the orthodox Rite bless the grain before it is ground. It is one of the few towns of Creideamh nan Ròdach and trades with Caol ruadh and Seann Skell.

Àth chrom

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,343

Founded 3 an t-Iuchar 950 DE by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for Tuathaich drovers at the bent ford.

A drovers' town at the bent ford, Ròdaich until the Severance and Tuathaich since. It lies a short way from the field of Àth leathan, and its people carried the dead from that battle. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

  • 30 an t-Samhain 1929 DE — The columns at Àth chrom

Siorrachd Muileann shean

Cill leathan

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 9,956

Founded 27 am Màrt 1310 BDE by keepers of the north-coast cell. Known for broad cell and its sea citadel.

Cill leathan is a large harbour village of the north coast, founded as a cell in the Holy Age. A citadel was raised over its harbour in the Age of Strangers to guard the human ships that used it. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Cnoc bheag

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 4,848

Founded 8 an Lùnastal 740 DE by farmers of the north coast. Known for north-coast hill farms.

Cnoc bheag of Muileann shean is a small town of hill farms on the north coast, founded in the long quiet centuries. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Its people send their sons to the Feallsanachd teachers at Cill àrsaidh.

Cnoc gheal

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,566

Founded 20 an t-Iuchar 1138 DE by watchmen of the north. Known for white-hill watchtower of the north coast.

Cnoc gheal is a white hill with a small citadel, raised as a watchtower in the long quiet centuries to give warning of ships on the northern coast. Its fire could be seen from Cill leathan and Àth fhionn, and the three kept a common watch. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, and its garrison is now a handful of old soldiers and their families.

Muileann shean

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 19,610

Founded 1 an t-Samhain 2462 BDE by the first millers of the northern river. Known for the oldest mill-wheel in the north.

The old mill of the north, whose wheel the Holy Age king-lists already call ancient, and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann shean. Its walls went up in the Age of Strangers, when it ground grain for the mining camps on contract and was raided for it. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and owns the well-village of Tobar ìseal below it.

  • 10 an Gearran 1844 BDE — Muileann shean on the northern road
  • 25 am Màrt 1150 DE — The millers of Muileann shean
  • 26 an t-Iuchar 1911 DE — The constable post at Muileann shean
  • 19 an Giblean 1988 DE — Muileann shean's school of hewers

Àth fhionn

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 2,707

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 778 DE by fishers of the north coast. Known for fair ford of the north coast.

Àth fhionn of Muileann shean is a ford town of the north coast, founded in the long quiet centuries where the coast road crosses a clear river. It shares the watch-fire of Cnoc gheal and trades with the harbour of Cill leathan. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Siorrachd Muileann àrsaidh

Achadh fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,753

Founded 19 an t-Iuchar 1473 DE by Ròdaich fishers of the west coast. Known for fishing within sight of the Sea-Watcher's waters.

A wild field village on the far western shore with a small harbour, kept in Ròdaich hands when the Tuathaich homeland was fixed to the north. It faces the waters where the Sea-Watcher is said to live, and pirates are still seen off the coast. Its people follow the Yellow Scorpion.

Achadh àrsaidh

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,756

Founded 14 am Màrt 2396 BDE by Ròdaich fishers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the watch for the Sea-Watcher.

An ancient field village on the far western coast, facing the waters of Uilebheist na Mara, the Sea-Watcher. Gorta Baile chrom, the Great Hunger, struck it in the Age of Strangers; it was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance and keeps the Yellow Scorpion. Pirates have been seen offshore and the villagers keep watch on the headland.

Cathair gheal

city · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 9,818

Founded 5 am Màrt 1813 BDE by Ròdaich builders; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for white walls against the pirate coast.

Cathair gheal is a walled city of white stone on the far western coast, built by the Ròdaich and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its walls face the sea, where pirate ships have been seen offshore. It is the market for the Tuathaich villages of Muileann àrsaidh province.

  • 24 an Gearran 6200 BDE — The long-house at Cathair gheal
  • 28 an Cèitean 1829 DE — Cathair gheal on the concession
  • 15 an Gearran 1929 DE — Cathair gheal behind its walls
  • 10 am Màrt 1949 DE — Cathair gheal arms its boats
  • 15 an t-Samhain 2020 DE — The fishermen of Cathair gheal

Cnoc bhàn

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 6,480

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 23 DE by Ròdaich fishers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for harbour facing the pirate waters.

Cnoc bhàn of the north-west is a harbour facing the pirate waters. It was founded by Ròdaich fishers in the long quiet centuries and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its boats avoid the waters where old sailors place the Sea-Watcher.

Cnoc gheal

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,883

Founded 16 an Cèitean 516 DE by Ròdaich shepherds; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for white hill sheepfolds on the line.

A white hill of sheepfolds, Ròdaich until the Severance and Tuathaich since. The Ròdaich Cnoc gheal lies a short walk south-west, over the line. The two villages share a name and a faith and very little else.

Cnoc uaine

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 6,864

Founded 9 an Dàmhair 899 DE by Ròdaich herders; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for green hill grazing.

Cnoc uaine of Muileann àrsaidh is a green hill of the north-west, founded by Ròdaich herders in the long quiet centuries. It was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is a grazing town and keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith.

Muileann leathan

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 3,096

Founded 23 an Lùnastal 1942 DE by Tuathaich millers. Known for Tuathaich grain mill.

Muileann leathan of the north-west was built by Tuathaich settlers soon after the Severance to grind grain for the northern villages, which had lost the Ròdaich mills to the south. It is a small town, and its mill-race was dug by hand by the first households. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith.

Muileann àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,643

Founded 10 an t-Iuchar 555 BDE by Ròdaich millers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the old mill of the north-west.

Muileann àrsaidh, the ancient mill, is the seat of its province in the Tuathaich north-west, founded as a Ròdaich mill town in the Holy Age. It was walled in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The mill still grinds for the surrounding villages.

  • 25 an Gearran 1929 DE — Muileann àrsaidh closes its road

Muileann àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 12,968

Founded 2 an Gearran 621 BDE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the elder of the two ancient mills.

An ancient mill town of the north-west, and seat of Siorrachd Muileann àrsaidh, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. A second Muileann àrsaidh lies close by, and the two are called the elder and the younger. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

Seann Skell

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,400

Founded 10 an Gearran 12,103 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for watch over the pirate waters.

Seann Skell is a Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the far north-west coast, named by the Ròdaich who resettled it; it passed to the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its citadel looks out over the waters where pirate ships are still reported and where old sailors place the Sea-Watcher. It is not the Seann Skell whose name the regiments carry, which lies far to the south-east.

  • 10 an Dùbhlachd 11,131 BDE — The tower at the north-western Seann Skell

Tobar dhearg

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 4,154

Founded 16 an Dùbhlachd 1849 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for red well of the western Tuathaich.

A Ròdaich village around a well of red water, resettled by Tuathaich families after the Severance. Like several villages of this coast it kept the shrine of the Yellow Scorpion that it inherited rather than raising its own. It lives on sheep and on the market at Cathair gheal.

  • 30 am Faoilleach 2016 DE — Tobar dhearg of the hills

Siorrachd Ros bheag

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 2,760

Founded 18 an Lùnastal 393 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the west. Known for western fishing and war-supply landing.

A low harbour on the western coast, sheltered by Ros bheag, which it has always served as a lesser port. Its people follow the Yellow Scorpion, the faith that runs along the west. The fighting of the Long War at Àth leathan was near enough that the harbour carried supplies for the crown's regiments.

Dùn thais

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 8,302

Founded 23 an Gearran 857 BDE by custodians of the western hills. Known for hill citadel of the western coast.

Dùn thais, the damp fort, is a hill stronghold above the western coast, held by custodians of the vein's western road since the Holy Age. Its walls were rebuilt in the Age of Strangers, when the western harbours began shipping ore, and its citadel has never stood empty since. In An Cogadh Fada its garrison marched to the field of Àth leathan, a short road to the north-east.

  • 3 an Dùbhlachd 1966 DE — Dùn thais in the west

Ros bheag

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 23,817

Founded 4 am Faoilleach 1058 BDE by custodians of the western coast. Known for citadel harbour of the western coast.

Ros bheag is the citadel harbour and provincial seat of the western coast, holding Dùn thais and Ros àrsaidh within its province. It was fortified in the Holy Age and has been the western sea's naval station through every age since. Its people keep the Yellow Scorpion faith.

Ros àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 4,072

Founded 16 an t-Ògmhios 1778 BDE by custodians of the western headland. Known for walled harbour on the ancient headland.

Ros àrsaidh is a small walled harbour on an ancient headland of the west, fortified by the Holy Age custodians. It lies within the province of Ros bheag and has always stood in the shadow of that citadel. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith.

  • 21 an t-Sultain 1929 DE — Outposts at Ros àrsaidh

Siorrachd Ros dhomhain

Doire fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 11,507

Founded 18 an Dùbhlachd 1467 DE by woodcutters of the wild oak wood. Known for oaks said to have built the Sundering fleet.

Doire fhiadhaich was a wild oak wood on the capital shore, and tradition holds that timber for the Sundering fleet was felled here. The wood is long gone and the village is now a fishing quarter between Ros dhomhain and the capital's harbours. It has kept its village rank and its own fishing rights.

Ros dhomhain

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 51,589

Founded 27 am Faoilleach 1232 DE by merchant families of the capital shore. Known for the capital country's great merchant port.

Ros dhomhain is the most populous place of the capital country, a merchant port that outgrew every wall it was ever given until no one built another. The first human traders lodged here after the Crossing, and its counting-houses have served every master of the island's trade since. It sits between the capital and the old harbour of Seann Vell, and the three have run together into one shore.

Seann Vell

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 12,072

Founded 29 an Lùnastal 4041 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for old quay stones of the capital shore.

Seann Vell on the capital shore stands on Seann-Dhaoine quay stones, still visible at low water beneath the later harbour. The Ròdaich resettled it in the Holy Age and walled it in the long quiet centuries. It has since been drawn into the sprawl of Ros dhomhain, but keeps its own walls and its own harbour-master.

  • 29 an Dàmhair 1912 DE — Seann Vell's dockers stay out

Siorrachd Ros gharbh

Cnoc gharbh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 4,691

Founded 5 an Giblean 975 DE by quarriers of Ros gharbh. Known for quarries on the rough hill.

Cnoc gharbh is a rough hill of quarries near Seann Bhral, whose walls were built of its stone. It is a town of nearly five thousand, of quarrymen and carters. The standing column at Cnoc ghorm is not of its stone, a fact its masons have checked more than once.

  • 25 an Giblean 1856 DE — The huts of Cnoc gharbh

Ros gharbh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 19,021

Founded 3 am Faoilleach 216 DE by fishers of the rough headland. Known for the gulf's fishing fleet.

Ros gharbh is a harbour town on a rough headland of the gulf and the seat of its province. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and grew with the gulf's fishing fleet. It keeps the capital's faith.

  • 31 an Dàmhair 1858 DE — Fish smuggled from Ros gharbh

Seann Bhral

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 3,945

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 5524 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for walled old harbour of Ros gharbh.

Seann Bhral is a walled harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site, settled by the Ròdaich and named by them for the Old Ones. It lies near Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, the ruined outpost no one can date. It is a port town of four thousand.

Siorrachd Ros gheal

Ros gheal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 26,562

Founded 29 an Dùbhlachd 1990 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the white headland. Known for white headland and the disputed bay.

Ros gheal, Ros leathan and Seann Skell share one bay on the north-central coast, and have quarrelled over its moorings for as long as the rolls run. Ros gheal is the largest of the three and the seat of its province. Its people keep the Hawk's rite of Mòd, and its white headland is the first land the northern fishing boats see coming home.

  • 22 am Màrt 200 DE — The hawk-house at Ros gheal
  • 2 am Màrt 1821 DE — A customs house at Ros gheal
  • 23 an Cèitean 1919 DE — The hawk-faithful of Ros gheal
  • 10 am Màrt 1953 DE — The ore-ships of Ros gheal

Ros leathan

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 12,619

Founded 30 am Faoilleach 1735 DE by Ròdaich fishers of the Hawk bay. Known for rival wharves of the Hawk bay.

Ros leathan is a harbour town on the Hawk bay, sharing it with Ros gheal and Seann Skell. It was founded in the long quiet centuries by fishers who would not pay Ros gheal's mooring dues. It keeps the Hawk's rite.

Siorrachd Seann Bhral

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 8,751

Founded 10 an t-Iuchar 200 DE by millers of the Seann Bhral country. Known for the other Muileann chiar.

A dusky mill town with a citadel in the south-east, not the silver town of the same name further north; the confusion of the two is an old grievance here. It grinds for Àth chiar and the harbour of Seann Bhral. It keeps the old spirits.

Seann Bhral

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 49,681

Founded 30 an Lùnastal 11,919 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the south-east's great walled harbour.

Seann Bhral of the south-east is a Seann-Dhaoine site that the Ròdaich resettled in the Holy Age, and it has grown into the greatest harbour of that coast and the seat of its province. It was walled in the Age of Strangers, when its quays shipped ore from the interior. It keeps the ancestor rite.

  • 26 an Cèitean 1042 DE — The cough at Seann Bhral

Siorrachd Seann Bhrenn

Seann Bhrenn

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 17,305

Founded 12 an Giblean 11,809 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the northern Seann-Dhaoine harbour.

A Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the north coast, called Seann Bhrenn by the Ròdaich, and the seat of the shire of the same name. It is a large village of the old spirits, and its fishers tell that the harbour-stones were laid by people who had no need of the Ròdaich's tides.

  • 16 an Cèitean 11,454 BDE — The slipways of Seann Bhrenn
  • 25 an Dàmhair 2579 BDE — Seann Bhrenn resettled

Àth fhionn

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,819

Founded 8 am Màrt 2761 BDE by the ford-keepers of Seann Bhrenn. Known for the fair ford.

A fair ford in the north below the city of Dùn thais, on the road from the Seann-Dhaoine harbour at Seann Bhrenn. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich and remains a small crossing town.

Siorrachd Seann Chwen

Baile ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 6,672

Founded 5 an t-Ògmhios 1273 DE by farmers of the Seann Chwen country. Known for grain town south of Cill ghlas.

A low town in the middle east, a short way south of Cill ghlas and the ground the Rending tore open. It follows the Dark Unicorn and sends its grain to the harbour at Seann Chwen.

Baile òg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,732

Founded 6 an Dàmhair 1819 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Known for camp-town of the Cill ghlas diggings.

Baile òg, "the young town", was a camp of the diggings east of the capital, raised in the Age of Strangers near Cill ghlas. It emptied when Scàineadh Cill ghlas closed the district for a generation. It was reopened after the Severance, and its people now follow the capital's faith.

Cathair naomh

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 14,058

Founded 1 an Gearran 158 BDE by priests of the capital's faith. Known for the priests' city by the old outpost.

A holy city near the ruins of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, built by the priesthood of the Dark Unicorn in the Holy Age as a seat of learning. The ruins are said to have been older than any Ròdaich memory when the city was founded, and the priests left them as they were. It is unwalled and trades with the harbour of Seann Chwen and with Ceann leathan.

Ceann leathan

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 8,870

Founded 19 an t-Samhain 2889 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the gulf. Known for Còmhrag Ceann leathan, the annual melee.

Ceann leathan, the broad headland, is a walled temple city on the gulf, older than most of the harbours around it. Its temple of the Dark Unicorn is the chief shrine of the gulf towns. Since the early years of the restored kingdom it has held Còmhrag Ceann leathan, the brutal annual melee, which draws fighters and crowds from every province.

Muileann fhionn

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,965

Founded 1 an Cèitean 1365 DE by millers of the Ceann leathan country. Known for grain milled for two harbours.

A fair-stoned walled mill town between Ceann leathan and Cuan dhearg, grinding grain landed at both harbours. Its walls went up in the Age of Strangers. It follows the Dark Unicorn.

Ros bhàn

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 3,591

Founded 24 an Lùnastal 65 DE by the garrison of the gulf mouth. Known for fortified headland at the gulf mouth.

Ros bhàn is a fortified headland at the mouth of the gulf, walled and given a citadel in the long quiet centuries to guard the harbours within. It is a city by rank, though most of its people are soldiers, customs clerks and their families. The white stone of its headland gives it its name.

Ros ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 4,551

Founded 27 am Faoilleach 61 DE by quarrymen of the red headland. Known for red stone for the gulf cities.

Ros ruadh is a small harbour on the gulf, founded by quarrymen who shipped its red stone to the gulf cities. Much of Ceann leathan and Ros bhàn is built of it. It keeps a ferry to the harbours across the water.

Seann Chwen

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 36,527

Founded 19 an Giblean 12,132 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the gulf's chief harbour and fish-market.

The larger Seann Chwen is the chief harbour of the gulf and the seat of the province that bears its name, built on a Seann-Dhaoine site the Ròdaich resettled in the Holy Age. It takes the fish of the gulf and the goods of Cathair mhòr. It has no walls; the fortified headlands of Ros bhàn and Ceann leathan stand to either side of it.

Àth chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,741

Founded 19 an t-Samhain 662 DE by ford-keepers of the Seann Chwen country. Known for bent ford south of Cill ghlas.

A small ford on a bent stream south of Cill ghlas, where the Rending opened. It follows the Dark Unicorn.

Siorrachd Seann Dunn

Baile fhada

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,593

Founded 27 an Dùbhlachd 681 DE by Ròdaich soldiers of the capital's south. Known for long street and citadel south of the capital.

A town of one long street with a citadel at its end, south-east of the capital. It was a garrison town in the Age of Strangers and has kept its citadel manned since. Its people are soldiers' families and carters, and its street is the last stage of the road from the southern coast to Cathair dhearg.

Seann Chwen

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,351

Founded 1 am Faoilleach 11,419 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for citadel on the capital's southern sea road.

The landing stones at Seann Chwen are of the Seann-Dhaoine, and the name was given by the Ròdaich who resettled the site in the Holy Age. It is a small harbour on the south shore, but its citadel guards the capital's southern sea road, and it has been garrisoned more often than its size would suggest. Its people keep the capital's faith of the Dark Unicorn, and its green is one of the two grounds where the travelling circus, An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn, pitches.

  • 9 an Dùbhlachd 8573 BDE — The Seann-Dhaoine keep to the shore
  • 13 an Gearran 1929 DE — The other Seann Chwen

Seann Dunn

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 14,296

Founded 28 am Faoilleach 11,444 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the Seann-Dhaoine harbour-mole.

The Seann-Dhaoine left the harbour-mole and the name Dunn; the Ròdaich called it Seann Dunn and built a citadel over the mole. It is the seat of the shire of the same name and follows the Dark Unicorn. It is a village in form but large in number, with the ford-town of Àth ghorm under its protection.

  • 6 an Gearran 11,293 BDE — The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn

Àth ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,701

Founded 28 an Giblean 1364 DE by ford-keepers of Seann Dunn. Known for the toll-ford of Seann Dunn.

A blue ford with a small citadel on the road inland from Seann Dunn, built to hold the crossing for the harbour. It follows the Dark Unicorn and is a small town of carters and toll-keepers.

Siorrachd Seann Skell

Achadh gheal

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 9,194

Founded 23 an t-Samhain 959 BDE by Ròdaich flax-growers of Seann Skell. Known for flax fields and bleached linen.

The white field is the flax country that feeds the linen-weavers of Seann Skell, and in the drying season the whole plain is laid with bleaching cloth. The village is large and prosperous for its kind, and it follows the Yellow Scorpion as the port does. Its growers' guild has sold to the same Seann Skell houses for longer than either side can prove.

Achadh ghlas

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 4,980

Founded 26 an Lùnastal 1658 BDE by Ròdaich farmers of Seann Skell. Known for grey fields on the Seann Skell road.

A village of grey-green fields on the road north from Seann Skell, whose barley and oats feed the great port. It lies just south of the Tuathaich line, and since the Severance its farmers have ploughed with one eye on the boundary. In the Long War its barns quartered soldiers of the seventh regiment on the way to Àth leathan.

Doire ghorm

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh nan Ròdach · pop. 2,552

Founded 26 an t-Sultain 1755 DE by charcoal-burners of the south-east. Known for charcoal for the south-coast smithies.

Doire ghorm is a grove village of the south-east, founded by charcoal-burners in the long quiet centuries. Its charcoal once fed the smithies of the south coast. It keeps the orthodox Obsidian Rite, like its neighbours.

Doire naomh

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 3,068

Founded 14 an t-Iuchar 1214 BDE by priests of the Yellow Scorpion. Known for graves of the Àth leathan dead.

A holy oak grove in the west near Àth leathan, where the Long War's first battle was fought. It stayed Ròdaich and kept the Yellow Scorpion, and it buried many of the dead of that battle in its grove. The grove is closed to strangers.

Inis àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 11,121

Founded 28 am Faoilleach 2923 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the west. Known for harbour near the field of Àth leathan.

Inis àrsaidh is an island harbour of the west coast, founded in the Holy Age. It was the nearest port to the field of Àth leathan, and in An Cogadh Fada it supplied the state's forces for the first battle. Its fairground is one of the two grounds where the travelling circus, An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn, pitches.

  • 12 an t-Sultain 34 BDE — The trial hull lost off Inis àrsaidh
  • 2 an Gearran 305 DE — The deep hull that would not float true

Muileann chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 10,454

Founded 22 an Cèitean 1187 DE by Ròdaich millers of the Seann Skell country. Known for a Ròdaich mill on the Tuathaich line.

A crooked mill on the edge of the north-west, left in Ròdaich hands when the Tuathaich homeland was fixed around it. It keeps the faith of the Yellow Scorpion like its Tuathaich neighbours, and its millers have ground for both peoples since the Severance, which the chroniclers note without comment. Cnoc ghlas and Àth àrsaidh over the line buy its flour.

Seann Skell

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 22,120

Founded 19 an t-Samhain 11,340 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for walled old harbour of the Hawk bay.

Seann Skell of the Hawk bay is a walled harbour city on a Seann-Dhaoine site, sharing its bay with Ros gheal and Ros leathan. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age and walled in the Age of Sundering. It keeps the Hawk's rite.

Seann Skell

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh nan Ròdach · pop. 57,907

Founded 29 am Faoilleach 7728 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the southern fleet harbour.

Seann Skell is the great southern port, a town of nearly sixty thousand whose harbour lies on a site the Seann-Dhaoine used before the Ròdaich; the name keeps their root. It is the seat of its province and a centre of Creideamh nan Ròdach. The ninth regiment and the second fleet, raised in the Long War, are stationed here. It shares its name with the great western port.

Seann Skell

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 74,120

Founded 6 an Gearran 12,185 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the great western port.

Seann Skell is the great port of the west, a city of seventy-four thousand and the largest place in this part of the island; the harbour is a Seann-Dhaoine site and the name keeps their root. It is walled by its citadel rather than by curtain walls, and the seventh regiment, raised in the Long War, is stationed here. The first battle of that war was fought at Àth leathan, a short march north.

Àth chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 4,227

Founded 21 am Màrt 1232 DE by fishers of the west. Known for bent ford at the river mouth.

Àth chrom, the bent ford, is a harbour town at a river mouth on the west coast. It was founded in the long quiet centuries. Since An Cogadh Fada, troops of the regiment named for Seann Skell have been quartered close by.

Àth fhionn

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh nan Ròdach · pop. 6,754

Founded 13 an t-Samhain 1743 DE by farmers of the south-east. Known for ford town beside the Seann Skell garrisons.

Àth fhionn of Seann Skell is a ford town of the south-east. It was founded in the long quiet centuries. Since An Cogadh Fada it has billeted soldiers of the regiments stationed at Seann Skell nearby. It keeps the orthodox Obsidian Rite.

Àth leathan

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 680

Founded 8 am Màrt 1264 DE by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for the first battlefield of the Long War.

A Ròdaich drovers' village at the wide ford, emptied at the Severance and resettled by Tuathaich families sent north. In the years before the Long War it became a gathering place for the coal-holdouts of the north-west. The Battle of Àth leathan, the first major engagement of An Cogadh Fada, was fought on the meadows just west of the ford, and the town has not recovered its numbers since.
