Àth shean

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an t-Seabhaig · pop. 10,697

Founded 9 an t-Ògmhios 1073 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of the northern ford. Known for old ford on the northern march.

An old ford on the road north out of the Ròdaich country, walled in the Age of Strangers and strengthened again after the Severance, when the Tuathaich country began a short way to the west. It is a town of the Hawk, Creideamh an t-Seabhaig, and its shrine is one of the oldest of that form of the Rite. It trades with Inis bhàn to the south and, warily, with the Tuathaich villages over the line.

Àth uaine

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 10,807

Founded 3 an Giblean 2858 BDE by ford-keepers of Seann Skell. Known for green ford inland of Seann Skell.

Àth uaine of Seann Skell is a ford town inland of the Hawk bay, founded in the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite. It is the market for the three quarrelling harbours of the bay.

Siorrachd Seann Tarr

Baile mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 4,675

Founded 15 an t-Samhain 1214 DE by craftsmen outside the walls of Baile Mòr ruadh. Known for trades outside Baile Mòr ruadh's walls.

Baile mhòr grew outside the walls of Baile Mòr ruadh, a suburb of tanners, dyers and other trades the city would not have within its gates. It has never been walled itself. In the Age of Strangers it was burned once in a quarrel between the city and the administration, and rebuilt in stone.

Baile Mòr ruadh

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 15,158

Founded 25 an t-Sultain 2717 BDE by a custodian house of the eastern shore. Known for red-stone walls of the east.

Baile Mòr ruadh is a walled city of red stone, crowned by a citadel, and the principal city of its province. It was fought over in the Age of Strangers, when the human administration made it a district seat, and its walls show repairs of every age. Travellers on the eastern road break their journey at An Taigh-seinnse Òir just west of the city.

  • 15 an Lùnastal 4273 BDE — Baile Mòr ruadh in the east
  • 18 an Dàmhair 1480 DE — Baile Mòr ruadh's fair
  • 25 an Giblean 1888 DE — Drought-fever at Baile Mòr ruadh

Baile ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 7,717

Founded 25 an t-Samhain 33 DE by herders of Seann Tarr. Known for supplier to Taigh-solais Baile ìseal.

Baile ruadh is a farm town near the eastern coast, founded in the long quiet centuries. Since the lighthouses were built its people have supplied the keepers of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal on the coast beyond. It keeps the ancestor rite.

Ceann chiar

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,169

Founded 10 an Dùbhlachd 807 DE by Ròdaich fishers of the eastern coast. Known for walled harbour against pirates.

Ceann chiar is a walled harbour on the eastern coast, walled against the pirate ships that have been seen in these waters in every age. It keeps a watch-fire on its headland. It is the port of Seann Tarr province.

  • 8 an Giblean 5184 BDE — The sharing holds after the Black Wind
  • 12 an Cèitean 3894 BDE — The Black Wind remembered at Ceann chiar

Doire fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,947

Founded 11 am Màrt 1078 DE by Ròdaich woodwards of Seann Tarr. Known for wild oakwood and boar.

A village in a wild oakwood between Baile Mòr ruadh and the east coast. It lives on timber and on the boar hunts that the city's families come out for. It keeps the folk tradition of the ancestors.

Seann Tarr

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 23,042

Founded 25 an Giblean 12,197 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the old eastern harbour and fleet.

A harbour of the Seann-Dhaoine on the eastern coast, named Seann Tarr by the Ròdaich, and the seat of the shire of the same name. It is a large village that follows the old spirits. The eastern pirates made it unsafe in the Age of Strangers, and it has a small fleet of its own.

  • 5 an Giblean 11,618 BDE — The script appears at Seann Tarr
  • 3 an Gearran 1360 DE — The grey storm at Seann Tarr

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,748

Founded 6 an Gearran 770 DE by harbour-folk of Seann Tarr. Known for fishing the eastern narrows.

A narrow harbour ford in the far east, close to the old Seann-Dhaoine harbour of Seann Tarr. It keeps the old spirits and sends its fishing to the market at Cnoc uaine.

Siorrachd Seann Toll

Cathair naomh

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 12,935

Founded 22 an Dùbhlachd 4439 BDE by unknown builders, later the Ròdaich spirit-keepers. Known for the unwalled ring of the ancestors.

The holy city of the north grew around a ring of stones older than the Ròdaich, and the chroniclers do not claim to know who raised them. The Ròdaich made it a place of the old spirits in the Holy Age and it has never had walls, since the ancestors' ground was held to need none. It is a city of pilgrims and hostels, and the shrine-keepers of Cnoc chiar and Inis bheag answer to its elders.

  • 20 am Faoilleach 2575 BDE — The ancestor-cairn at Cathair naomh
  • 19 an Lùnastal 1782 DE — Cathair naomh sends its wool
  • 5 an Giblean 1995 DE — Cathair naomh sends its rolls

Cnoc chiar

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,941

Founded 12 an Giblean 2403 BDE by shrine-keepers of Cathair naomh. Known for way-shrines on the pilgrim road.

A dusky hill beside the harbour of Seann Toll, settled by keepers of the old spirits who tended waymarks on the pilgrim road to Cathair naomh. It remains a small town of hostels and way-shrines, busy in the feast seasons and empty between them.

Inis bheag

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,760

Founded 4 an Dàmhair 755 BDE by the island-keepers of Seann Toll. Known for the pilgrims' ferry to Cathair naomh.

A small walled island harbour on the north coast, near the holy city of Cathair naomh. It ferries pilgrims from the sea to the holy city and keeps the old spirits.

Seann Toll

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 19,261

Founded 8 an t-Samhain 12,608 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for sea-caves and the north-coast herring.

Seann Toll, old hollow, is named for the sea-caves under its headland, where Seann-Dhaoine marks are said to be cut into the rock. The Ròdaich resettled it in the Holy Age and it has been a fishing port ever since. It keeps the ancestor rite and the northern herring fleet.

Siorrachd Seann Vell

Cnoc chaol

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 5,467

Founded 23 am Faoilleach 128 DE by Ròdaich shore farmers of Seann Vell. Known for the town the Great Wave named.

Cnoc chaol is the town the Great Wave is named after. Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol struck the southern coast without warning in a single night, devastating it together with Cuan dhearg and Achadh mhin. The town was rebuilt higher up the narrow hill, and its people still leave the lowest street empty.

Cuan chrom

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 4,133

Founded 10 am Faoilleach 1192 DE by Ròdaich innkeepers of Seann Vell. Known for An Taigh-seinnse Mòr and steamed carp.

Cuan chrom is a harbour town on a bent inlet, and An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, one of the great houses of the old tavern circuit, stands at its quay. The tavern was a waypoint on the mining roads and doubled as a militia halt in the years before the war. It is known across the island for its steamed carp and green brandy.

Cuan dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 14,659

Founded 31 am Faoilleach 1615 BDE by fishing clans of the southern shore. Known for rebuilt after the Great Wave.

A red-cliffed harbour on the southern coast that was a fishing town for three ages. The Great Wave, Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol, struck it in a single night in the first years of the new kingdom and destroyed the lower town with its fleet, and the harbour was rebuilt higher up the cliff. Its people keep the old spirits of the Ròdaich, and every house facing the sea keeps a lamp in the upper window.

Inis mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 3,975

Founded 12 an t-Sultain 691 DE by boatmen of Seann Vell. Known for barracks of the First Regiment.

An island harbour settled in the long quiet centuries by boatmen from the Seann Vell shore, Inis mhòr was walled once the capital's eastern approaches became worth defending. A' chiad rèisimeid, raised in the campaign of An Cogadh Fada, is stationed here and bears the town's name. Its barracks now outsize the old fishing quarter, and it lies within sight of the temple harbour of Cuan uaine.

Seann Vell

city · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 6,543

Founded 4 an t-Ògmhios 12,891 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for south-eastern citadel harbour.

Seann Vell of the south-east is a citadel harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. Its citadel guards the south-eastern coast and the approach to Seann Bhral, its larger neighbour and old rival. It keeps the ancestor rite.

  • 20 an Gearran 119 BDE — Seann Vell's harbour
  • 17 an t-Ògmhios 205 DE — Flood at Seann Vell

Seann Vell

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 3,382

Founded 16 an Dàmhair 11,907 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for old harbour of the west coast.

Seann Vell of the west coast is a small harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site, the seat of its province. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age and took up the Yellow Scorpion faith with the rest of the coast. An ceathramh cabhlach is stationed at Cuan shean, a short way up the coast.

  • 20 an Giblean 10,481 BDE — The western Seann Vell
  • 4 an t-Samhain 150 BDE — Seann Vell swears on the sting

Seann Vell

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 26,204

Founded 1 an t-Ògmhios 9251 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for walled harbour on the Cuan chrom road.

Seann Vell of the capital's east is a walled harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site and the seat of its province. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. An Taigh-seinnse Mòr stands just east of it, at the quay of Cuan chrom.

  • 7 an t-Ògmhios 1839 DE — The flux reaches Seann Vell

Siorrachd Seann Warr

Seann Warr

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh · pop. 19,842

Founded 27 am Màrt 12,352 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the Fifth Regiment's walled harbour.

Seann Warr is a Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the capital's western shore, resettled by the Ròdaich and walled in the Holy Age. Its citadel guards the western approaches to the capital. An còigeamh rèisimeid, raised in An Cogadh Fada, is stationed here and carries its name.

Siorrachd Tobar dhearg

Baile gharbh

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh nan Ròdach · pop. 5,279

Founded 1 an t-Ògmhios 661 DE by the carters of Seann Vell. Known for an orthodox Rite town on the coast road.

A rough town on the south coast road between Seann Vell and the lighthouse village of Tobar dhearg. It is one of the few towns where Creideamh nan Ròdach holds the majority, its orthodox priests having come from the pilgrim harbour at Caol naomh. It trades with Muileann naomh and the great port of Seann Skell.

Tobar dhearg

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh nan Ròdach · pop. 23,039

Founded 31 an Cèitean 110 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers of the southern coast. Known for the southern lighthouse and red well.

Tobar dhearg is a large village around a well of red water, the seat of its province. Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, one of the five lighthouses of the Age of Strangers, stands on the shore below it; it burned obsidian-lit flame for over a century before it was converted to dubhan. The village holds to Creideamh nan Ròdach and its priests keep the light's log.

  • 12 an Dàmhair 4651 BDE — Tobar dhearg on the southern cape
  • 28 am Màrt 407 DE — Fire at Tobar dhearg
  • 29 am Màrt 1795 DE — The first keeper of Tobar dhearg

Siorrachd Tobar fhiadhaich

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 965

Founded 21 an Giblean 526 DE by Ròdaich peat-cutters of the northern uplands. Known for rough upland fields and peat.

A hamlet-sized village of rough upland fields and peat banks above Tobar fhiadhaich. Its peat warmed the northern towns when the Small-Burning Law still held and the ore was not burned freely. Fewer than a thousand people live there now.

Baile mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,585

Founded 17 an t-Iuchar 2873 BDE by herders of the northern moor. Known for moorland wool and an ill-fitting name.

The name promises a great town and the place has never been one; the chroniclers suppose it was large only beside the shielings around it when it was named. It is a quiet market for wool from the moor, dependent on Cnoc dhubh for its road and on Tobar fhiadhaich for its law. Its folk follow Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and keep a small reading-house where the school's questions are argued on winter nights.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 6,435

Founded 22 an t-Sultain 1478 DE by the peat-cutters of the northern moor. Known for peat cut from the black hill.

A black hill of peat in the north, cut for fuel since the Small-Burning Law left the ore to the custodians and ordinary hearths to turf. It is the road-town for Baile mhòr and Àth shean and follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. The peat-banks are now nearly as worked out as the vein.

Cnoc ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 7,911

Founded 3 an Cèitean 403 BDE by hill shepherds of the northern coast. Known for grey slate and northern sheepwalks.

Cnoc ghlas is a hill town of the northern coast, a sheepwalk settlement of the Holy Age that later opened quarries in the grey slate of its hill. Its slate roofs much of the province of Tobar fhiadhaich. Its people follow Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, and the town sent more than its share of students to the school's revival.

Muileann chrom

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 4,206

Founded 27 an Gearran 432 DE by millers of Tobar fhiadhaich. Known for north-coast mill of Tobar fhiadhaich.

A mill town on the north coast, grinding for Tobar fhiadhaich and the upland farms behind it. It is one of several places named Muileann chrom and is not the great mill town of the central country. It is a quiet town of millers and inshore fishers.

Tobar fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 16,436

Founded 10 an t-Samhain 2045 BDE by Ròdaich herders of the northern moor. Known for wild spring and moorland grazing.

Tobar fhiadhaich is a large village around a wild spring on the moor, and the seat of its province. It lives on grazing and on the peat of Achadh gharbh. Its herders have walked the same moor paths since the Holy Age, and its spring is said never to have failed, even in the driest years.

  • 10 am Màrt 5712 BDE — Wolves at Tobar fhiadhaich
  • 18 an Giblean 1920 DE — The fever at Tobar fhiadhaich

Tobar ìseal

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,690

Founded 26 an Dùbhlachd 505 BDE by the well-keepers of Muileann shean. Known for the guarded low well.

A low well in a hollow below Muileann shean, ringed with stone in the Holy Age and watched ever since. The small keep that gives it a citadel was built to guard the water for the mill town in dry years, and the dry summers since have proved the builders right. It remains a village, owned in all but name by the millers upstream.

Siorrachd Tobar ghorm

Baile gheal

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 7,515

Founded 2 an t-Ògmhios 1062 DE by the lime-burners of Tobar ghorm. Known for lime-kilns and whitewashed walls.

A white town named for the lime-kilns that whitened it, walled in the Age of Strangers after raids on the road to the harbour at Inis naomh. It is paired with Cnoc mhòr on the hill above, and the two share a market and a quarrel over which is older. Its people follow Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Inis naomh

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 4,681

Founded 9 am Faoilleach 478 BDE by keepers of the holy isle. Known for holy isle and its walled landing.

Inis naomh is a walled harbour on a holy isle of the north coast, founded in the Holy Age. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Its walls were built to keep the isle's shrine safe from raiders.

Muileann mhin

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 4,313

Founded 8 an t-Iuchar 617 DE by millers of Tobar ghorm. Known for fine flour for Tobar ghorm.

Muileann mhin grinds the fine flour of Tobar ghorm, a short way east, and has risen and fallen with the larger village's harvests in every age. Its wheels are the oldest still turning in the province, and the miller families keep a roll of their masters going back to the Age of Sundering. In fair season the carts from the wool fairs come back loaded with its flour.

Tobar ghorm

village · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 25,305

Founded 31 am Faoilleach 2049 BDE by Ròdaich herders of the northern plain. Known for blue spring and wool fairs.

Tobar ghorm is a large village around a blue spring, the seat of its province, and home to the greatest wool fairs of the north. The fairs were old before the humans came, and the humans' wool-buyers made them larger. The mills of Muileann mhin grind its grain.

  • 24 an Lùnastal 1911 DE — A barracks at Tobar ghorm

Àth shean

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 5,697

Founded 15 an t-Iuchar 1340 BDE by the ford-lords of Tobar ghorm. Known for the old walled ford.

An old walled ford with a citadel in the north, holding the road between Tobar ghorm and Cnoc dhubh. Its keep was fought for in the war before the Severance. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Siorrachd Àth bheag

Baile ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 1,763

Founded 14 an t-Samhain 158 DE by fishers of the far east coast. Known for Taigh-solais Baile ìseal and the pirate watch.

A small low town on the far east coast, beside Taigh-solais Baile ìseal, one of the five lighthouses completed in the Age of Strangers. Pirates are still seen off this coast, and the lighthouse-keepers double as the town's watch. It keeps the old spirits.

  • 9 an Cèitean 1807 DE — The keepers of Baile ìseal

Àth bheag

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 20,251

Founded 30 am Faoilleach 118 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the east coast. Known for east-coast ford under pirate watch.

Àth bheag is a town of twenty thousand on the east coast, the seat of its province. Pirate ships have been seen offshore, and the town keeps watchers on the dunes. The lighthouse of Baile ìseal lies a short way south.

Siorrachd Àth chiar

Seann Mhorn

village · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 2,960

Founded 31 an Cèitean 10,901 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for small old harbour.

Seann Mhorn is a small old harbour, one of several Seann names on this stretch of the southern coast, and was settled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. It lies between Seann Skell and Seann Vell. It is a fishing village of three thousand.

  • 4 an Cèitean 10,887 BDE — The shell beds of the southern Seann Mhorn

Seann Warr

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 3,337

Founded 15 an Gearran 10,679 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for old landing on the gulf's south shore.

Seann Warr of Àth chiar is a small harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine landing on the south shore of the gulf. The Ròdaich resettled it in the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite and a few boats, and pays its dues to the larger harbours across the water.

Àth chiar

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 18,876

Founded 18 an Giblean 126 DE by the drovers of the south-east. Known for the rebels' keep and southern cattle-market.

A dusky ford in the south-east with a citadel, the seat of Siorrachd Àth chiar and a large market town. Its keep was held by Ròdaich rebels in the war before the Severance and is still garrisoned. It keeps the old spirits and trades with the coast at Seann Mhorn and Muileann chiar to the south.

Siorrachd Àth dhomhain

Baile ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 5,197

Founded 7 am Màrt 1718 DE by slate-quarriers of Àth dhomhain. Known for blue slate quarries.

Baile ghorm is a quarry town whose blue slate roofs half the northern plain. It sends slate to Inis mhòr and takes grain in return. It shares its name with a dyers' town far to the east, and the two are told apart in the record by their provinces.

Cnoc mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 3,757

Founded 11 an Dùbhlachd 624 BDE by hill-farmers of the Àth dhomhain country. Known for hill farms and a quarrel with Baile gheal.

The great hill above Baile gheal, farmed since the Holy Age and never walled, since Baile gheal's walls stand close below. The two towns share a market and a long quarrel over which is the elder. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh.

Àth dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 17,119

Founded 19 an Lùnastal 1572 DE by Raghnall Àthach and his kin. Known for the horseman's ford and shire citadel.

The deep ford here could only be crossed on horseback, and a family of ferrymen became a family of lords by owning the one safe path over it. The citadel on the near bank was fought for in the troubles before the Severance and has been the seat of Siorrachd Àth dhomhain since. The town is large and orderly, a house of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh stands by the gate, and Cnoc mhòr and Baile gheal send it their grain.

  • 27 am Màrt 1922 DE — The northern pits at Àth dhomhain

Siorrachd Àth fhiadhaich

Àth fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 19,293

Founded 21 an t-Samhain 2771 BDE by ford-wardens of the eastern road. Known for river-mouth harbour of the eastern road.

Àth fhiadhaich stands at the ford where the eastern road meets the sea at a wild river mouth, and it has been a harbour since the Holy Age. It grew great on the traffic of the vein country in the Age of Strangers, and the famous tavern An Sligeanach Fad' às stands at Ceann bhàn, a short way down the road. The town keeps the oldest folk rite, and its fishing fleet still blesses its nets at the ford.

Siorrachd Àth fhionn

Àth fhionn

town · Ròdaich · Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach · pop. 15,519

Founded 26 an Giblean 2099 BDE by drovers of the southern roads. Known for fording place of the southern drove road.

Àth fhionn, the fair ford, is a large inland town at the crossing of the southern drove road. It has been a resting place for herds and drovers since the Holy Age. Its people keep the ancestor rite and hold the drove-road fair at the ford.

  • 16 an t-Iuchar 10,286 BDE — The kerbed way between the forts
  • 6 an Dùbhlachd 1878 DE — Àth fhionn signs

Siorrachd Àth ghlas

Doire bhàn

village · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,837

Founded 7 an t-Sultain 1248 DE by Ròdaich woodwards of Àth ghlas. Known for white-barked copse by Àth ghlas.

A small village in a copse of white-barked trees across the river from Àth ghlas, cutting firewood and poles for the town. It keeps clear of the ruin of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire to the east, as its elder neighbour does. It follows the capital's faith.

Àth ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 17,813

Founded 12 an t-Iuchar 2850 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the central country. Known for grey ford below the ruined outpost.

The grey ford is the seat of its province, a large town beside Cathair mhòr and a short way from the ruin of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire. The ruin predates every known pattern of settlement on the island, and the town has kept its people out of it by custom. It lives on trade between Cathair mhòr and the eastern towns.

  • 20 an Cèitean 1325 BDE — The toll-house at Àth ghlas

Siorrachd Àth mhòr

Baile bheag

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 1,961

Founded 20 an Dùbhlachd 141 DE by carters across the ford from Àth mhòr. Known for carters across the ford.

A small town across the ford from Àth mhòr, grown up to serve the traffic that the walled town would not let in after dark. It is a town of stables, carters and cheap lodging. It has always been a dependent of Àth mhòr and has never been allowed a market of its own.

Àth mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Feallsanachd an Fhèidh · pop. 12,234

Founded 1 an t-Ògmhios 1452 BDE by a custodian house of the northern ford. Known for walled great ford of the north.

Àth mhòr is the walled great ford of the north and the seat of its province, a town of twelve thousand. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the northern road carried ore to the coast and the ford was worth holding. Baile bheag lies across the river and handles the traffic after the gates are shut.

  • 13 an Dùbhlachd 5749 BDE — The hawk lintel at Àth mhòr
  • 3 an Gearran 1890 DE — The petition of Àth mhòr

Siorrachd Àth shean

Baile uaine

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 1,857

Founded 5 an Gearran 1093 DE by market gardeners of Àth shean. Known for market gardens for the capital.

Baile uaine is a small town of market gardens, sending green stuff to Dùn gheal and on to the capital each market day. It has never been walled or fought over. Its people follow the capital's faith and pay their dues at Dùn gheal.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 10,778

Founded 24 an Cèitean 85 DE by farmers from Àth shean. Known for lodgings for the Fèill Muileann òg.

A young hill town close to Muileann òg, whose fair is the largest gathering on the island. It lodges traders and their beasts during the fair and is quiet the rest of the year. It follows the Dark Unicorn.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,925

Founded 17 an t-Sultain 1822 DE by suppliers to the garrison at Inis mhòr. Known for supplies for the first regiment.

Cnoc òg grew up in the Age of Strangers to supply the garrison at Inis mhòr, where the first regiment is now stationed. It is a town of bakers and harness-makers. It follows the capital's faith.

Dùn gheal

city · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 2,211

Founded 26 an Dùbhlachd 1065 BDE by a custodian house of the southern approach. Known for white-limed hill fort.

The white fort is ranked a city though it holds only a few thousand people, a hill fort limed white so that it could be seen from the capital. It watched the southern road in the Holy Age and has done so since. It now serves as a market for Baile uaine and the farms of Àth shean.

Seann Chwen

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 10,732

Founded 29 an Lùnastal 9436 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for south-coast old harbour.

Seann Chwen of Àth shean is a harbour on the south coast, on a Seann-Dhaoine site. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age and is the port for the southern Àth shean. It keeps the capital's faith.

  • 5 an Cèitean 7091 BDE — The half-cut stone of Seann Chwen

Àth chiar

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 9,862

Founded 21 an Dùbhlachd 1323 DE by ford-keepers of the east road. Known for dusky ford near Muileann ghlas field.

Àth chiar is a ford town east of the capital, founded in the long quiet centuries. The field of Muileann ghlas lies to its south-west, and the town was a supply post in the last battle of An Cogadh Fada. It keeps the capital's faith.

  • 25 an Lùnastal 1928 DE — The fight at the ford of Àth chiar

Àth shean

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 23,705

Founded 9 an t-Iuchar 1019 BDE by ford-wardens of the capital road. Known for old ford of the eastern road.

The northern of the two Àth shean holds the old ford where the road east from the capital crosses its river. It was walled in the Holy Age to guard that crossing and has grown into a large town. An Taigh-seinnse Mòr stands a short way up the road toward Seann Vell.

  • 14 an t-Samhain 5223 BDE — A household turned out at Àth shean
  • 22 an Gearran 515 DE — The ford at Àth shean

Àth shean

town · Ròdaich · Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh · pop. 37,915

Founded 15 an Dàmhair 1036 BDE by ford-wardens of the south. Known for the great southern ford market.

The southern Àth shean is the larger of the two, a great ford town near the south coast. It has been a market since the Holy Age and has never needed walls. Its harbour is the old site of Seann Chwen, a short way east.

  • 21 am Màrt 2 BDE — Àth shean shuts its granaries
  • 19 an t-Ògmhios 660 DE — The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt
  • 24 an t-Sultain 1460 DE — The firlot of Àth shean

Siorrachd Àth àrsaidh

Baile gheal

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 8,925

Founded 27 an Giblean 2284 BDE by Ròdaich salt-boilers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the doubled shrine of the Scorpion.

A white-washed Ròdaich village of the Holy Age, it was one of the settlements emptied and handed to the Tuathaich after the Severance. The newcomers made it a town and a market, trading with the harbour at Caol naomh a short distance away. Its shrine of the Yellow Scorpion stands in the shell of the older Ròdaich one, and the two sets of carvings can still be told apart.

Baile ghlas

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 12,477

Founded 13 an t-Samhain 279 DE by Ròdaich green-dyers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for green dyes and Tuathaich folk rites.

A green-grey town of dyers, emptied at the Severance and resettled by the Tuathaich. It keeps Creideamh nan Tuathach and is a market for Baile Mòr ruadh and Cnoc ghlas.

Baile Mòr ruadh

city · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 9,642

Founded 3 an Gearran 747 BDE by Ròdaich lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the red city of the Tuathaich.

A red walled city in the north-west, held by Ròdaich lords from the Holy Age to the Severance, and since then one of the principal Tuathaich cities. It follows the Yellow Scorpion and governs the Àth àrsaidh country with its fords and towns.

  • 2 an t-Samhain 1929 DE — Baile Mòr ruadh receives the columns

Cnoc ghlas

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh nan Tuathach · pop. 2,120

Founded 13 an Cèitean 1801 DE by human settlers from an Tìr Thall. Known for strangers' settlement on the grey hill.

Cnoc ghlas of Àth àrsaidh was settled by humans in the Age of Strangers and became a Tuathaich town after the Severance. It keeps the Tuathaich folk tradition, and its singers are among the keepers of the First Canoe fragment.

Cnoc ghlas

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 1,740

Founded 12 an Dùbhlachd 1236 DE by Ròdaich herders, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for trade across the line at Muileann chrom.

A small green-grey hill town of the north-west, emptied and resettled at the Severance. It follows the Yellow Scorpion and trades with the Ròdaich mill at Muileann chrom over the line.

Doire mhòr

village · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 13,974

Founded 24 an t-Sultain 1683 BDE by Ròdaich woodwards; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for great oakwood and charcoal.

A great oakwood village, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance and now one of the largest places they hold, with fourteen thousand people. It lives on timber and charcoal, and its charcoal fed the northern smithies when the ore was no longer theirs to burn. It follows the Yellow Scorpion.

Àth gheal

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 12,996

Founded 29 an t-Sultain 643 DE by Ròdaich ferrymen; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for a walled town of the coal-holdouts.

Àth gheal was a Ròdaich ford-and-harbour town of the long quiet centuries, walled in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. When the dubhan economy came it was among the northern towns that went on working the last coal seams. It was one of the holdouts broken in An Cogadh Fada, and its people still speak bitterly of that year.

Àth àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe · pop. 16,434

Founded 12 an t-Samhain 743 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the ancient ford of the Tuathaich.

An ancient ford in the north-west, the seat of Siorrachd Àth àrsaidh, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is a large town of the Yellow Scorpion and the market of the Tuathaich southern country.
